LG Chem's EP2730933A1 offers a way to see it: with the balancing circuit commanded off, the voltage across the diagnosis resistor should match the idle pattern; if it looks like the active pattern, current is still flowing. Group E then loses charge around the clock and drifts below the others, which in time can block charging or limit power because the lowest cell sets the lower limit. A shorted transistor is the classic cause. Ford's hybrid BECM sets P0DBD as well; the 2017 OBD summary describes a 100 ms start-up test with open contactors in which any cell of circuit E deviating more than 75 mV from the mean marks the circuit. The circuit fault is P0DBC, the inactive case P0DBE.

title: DTC P0DC1 - Hybrid/EV Battery Cell Balancing Circuit F Stuck On
problem_description: P0DC1 says that the bleed path of cell group F appears to stay engaged. Ford lists it for the BECM of its full and plug-in hybrids in the OBD system summaries of model years 2014 to 2019. The battery there is split into fourteen balancing circuits, A to N, each looking after six cells. title: DTC P0DC2 - Hybrid/EV Battery Cell Balancing Circuit F Stuck Off

An Intersil (now Renesas) application note estimates that lithium cells 150 mV apart at full charge can lose up to a quarter of usable pack capacity. CARB's section 1968.2 counts the missing response as a malfunction. The always-on opposite is P0DC1.

title: DTC P0DFB - Generator Position Exceeding Learn Limit
problem_description: The position sensor of a hybrid generator, normally a resolver, is never mounted exactly in line with the magnetic poles of the rotor. The remaining angle error is determined once and saved in the controller; Hyundai describes doing this after assembly and again whenever the machine or its control unit is replaced, and Ford describes an in-vehicle routine started by a scan tool that sweeps the current angle and reads the offset where the q-axis current crosses zero. P0DFB means such a learned offset lies outside the window the software accepts, so it cannot be used for field-oriented control. No manufacturer documents P0DFB publicly. Possible reasons are a resolver that moved on its shaft, an aborted learning run or a faulty controller. A missing value is P0DFC instead.

title: DTC P0DFF - Battery Charger Coolant Control Valve Control Circuit High
problem_description: P0DFF is the short-to-voltage case for the valve that cools the on-board charger. The controller sees the drive line high while commanding it low. title: DTC P0E04 - Generator Phase V Current Sensor Circuit
problem_description: P0E04 is the general circuit code for the generator inverter's V-phase current sensor, meant for an electrical fault that is not narrowed down to offset, low or high. What B means differs between makers: on the 2011 Chevrolet Volt, GM's own codes for valve B (P1EC7, P1EC8) actually watch the second drive line of the same valve motor that serves as valve A, whereas other layouts have a physically separate second valve for a chiller or radiator branch. For diagnosis it is therefore worth checking first which actuator the maker calls B. The protection itself works like that of TI's integrated high-side switches for cars, which cut off at their current limit or near 150 °C and report it. CARB obliges makers to monitor these outputs electrically. Electrical circuit faults of valve B are P0D1A, P0D1D and P0D1E.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Coolant routing does not change as commanded
Battery temperature drifts, power or charging limited
possible_causes: Valve B binding so its actuator stalls against the stop (likelihood: high)
Short or low resistance in the valve B actuator or harness (likelihood: medium)
Degraded driver stage in the control module (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P0E21 (Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Control Valve B Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: hv battery pack coolant valve b, bms.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-3 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Valve B binding so its actuator stalls against the stop (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Short or low resistance in the valve B actuator or harness (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.
source: OBDex / SAE J2012 & ISO 15031-6 Open Diagnostic Standard

title: DTC P0E22 - Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Control Valve C Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
problem_description: P0E22 tells that the driver for a third coolant control valve, C, has protected itself against excessive current or heat. No manufacturer documents P0E22 publicly, and none of the reviewed GM, Ford, Stellantis or Mercedes documents uses a valve C at all. Three valves suggest a loop with several branches, for example radiator, air-conditioning chiller and heater, with C switching one of them. Unlike a plain ground short (P0DEB), the overload code catches a load that still conducts but draws too much, so a stiff valve or a shorted turn in its motor is the likely trigger rather than a broken wire. CARB requires that every electronic output of battery thermal management be checked for circuit faults; TI's automotive smart switches show the mechanism: they disconnect once current reaches the limit or the junction nears 150 °C.

One branch of the coolant loop no longer switches
Battery overcooled in winter or kept too warm in summer

Shorted turn in the valve C actuator motor (likelihood: medium)
Degraded driver stage in the control module (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P0E23 - Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor G Circuit
problem_description: P0E23 is the catch-all circuit code of drive motor inverter temperature sensor G, a thermistor that watches the power switches of the motor inverter. It stands for an electrical fault the controller cannot pin down as low, high or erratic. No manufacturer documents P0E23 publicly. The only published user of the G series is Mitsubishi: in the 2023 Outlander PHEV the seventh IGBT sensor of the front motor unit (U-phase H2) reports its faults as P0E24, P0E25 and P0E26, but not as P0E23. CARB requires hybrid input components to be tested for open circuits and out-of-range signals. Without a valid temperature the inverter is usually run with reduced torque; the sensor sits inside the inverter, so repair often means that assembly.

Reduced electric drive power
possible_causes: Temperature sensor or sensing board inside the inverter failed (likelihood: high)
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector (likelihood: medium)
Faulty evaluation input in the motor control unit (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P0E24 - Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor G Circuit Range/Performance
problem_description: P0E24 is the plausibility test of inverter temperature sensor G: the signal is electrically fine, but the temperature it reports does not fit. Mitsubishi uses the code on the 2023 Outlander PHEV for IGBT sensor number 7 in the front motor control unit, labelled U-phase H2. The check runs only after a soak of at least 600 s, with the IGBTs shut down and the unit fed with 8 V or more, within 1.5 s of these conditions being met. Should it then deviate from either of two other IGBT temperatures by more than 47 °C for 0.1 s, P0E24-00 is logged; MIL and plug-in hybrid warning light both light up. After a long stand all switches should be equally warm, so the code points to a drifting sensor. Mitsubishi's flow ends with a new power drive unit.

Often no noticeable change in driving

Uneven inverter cooling, e.g. air in the coolant circuit (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P0E25 - Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor G Circuit Low
problem_description: P0E25 means the voltage of inverter temperature sensor G has fallen below its valid window. In the 2023 Outlander PHEV, Mitsubishi assigns it to the U-phase H2 sensor of the front motor control unit and sets P0E25-00 once that signal does not rise above 1.25 V during 0.08 s with a unit supply of 8 V upward; the MIL is switched on together with the hybrid warning lamp. Mitsubishi states only the voltage. For an NTC element fed through a pull-up resistor, as GM describes for its inverter sensors, a low voltage equals a very hot sensor, so a ground short or a damaged sensing line looks like an overheated switch. Real overheating is reported by separate temperature codes. The opposite limit is P0E26; the sensor is not sold separately.

Motor power limited as if the inverter were overheating

Damaged sensing board, e.g. after coolant ingress (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P0E26 - Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor G Circuit High
problem_description: P0E26 is logged when the signal of inverter temperature sensor G climbs above its permitted range. In the 2023 Outlander PHEV it belongs to the front motor unit's U-phase H2 sensor: at least 3.75 V lasting 0.08 s, with at least 8 V supply to the unit, sets P0E26-00 together with MIL and hybrid warning light. With an NTC element and pull-up resistor, the layout GM documents for its inverter thermistors, such a voltage would mean an extremely cold power switch, which a working inverter never shows; the usual reasons are an open sensing line, a lost reference ground or a broken thermistor. The low-side fault is P0E25. Because the sensor is built into the unit, Mitsubishi replaces the power drive unit.

title: DTC P0E27 - Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor G Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
problem_description: P0E27 marks short dropouts or jumps in the signal of inverter temperature sensor G. Between the events the reading is normal again, which is what separates it from the steady faults P0E25 and P0E26. No manufacturer documents P0E27 publicly; Mitsubishi, the one documented user of sensor G on the 2023 Outlander PHEV, checks that sensor for plausibility and for both voltage limits only. CARB expects hybrid sensor circuits to be monitored for circuit faults, which covers unstable signals as well. Likely sources are a connector with poor contact, a cracked solder joint on the sensing board or a thermistor with unstable resistance. The code can vanish before the workshop sees it, and the drive may be limited while it is active.

title: DTC P0E2A - Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor H Circuit Low

title: DTC P0E2C - Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor H Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
problem_description: P0E2C covers an unsteady signal from inverter temperature sensor H: it flickers, jumps or drops out for moments and then recovers. title: DTC P0E2D - Internal Control Module Hybrid/EV Battery Monitor Performance
problem_description: P0E2D is an internal self-test result of the module that supervises the high-voltage pack: the part that measures cell voltages, usually a dedicated monitor chip with its own converter and reference, does not behave as expected. It casts doubt on the measurement itself, not on a cell. Battery monitor patents such as Renesas US9735567B2 show the kind of checks involved, for example self-diagnosis of the A/D converter, detection of a broken sense line between cell and chip, or a second, simpler fault monitor. No manufacturer document on an official server explains P0E2D. CARB requires computers and hybrid components feeding the drive to be monitored. Without trusted cell voltages the pack cannot be shielded from over- or undercharge, so power is limited or the car will not get ready.

title: DTC P0E2E - Battery Charger A Fuse
problem_description: P0E2E concerns the high-voltage fuse that protects the branch from the battery to on-board charger A. Audi documents P0E2E00 for the 2022 Q5 plug-in hybrid: the hybrid battery regulation module J840 stores it intermittently with symptom code 28733, often next to P0A95, and the driver sees an electrical system fault message or the car does not start. According to Audi, a diagnostic irregularity during very dynamic cornering creates the entry without a real defect; replacing the switching unit, as guided fault finding suggests, does not help, a software update does. A truly open charger fuse stops AC charging. P0A95, P0E2F and P0E30 cover other HV fuses.

title: DTC P0E2F - High Voltage Fuse B

On EQB models a DC/DC wake-up fault can set it without a blown fuse. Porsche lists it as fuse 2 on the 2020-22 Taycan, which is then not ready to drive. Volvo and Polestar compare the voltages after the front and rear fuse outputs with pack voltage. Main fuse: P0A95.

title: DTC P0E30 - High Voltage Fuse C
problem_description: P0E30 is the code for a third fuse in the high-voltage system, after A (P0A95) and B (P0E2F). No manufacturer documents P0E30 publicly. How such a fuse is checked can be seen from the siblings: Volvo and Polestar have the battery control module compare the voltage measured after each fuse output with the pack voltage, and Porsche numbers its Taycan fuses as fuse and fuse 2 under P0A95 and P0E2F. A pack with only two fused branches never sets P0E30. What the third fuse protects, for example a heater, compressor or charger branch, is decided by the maker. If it opens, the consumers on that branch lose power; a blown fuse normally follows a short circuit that has to be found before the fuse or the battery unit is replaced.
symptoms: HV system warning message
Consumers on the affected branch without function
possible_causes: Short circuit in a consumer on the third fused branch (likelihood: high)
Faulty voltage measurement behind the fuse (likelihood: medium)
Software error in the battery control module (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P0E30 (High Voltage Fuse C).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: high voltage fuse, battery energy control module.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 1-8 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Short circuit in a consumer on the third fused branch (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Faulty voltage measurement behind the fuse (likelihood: medium).

title: DTC P0E31 - DC/DC Converter Voltage Sensor A Circuit

GM's 2025 engine tables use the neighbouring codes for the same sensor in a converter that steadies the 12 V supply during engine auto-starts: P0E33 below 1 V, P0E34 above 28 V, P0E32 for implausible values. FCA names sensor A as voltage sensor 1 on the 2021 Ram 1500 eTorque. CARB wants open circuits and out-of-range signals of such inputs reported separately where feasible. With a lost voltage signal the converter tends to stop or run in a fallback mode.

The neighbouring GM codes for the same sensor (25OBDG03A, a converter backing up the 12 V network during engine auto-starts) show the frame: valid readings lie between 1 V and 28 V and are sampled every 12.5 ms. Loose terminals, a cracked solder joint or a ground that only fails under vibration are the usual suspects, so the fault may come and go.

title: DTC P0E3C - Hybrid/EV Battery Coolant Pump Underspeed
problem_description: P0E3C is set when the battery coolant pump stays below the speed it has been asked for. Only if the code returns after two or more purges is the pump itself diagnosed. Overspeed of the same pump is P0E3B.

title: DTC P0E4E - Engine Failed to Crank
problem_description: P0E4E reports that the hybrid system commanded an engine start but the crankshaft did not turn, or did not reach the cranking speed it expected. In most hybrids a motor-generator fed by the high-voltage battery cranks the engine, so causes range from a seized engine or transaxle to missing battery energy or a drive fault. No manufacturer documents P0E4E publicly. GM's bulletin PIC6229C for the 2016-2019 Malibu hybrid shows why charge matters: below a pack voltage of 154 to 210 V, depending on temperature, the system stops trying to crank until a recovery charge is done. CARB requires the energy storage monitor to catch faults that prevent engine starts.

title: DTC P0E5C - DC/DC Converter Temperature Sensor C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
problem_description: P0E5C flags a sensor C signal that changes faster than the part it watches could heat or cool. A converter inductor or heat sink has thermal mass, so a jump of many degrees within a few milliseconds points to a contact problem in the circuit, not to the converter itself. No manufacturer documents P0E5C publicly. The sensor is known from Ford, where sensor C watches the boost converter inductor and is checked only through P0E59 with fixed voltage and temperature limits; an erratic check is not described there. title: DTC P0E6B - Battery Charging System Precharge Contactor Circuit Stuck Closed

CARB requires faults that disable charging to be detected. The opposite fault is P0E6C.

title: DTC P0E72 - Control Pilot Signal Low Frequency
problem_description: P0E72 refers to the pulse train that an AC charging station places onto the pilot wire. Under SAE J1772, matched by IEC 61851-1, this is a rectangular ±12 V signal at 1 kHz, and its duty cycle tells the car how much current it may draw. The vehicle measures the period of this signal; if it is clearly slower than 1 kHz, the reading is distrusted and P0E72 is stored, because a wrong frequency also makes the current limit unreliable. No manufacturer documents P0E72 publicly. A US Department of Energy test report on pilot-line communication (PNNL) treats the 1000 Hz frequency and pulse width as values that added equipment must not disturb. Causes are a faulty station or adapter, interference on the line, or the car's measuring circuit. P0E73 is the high case; voltage faults are P0CF4 to P0CF6.

Charging works normally at other stations
possible_causes: Charging station or portable charger generating an off-spec pilot (likelihood: high)
Faulty charging adapter or extension in the cable path (likelihood: medium)
Pilot measuring circuit in the vehicle charger misreading (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P0E73 - Control Pilot Signal High Frequency

No manufacturer documents P0E73 publicly. Simulation notes from Typhoon HIL describe the station side of this interface, a PWM signal of ±12 V at 1 kHz evaluated by a resistor network in the car. If the fault follows the vehicle across several stations, check the charge port and the charger's input. P0E72 is the low case.

title: DTC P0E88 - Battery Charger B Input Current Too Low

A low value with normal voltage suggests that the charger does not ramp up, that a resistive inlet or cable limits the flow, or that the charging station offers less current than expected. A measurement error is possible too, but those have their own sensor codes (P0E8A). CARB requires charger faults that limit the charging rate to be detected. title: DTC P0EC3 - A/C Refrigerant Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low

problem_description: P0ED2 means hybrid/EV battery F delivers less voltage than the controller predicts from current draw and state of charge. No manufacturer documents P0ED2 publicly. For one unit the limits scale with its number of cells. Typical causes are an aged module with lost capacity, a cell with internal leakage that drained during standstill, or a high-resistance joint that loses voltage under load. Discharge power is cut back. High voltage of unit F is P0ED3, low voltage of unit E is P0ECE.

title: DTC P0ED9 - Generator Phase Y Current High

title: DTC P0EE1 - Hybrid/EV Battery Pack F Deterioration

title: DTC P0EE3 - A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve B Control Circuit/Open

title: DTC P0EE6 - A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve B Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High

title: DTC P0EEF - Drive Motor A Control Module Overtemperature

GM gives an idea of the limits on the 2016 Volt: its motor control processor A sets P0C11, P0C12 or P0C13 when power inverter phase U, V or W stays above 126 °C for 1.2 s within a 2 s window, rated Type A with the MIL after one trip. CARB demands that hybrid systems monitor electric motor performance. Low coolant in the electronics loop, a weak coolant pump, trapped air or long heavy load in hot weather heat the module, which then reduces motor torque to protect itself.

title: DTC P2002 - Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)

title: DTC P2004 - Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 1)

title: DTC P202B - Reductant Tank Heater Control Circuit Low

title: DTC P202D - Reductant Leakage

title: DTC P2039 - Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
problem_description: P2039 is stored when the signal of injection air pressure sensor A sits below the lowest voltage a working sensor can deliver. Deutz documents it on its EMR L1 controller as P2039-00 under SPN 4335 and lumps two causes together: a grounded signal and an open circuit, since the input is pulled low when the signal wire is interrupted. A loss of the 5 V reference is another common reason for a reading near zero. Because the controller can no longer confirm that atomizing air is present, it stops DEF injection; Deutz engines then run without NOx reduction until the inducement logic of the machine steps in. The opposite fault is P2040, and electrical faults of the sensor supply fall under P2037.

title: DTC P2040 - Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
problem_description: With P2040 the injection air pressure sensor A reports a voltage above its upper limit, more than a real air pressure could produce. On Deutz's EMR L1 controller this is P2040-00 under SPN 4335, defined as a short circuit to battery. In practice that means the signal wire touches a powered conductor, the sensor ground is missing so the output floats up to the reference, or the sensor itself has failed high. title: DTC P2048 - Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 1 Unit 1)
problem_description: P2048 means the control line of the Bank 1, unit 1 DEF injector is pulled toward ground, typically a chafed wire touching the chassis or an internal short in the coil. GM's LML calibration treats less than about 0.5 ohm between signal and ground for 2 s as a failure (Type A). Ford's 2023 diesel logic reports the code once injector current exceeds 1.6 A; Deutz's EMR5 list files it under voltage below normal on the metering unit. Nissan reflashed the ECM of the 2016 to 2019 Titan XD with the Cummins 5.0 L V8 because P2048 appeared without a real defect, and Volvo traced it to a harness rubbed through on VNR trucks. While the code is active, dosing is normally blocked; the catalyst no longer reduces NOx and the inducement countdown may begin.
symptoms: MIL on
DEF dosing suspended, warning in the instrument cluster
Inducement or reduced power after a countdown
possible_causes: Control wire chafed against chassis or exhaust bracket (likelihood: high)
Shorted winding inside the DEF injector (likelihood: medium)
ECM software setting the code without a fault (Nissan Titan XD reflash) (likelihood: medium)
DEF residue or water bridging the connector pins (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2048 (Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 1 Unit 1)).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: reductant injection valve.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-3 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Control wire chafed against chassis or exhaust bracket (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Shorted winding inside the DEF injector (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.
source: OBDex / SAE J2012 & ISO 15031-6 Open Diagnostic Standard

title: DTC P2049 - Reductant Injection Valve Circuit High (Bank 1 Unit 1)
problem_description: P2049 is the opposite electrical case for the Bank 1, unit 1 DEF injector: the low-side control line sees battery voltage, for instance through contact with a powered conductor or water inside the connector. On the 2014 Cruze diesel GM rates it Type B (two trips), whereas the LML and the 2018 diesel tables treat it as Type A; the 2018 test needs more than 11 V and counts 30 bad samples out of 60 at 100 ms. Deutz lists it for the EMR5 metering unit as an over-normal voltage or high-side short, and Ford's 2023 summary gives an injector current below 0.1 A as the trigger. GM's DEF bulletin sorts P2049 among non-tamper faults, so it brings up the emission service message rather than the tamper warning. The output stage shuts off to protect itself, which stops dosing.

Internal fault of the DEF injector coil (likelihood: medium)
Defective output stage in the control module (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P204A - Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit
problem_description: P204A is the general electrical fault of the sensor that measures DEF pressure between pump and injector; in most systems it is built into the pump module. The secondary ECU of Deutz's EMR L1 uses it for two states that are neither low nor high: a ground fault (failure type F0) and a sensor supply outside its window (1C), while shorts to ground or battery go to P204C and P204D. Mack trucks to US13 emissions report P204A-13 for an open signal or ground wire; repair instruction GDC18-058 has the harness checked and otherwise lists the complete DEF pump unit as the part to fit. Without a valid pressure value the controller cannot regulate dosing, so it stops the pump and the inducement timer starts. CARB requires such inputs to be monitored for circuit faults.
symptoms: MIL on, DEF system warning
No DEF dosing
Power or speed limitation after the countdown
possible_causes: Open signal or ground wire to the pressure sensor (likelihood: high)
Sensor supply voltage out of range (likelihood: medium)
Pressure sensor inside the DEF pump unit failed (likelihood: medium)

Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: reductant pressure sensor, reductant supply line.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.7-3 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Open signal or ground wire to the pressure sensor (likelihood: high).

title: DTC P204B - Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
problem_description: P204B is a plausibility test: the DEF pressure sensor is electrically fine, but its value disagrees with the system state. GM uses moments when the true pressure is known. The 6.6 L LML sets it if more than 50 kPa appears while the line is empty and unpressurised (Type A, Type B on the 2014 Cruze diesel); GM's 2018 diesel table compares the reading with ambient after the end-of-trip purge, and GM's 2025 DEF controller fails it when the value strays more than 36.4 kPa from ambient before priming. Deutz marks the case on the EMR L1 with failure type 64. Hino released new DCU software in 2016 (SB-16-015) because the unit stored P204B falsely on conventional trucks. A genuine offset mostly means an ageing sensor in the pump module.

Emission service message

Line not emptied at shutdown, e.g. afterrun interrupted or frozen DEF (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P204C - Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
problem_description: P204C means the DEF pressure sensor output has fallen below its valid range, which points to an open signal wire, a short to ground or a missing 5 V supply. On the 6.6 L LML, GM fails anything under 0.41 V lasting 0.4 s, GM's 2018 diesel table a raw value under 5 % of the supply, and the 2025 DEF controller less than 0.45 V in 6 of 100 samples, each Type A. Ford's 2023 diesels set it under 0.2 V. On 2017 to 2019 Super Duty trucks with the 6.7 L, Ford (TSB 19-2315) found water entering connectors C3613 and C4851 of the reductant harness and replaced harness, pump/heater assembly or tank. Deutz uses failure type 11 for it on the EMR5. Lacking a pressure value, the controller suspends dosing.

Missing 5 V reference to the sensor (likelihood: medium)
Failed sensor in the pump/heater assembly (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P204D - Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit High
problem_description: P204D is the high-side counterpart: the pressure signal sits near or above the supply voltage, typically because the signal wire touches 5 V or battery voltage, the sensor ground is open, or the sensor has failed internally. Published limits are 4.80 V on GM's 6.6 L LML, 98 % of the supply in GM's 2018 diesel table, 4.90 V in GM's 2025 DEF controller and 4.85 V on Ford's 2023 diesels. GM's 2014 Cruze diesel logs it as Type B, the other GM tables as Type A. Deutz's EMR L1 calls the same state a short circuit to battery. To the controller such a reading could look like over-pressure, which is why it stops the pump; check the connector at the pump module and the sensor ground before replacing the module.

title: DTC P204E - Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
problem_description: P204E covers a DEF pressure signal that jumps around although it stays inside the electrical limits, as with a loose terminal, a cracked wire or a sensor with an internal contact problem. GM's 2025 DEF controller is the public calibration: it adds up all absolute pressure changes over a moving window of 100 readings taken every 10 ms and counts a failure when that sum passes 1500 kPa while pumping forward, 1000 kPa when stopped or heating, or 200 kPa in reverse; ten failures within 100 runs store a Type A code. No other manufacturer documents the code in public. CARB expects input components to be checked for implausible as well as out-of-range signals. Besides the wiring, air in the line or a pump delivering unevenly can also make the pressure swing.

title: DTC P204F - Reductant System Performance (Bank 1)
problem_description: P204F (Bank 1) is the functional check of the whole DEF delivery path: the parts are electrically intact, yet the system cannot build or hold the pressure needed for dosing. GM's 6.6 L LML stores a Type A code if the pump module stays at or below 350 kPa after 30 build-up and venting attempts of at least 10 s each; the 2014 Cruze diesel uses 375 kPa and 20 attempts. GM treats P204F as a tamper fault. On Hino trucks P204F is the engine ECU's summary code for urea SCR faults seen by the dosing unit; per TT-14-025 it clears only after the DCU faults are repaired and the SCR memory has been reset. Ram's 3.0 L V6 EcoDiesel received PCM updates covering it (18-008-21). CARB demands this delivery check. Causes include frozen or clogged lines, a worn pump, air leaks or an empty tank.
symptoms: MIL and DEF warning on
Countdown to speed or power limitation
Code returns after clearing until the cause is fixed
possible_causes: DEF line clogged by crystals or frozen (likelihood: high)
Worn DEF pump that cannot reach target pressure (likelihood: medium)
Air leak on the suction side or loose line couplings (likelihood: medium)
Dosing unit faults repaired but SCR memory not reset (Hino) (likelihood: medium)
Control module software needing an update (Ram 3.0 L) (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P204F (Reductant System Performance (Bank 1)).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: reductant pump, reductant pressure sensor, reductant lines, reductant injection valve.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 1-6 hours

title: DTC P2050 - Reductant Injection Valve Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Unit 1)
problem_description: P2050 reports an open circuit at the first DEF injector of Bank 2, the cylinder bank opposite cylinder 1. No manufacturer publicly documents P2050; V-engines found in bulletins, such as the Cummins 5.0 L V8 in Nissan's Titan XD, combine both banks into one SCR line and report their only valve as Bank 1, unit 1. Detection would mirror P2047: GM's 2018 diesel logic reads the driver status every 100 ms with more than 11 V and needs 30 bad samples out of 60. CARB requires such actuators to be checked as comprehensive components. Suspects are plug and harness on the second exhaust branch and the coil itself; without dosing that branch emits more NOx.

title: DTC P2051 - Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 2 Unit 1)

The comparable Bank 1 tests give an idea of the limits: GM's 6.6 L LML flags less than roughly 0.5 ohm to ground for 2 s, and Ford's 2023 diesel logic reacts to valve current above 1.6 A. Where the second branch's harness passes hot exhaust parts, damaged insulation is the first thing to inspect. CARB treats the valve as a monitored component; once the code sets, that branch stops dosing and its NOx conversion collapses.

A driver that sees a short to positive normally switches off to protect itself, leaving the second branch without DEF. CARB's comprehensive-component rules apply; check plug, harness and coil resistance first.

title: DTC P2053 - Reductant Injection Valve Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Unit 2)
problem_description: P2053 concerns a second DEF injector on the same exhaust line as Bank 1, unit 1, used where a manufacturer doses at two points, for instance ahead of two separate catalysts. Deutz's EMR5 engines assign P2053 to metering unit 2, with failure bytes for current above normal (grounded) and below normal (open). If valve 2 drops out, valve 1 keeps working, so the downstream catalyst simply loses its DEF and NOx rises only partly, often noticed just through the MIL.

title: DTC P206A - Reductant Quality Sensor Circuit

title: DTC P206F - Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 2)

title: DTC P2072 - Throttle Actuator Control System - Ice Blockage (Bank 1)
problem_description: Not related to the tuning valve: P2072 belongs to the electronic throttle system. If the throttle plate cannot move freely in frost, the controller assumes ice and runs repeated open and close strokes to break it loose; the code records that event. Ford's 2012 OBD summary lists it for second-generation throttle control as a non-MIL fault, and Ford's 2014 code list marks it for the wrench lamp only. FCA bulletin 09-023-23 covers the 2013 to 2023 RAM 1500 with the 3.6L V6: P2072 together with P2110 and P2118, sometimes a no-start below freezing, caused by moisture from the crankcase ventilation freezing on the throttle blade. The fix is drying throttle body and PCV parts, a kit with new air cleaner lid and make-up air hose, plus an oil change. Speed may be limited meanwhile.

title: DTC P2073 - Manifold Absolute Pressure/Mass Air Flow - Throttle Position Correlation at Idle

Ford bulletin 22-2115 reprograms the PCM of 2011 to 2012 F-Super Duty 6.7L trucks that set P2073 or P2074. Ford's 2014 code list also gives it MIL status. Air leaks, a dirty sensor or a clogged filter are typical; P2074 is the load case.

title: DTC P207F - Reductant Quality Performance

title: DTC P2082 - Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
problem_description: P2082 is the plausibility fault of the first exhaust temperature sensor on bank 2, the cylinder bank without cylinder 1. It only exists where both banks carry separate sensors ahead of the merge point, which in practice means V-type petrol engines with turbo or catalyst protection. The diesel tables from GM, Ford and VW number every sensor on bank 1 because one aftertreatment line serves the engine. title: DTC P2090 - "B" Camshaft Position Actuator Control Circuit Low (Bank 1)
problem_description: P2090 refers to actuator B, on engines with twin phasers the exhaust camshaft valve, on bank 1. What Low means depends on how the ECM drives the solenoid. GM's usual high-side output flags a ground short while the valve is energised; the 3.6 L LFX V6 (19OBDG03B) sets P2090 after 20 of 25 samples as Type A, the 2018 hybrid table 18OBDG02 as Type B. title: DTC P2096 - Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Lean (Bank 1)
problem_description: Petrol engines run a slow outer control loop on the oxygen sensor behind the catalyst that shifts the mixture target of the front sensor. P2096 means this post-catalyst trim on bank 1 has hit its limit in the lean direction. The name describes the correction, not the engine: the rear sensor keeps reporting rich exhaust, so the loop keeps taking fuel away. GM's Bosch-based 2005 V6 calls it a rich shift with a correction below -0.03 lambda; GM's 2018 four-cylinders list it as the low limit, with the integral offset at -99 % and the total offset at -50 % or less (Type B); Ford's 2020 to 2023 engines set it 5 s after reaching a rear bias trim of -0.083. Causes are therefore a skewed rear sensor or an upstream sensor reading lean. Audi found a contaminated reference air duct in the rear sensor on 4.0 TFSI engines and warns against replacing the front sensor; GM saw P2096 on new Encore and Trax 1.4 catalysts before break-in and fixed a 2017 Malibu 1.5 by software.

title: DTC P209A - Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor B Circuit
problem_description: Air-assisted DEF dosing, as in Bosch's first Denoxtronic generation of 2004, mixes the fluid with compressed air before it reaches the exhaust, and a pressure sensor confirms that this air is there. title: DTC P209D - Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor B Circuit High

title: DTC P209E - Reductant Injection Air Pressure Sensor A/B Correlation
problem_description: When an air-assisted DEF system carries two air pressure sensors, the controller can compare them under conditions where both should read alike, for instance with the air supply shut and the lines vented to ambient, or at a steady dosing point. The code says nothing about which sensor is wrong; a slow drift of one, a restriction in only one branch or a leak between them all show up this way. The individual sensor faults are P2037 to P2041 for A and P209A to P209D for B. No manufacturer documents P209E publicly. CARB asks for such cross-checks wherever redundant inputs exist. The SCR system typically limits or stops dosing until the cause is found.

Leak in the air path between the two measuring points (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P20A3 - Reductant Purge Control Valve A Circuit High

title: DTC P20A4 - Reductant Purge Control Valve A Stuck Open

title: DTC P20A7 - Reductant Injection Air Pressure Control Valve Performance

problem_description: P20E9 is the overpressure counterpart of P20E8: during closed-loop control the DEF pressure ahead of the dosing valve rises clearly above its target. Ford's 2023 diesel summary sets it at more than 150 kPa over setpoint; GM's 18OBDG04 table asks for the same 150 kPa excess while the pump runs below 3,200 rpm (Type A), and GM's 2025 DEF table 25OBDG04A uses a 63 kPa window for 4 s. VW's 2014 Touareg TDI data book names absolute limits of 650 and 795 kPa. Typical reasons are a blocked return path or dosing valve, deposits from contaminated fluid and a pressure sensor reading high. Audi traced Q7 TDI cases to a damaged AdBlue filter seal that let unfiltered fluid harm sensor and pump; Hino links it to debris in the tank. Ram and Jeep EcoDiesel software bulletins list it as well.

Dosing shut off, NOx warning and later inducement countdown
possible_causes: Blocked return path, restricted line or dosing valve not opening properly (likelihood: high)
Debris in the fluid after a damaged filter seal or dirty refilling (likelihood: medium)
Reductant pressure sensor reading too high (likelihood: medium)
Pump control software needing an update (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P20EA - Reductant Control Module Power Relay De-Energized Performance - Too Early
problem_description: Many SCR systems supply the reductant control module, and through it pump and heaters, via a power relay. After the key is switched off the relay should stay energised for a short after-run so the pump can empty the lines and the module can save its learned values, and only then drop out on the module's command. P20EA means the supply disappeared before that point. Fluid left in the lines can then freeze or crystallise, and stored data may be lost. No maker documents P20EA publicly. The monitoring follows the engine-module pair P068A/P068B: Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel reads back the relay voltage on its control line, and Ford's 2023 diesel summary checks the reductant control module relay (P21C7) by comparing commanded state with the measured voltage. A relay that drops out late is P20EB.
symptoms: Check engine light, often without noticeable driving symptoms
DEF lines not purged, risk of frozen or crystallised lines in winter
possible_causes: Worn relay contacts or coil interrupting the supply early (likelihood: high)
Loose fuse, terminal or ground in the relay or module feed (likelihood: medium)
Battery disconnected or voltage collapsing right after shut-off (likelihood: medium)
Reductant control module releasing the relay prematurely (likelihood: low)

Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: reductant control module, reductant supply relay.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.3-2 hours

title: DTC P20EB - Reductant Control Module Power Relay De-Energized Performance - Too Late
problem_description: Here the opposite of P20EA happens: after the reductant control module has finished its after-run and released the power relay, voltage is still present on the switched side, so the relay opens late or not at all. Typical reasons are welded contacts, a control line shorted to ground that keeps the coil energised, or a module that never ends its shut-down. The DEF module, pump and heaters may then stay powered with the engine off, which drains the battery and keeps the system awake. No maker documents P20EB publicly. The check mirrors P068B on the engine module, which Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel derives from the relay control circuit, and Ford's 2023 diesel summary flags a reductant relay voltage above 0 V while the output stage is off (P21C7). CARB requires such SCR components to be monitored.

title: DTC P20EC - SCR NOx Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 1)
problem_description: P20EC means the engine computer has registered a temperature in the SCR catalyst of bank 1 above the limit its washcoat can tolerate. The limit depends on the formulation: vanadium-based SCR material starts to sublimate irreversibly above roughly 550 °C, as Navistar's patent US20190232224 and the US rule 40 CFR 1036.115 both state, and US heavy-duty certification requires engine makers to protect such catalysts from high temperatures. Copper and iron zeolites tolerate more. No manufacturer documents P20EC publicly with thresholds; Ford's 2023 diesels, for example, report aftertreatment overheating as P200C/P200E. Typical triggers are an uncontrolled exotherm during filter regeneration, fuel or oil reaching the exhaust, or a faulty temperature sensor. The code warns of possible lasting damage, so a later P20EE is a common follow-up.

Regeneration interrupted or power reduced to protect the aftertreatment
Later loss of NOx conversion (follow-up code P20EE)

Unburnt fuel or oil reaching the exhaust (leaking injector, turbo seal) (likelihood: medium)
SCR temperature sensor reading too high (likelihood: medium)
Regeneration or thermal-management calibration needing an update (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P20ED - SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 1)

Paccar's patent US11976582 explains why such close-coupled SCR units exist: they sit where exhaust heat arrives first, so they work soon after a cold start, but for the same reason they see the highest temperatures, including those released by the oxidation catalyst during filter regeneration. P20EC is the same fault on the main catalyst. Expect the MIL; damage later shows as P20EF.

title: DTC P20EE - SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
problem_description: P20EE is the main monitor CARB requires for the NOx-reducing catalyst: the share of NOx removed by the SCR catalyst on bank 1, judged by the NOx sensors before and after it, has fallen below what the system needs. Ford's 2023 6.7 L diesel fails it when cumulative efficiency drops under 55 % with the SCR inlet at 200–320 °C. GM's 2018 diesels compare measured with expected efficiency, partly via an EWMA filter, as a Type A code. Ram and Jeep 3.0 L and 6.7 L diesels had bulletins replacing the SCR catalyst (18-064-15, 18-038-16), Isuzu N-Series and the 2015 Cruze diesel got new software. Because poor DEF also cuts efficiency, GM pairs this code with a DEF quality warning, and a speed limit may follow. Check DEF quality, dosing, leaks and NOx sensors before condemning the catalyst.

title: DTC P20EF - SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)

title: DTC P20F0 - SCR NOx Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2)

When only one bank overheats, the cause tends to sit on that bank, for instance a leaking injector, a misfiring cylinder or a wrong temperature sensor. problem_description: P20F7 is the bank 2 version of P20F6 and only applies to engines with a second exhaust line that has its own SCR catalyst and dosing valve, typically V engines with separate aftertreatment per bank. The control unit judges that this valve no longer closes, usually because pressure cannot be held or the pump must deliver far more than the commanded dose. No maker documents P20F7 publicly; on the bank 1 side FCA uses P20F6 on the 2.0 L diesel Jeep Compass and cures it with software. A Cummins patent explains the underlying comparison of pump effort and expected flow, where a large negative error means a stuck-open valve or a leak. CARB requires reductant delivery faults to be detected before emissions exceed the limits. Overdosing on one bank causes ammonia slip and deposits there. The stuck-closed code for bank 2 is P208F.

Higher DEF consumption and deposits in the bank 2 exhaust
Dosing switched off and later inducement

Mechanically sticking or heat-damaged bank 2 dosing valve (likelihood: medium)
Leaking or detached supply line at the bank 2 valve (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P20F8 - Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 1)
problem_description: P20F8 means the intake manifold runner or swirl flaps on bank 1 do not follow the commanded position, judged by comparing set point and feedback from the position sensor. Mazda found P20F8 on 2023–2025 Mazda3, CX-30, CX-5 and CX-50 caused by the swirl valve motor overheating from frequent actuation and fixed it with new PCM software (bulletin 01-003/26). Drivers notice the MIL and sometimes rough idle or weaker low-end torque.

title: DTC P20FA - Reductant Pump B Control Circuit/Open
problem_description: P20FA means the controller has found an open or otherwise faulty drive circuit for the second reductant (DEF/AdBlue) pump, called pump B or pump 2. FCA lists it as Reductant Pump 2 Control Circuit/Open for 3.0L EcoDiesel models and counts it among the faults that start the Service DEF countdown. With the pump unpowered, dosing stalls and NOx output climbs.

title: DTC P20FC - Reductant Pump B Control Circuit Low

title: DTC P2105 - Throttle Actuator Control System - Forced Engine Shutdown
problem_description: P2105 is the most severe throttle failure mode: the controller has decided that throttle control can no longer be trusted and stops the engine. In Ford's 2012 summary the trigger is a serious processor fault found by the separate monitoring processor (Ford calls it the Quizzer); all injectors are switched off and the wrench lamp comes on. Ford sets it without MIL, arguing that a shutdown cannot raise emissions, which matches the CARB idea of emissions-neutral default actions. The cause sits in the engine computer, its supply or a companion code such as P0606 or P2107. For the driver the engine dies or will not keep running. Milder states are forced idle (P2104), limited power (P2106) and limited rpm (P2110).

Wrench or ETC warning lamp, often without MIL

No manufacturer documents P2141 publicly, so no figures can be quoted; CARB requires circuit faults on output components to be reported. The module usually disables the flap, which then rests open, and EGR is reduced.

title: DTC P2142 - EGR Throttle Control Circuit A High
problem_description: P2142 reports a high signal or overcurrent in the drive circuit of EGR throttle A. Either a motor lead has contact with battery voltage, or the motor draws more current than the output stage allows – from shorted turns or because carbon has jammed the blade. The driver then shuts down for protection, the flap springs back to its rest position and EGR regulation is lost. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P2142; CARB obliges the system to recognise circuit faults of output components in both directions. P2141 is the low counterpart, P0487 the open circuit and P0488 the function check of the same flap; flap B reports a high circuit as P213D. If the cause is mechanical, cleaning or replacing the flap removes it, a wiring short needs a harness repair.

title: DTC P2143 - EGR Vent Control Circuit/Open
problem_description: Vacuum-operated EGR valves are often run by a pair of solenoids: one feeds vacuum to the valve diaphragm to open it, the other – the vent solenoid – lets air in to release the vacuum and close the valve. Ford's EEC engine computers had separate outputs for EGR vent and EGR control, and a Kia diesel patent maps both solenoids by duty cycle, using the vent side whenever the measured EGR value is above target. P2143 means the module found the vent solenoid circuit open or otherwise faulty. Without a working vent the valve may close slowly or stay open longer than wanted, causing rough idle; many systems simply disable EGR. No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P2143. Shorts are reported separately as P2144 and P2145.

title: DTC P2144 - EGR Vent Control Circuit Low
problem_description: P2144 reports a low signal in the circuit that drives the EGR vent solenoid – the valve that bleeds vacuum from a vacuum-operated EGR valve so it can close. With the usual low-side switching, a control wire touching ground keeps the solenoid energised regardless of the command. Whether that leaves the EGR valve unable to open or unable to close depends on the plumbing, but in both cases the EGR rate can no longer be controlled. Ford's 2014 spark-ignition code list includes P2144 with the warning lamp and a continuous test, though Ford gives no threshold; no other public manufacturer document names the code. P2143 covers an open circuit and P2145 the high fault of the same solenoid. Typical results are rough running, higher NOx or a failed EGR readiness test.

title: DTC P2145 - EGR Vent Control Circuit High
problem_description: P2145 is the high fault in the vent solenoid circuit of the EGR system: the control line shows supply voltage while the module tries to pull it to ground, or the driver detects overcurrent through a shorted coil. Ford's 2014 spark-ignition code list names P2145 alongside P2144, both with the warning lamp and a continuous test; thresholds are not given and no further manufacturer document is public. title: DTC P2146 - Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
problem_description: Direct-injection and common-rail injectors are fed by a high-side driver in the engine module, often shared by several injectors. GM bulletin PIP4924D links it to chafed V6 injector harnesses. Expect misfire and rough running.

title: DTC P214A - SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too High
problem_description: P214A reports that the exhaust entering the SCR catalyst was hotter than a calibrated ceiling while no particulate filter regeneration was active. The reading normally comes from the temperature sensor between the filter and the urea mixing section. Heat at this point is a threat to the SCR coating: Navistar's patent US20190232224 states that vanadia sublimates above roughly 550 °C, and 40 CFR 1036.115 obliges heavy-duty engine makers to shield vanadium catalysts from such temperatures. No manufacturer documents P214A publicly; Ram bulletins for the 6.7L Cummins name only the sibling P214D, and Ford flags aftertreatment overheating with P200C/P200E. P214B covers the same fault during regeneration, P214C the outlet side. Typical triggers are fuel or oil in the exhaust, overfuelling or a drifting sensor.

title: DTC P214B - SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too High During Particulate Filter Regeneration
problem_description: P214B is limited to the regeneration phase. To burn soot out of the particulate filter, the engine control adds late injections or uses a separate exhaust fuel injector, and the oxidation catalyst converts that fuel into heat. The code sets when the gas leaving this hot zone arrives at the SCR inlet above the limit allowed during regeneration. Navistar's patent US20190232224 describes exactly this conflict: repeated regenerations push vanadium SCR material towards its sublimation point near 550 °C, so the layout and temperature control must keep the SCR below it. No manufacturer documents P214B publicly. Compared with P214A, suspicion falls on regeneration control: a dripping exhaust injector, excess post-injection or soot burning too fast. The control unit usually aborts the regeneration.

Filter warning or rising soot load because regeneration cannot finish

Excess post-injection quantity from a worn engine injector (likelihood: medium)
Exhaust temperature sensor upstream of the SCR reading too high (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P214C - SCR NOx Catalyst Outlet Temperature Too High

title: DTC P214F - Reductant Heater A Current Too High
problem_description: P214F concerns heater A of the DEF system, which Ford and GM both assign to the heater inside the tank (heater circuit 1). A shorted element, wet connector or chafed lead is the usual reason. Without tank heating, frozen DEF thaws late or not at all, so dosing and NOx reduction start late in winter. title: DTC P215D - Reductant Pump B Stuck On

title: DTC P216C - Fuel Injector Group E Supply Voltage Circuit High
problem_description: P216C is the opposite fault of group E: the feed of the cylinder 5 injector carries voltage when it should not. GM tests it while the high-side driver is switched off; if 1 V or less remains between the signal and the controller supply, the line is treated as shorted to power. Its 2016 3.6 LGX V6 and 2018 6.2 LT4 V8 tables need at least 11 V and count 10 failures out of 20 samples at 100 ms, type A with the MIL on the first trip. Typical sources are a chafed wire touching another powered circuit or an injector winding contacting a live conductor; GM's PI0631H lists this code with dozens of others for the Impala harness that wears on the transmission. Because the injector may stay energised, the module cuts it off and cylinder 5 drops out. P216B is the short to ground.

title: DTC P2172 - Throttle Actuator Control System - Sudden High Air Flow Detected
problem_description: P2172 is set when the engine abruptly takes in far more air than the throttle opening can explain, as if a large leak had appeared behind the throttle plate. title: DTC P2175 - Throttle Actuator Control System - Low Air Flow Detected

title: DTC P2177 - System Too Lean Off Idle (Bank 1)

GM's 2005 V6 and 2008 3.6 LLT set it above a factor of 1.23, GM's 2023 and 2024 tables above 1.27, both over two trips. title: DTC P2180 - System Too Rich Off Idle (Bank 2)

title: DTC P2181 - Cooling System Performance
problem_description: P2181 is the engine computer's verdict that the coolant warms up too slowly or settles below its target, almost always because the thermostat no longer closes. The heater stays lukewarm and fuel use climbs. P0128 is a similar thermostat code.

title: DTC P2182 - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit

title: DTC P2187 - System Too Lean at Idle (Bank 1)

An air leak adds a fixed amount of unmeasured air, which matters most at idle, so it shows up in the additive part. GM's 3.6 V6 engines set the code above 7 % (2005) or 6.1 % (2008 LLT, at 520 to 1120 rpm, 1.7 to 7.8 g/s and coolant above 60 °C), and GM's 2024 tables above about 5.5 %, over two trips. On the Opel/GM 2.0 turbo in the Saab 9-5 (2010) the weighted long-term trim must exceed its limit for 4 s continuously or 50 s in total (Type B). Audi traced P2187 with P2279 on 2.0 TFSI engines to a crankcase ventilation valve that let boost into the crankcase; Mazda found A/F sensor wiring on the CX-7 2.3 turbo shorted after brake fluid was spilled on it.

title: DTC P2189 - System Too Lean at Idle (Bank 2)
problem_description: P2189 is the bank 2 version of P2187: on engines with a front oxygen sensor per bank, the long-term trim of bank 2 has to add more fuel than allowed at idle and low load. Because both banks share the throttle, crankcase ventilation and brake booster vacuum, a leak there normally lifts the idle trim on both banks, setting P2187 and P2189 together. A code on bank 2 alone points to something only that bank sees: an intake manifold gasket or runner leak on that side, an injector on that bank, or the bank 2 front sensor or its wiring. Comparing both banks' trims at idle and at 2500 rpm narrows it down.

Rough or hunting idle

Shared vacuum leak, usually with P2187 present too (likelihood: medium)
Bank 2 front sensor, its wiring or an injector on that bank (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P218A - Throttle Actuator B Control System - Idle Position Not Learned
problem_description: P218A is the throttle B counterpart of P2176: on engines with a second electronic throttle, usually one per cylinder bank, that second unit failed to learn its closed rest position. GM's 2023 table 23OBDG07 runs the same three-step learn for bank 2 as for bank 1. First the plate must reach the closed target within 1.5 %, then the motor has to press it onto the stop with enough duty cycle, and finally the stored voltages must fall inside 0.33-0.58 V for sensor 1 and 4.42-4.67 V for sensor 2; any failed step stores the code within one trip. No other manufacturer documents P218A publicly. Ice, carbon, a weak motor or wiring faults at throttle B are typical causes, and engine power may be limited. Electrical motor faults of throttle B use P210A.

Supply or signal wiring fault at throttle B (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P218F - Reductant No Flow Detected

Ford also lists it for the 6.7 L Power Stroke (18-2127, PCM update). Nissan reflashed Titan XD trucks with the Cummins 5.0 L V8 when P218F appeared at 0 °C or below. title: DTC P2198 - O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 2, Sensor 1)

title: DTC P21B4 - NOx Adsorber - Over Temperature (Bank 1)
problem_description: P21B4 reports that the NOx adsorber on bank 1 has run hotter than the manufacturer's protection limit. The risk is greatest during desulphation, when the adsorber is heated on purpose: Eaton patent US7251929 gives about 750 °C as the maximum desulphation temperature, beyond which the adsorber ages thermally, while Cummins aims for roughly 650 °C during regeneration (US7594392). Excess heat comes from too much fuel in rich phases, leaking injectors, unburnt fuel after misfires, or a temperature signal that reads wrong. No manufacturer documents its P21B4 limit publicly; the code can only occur on engines with such a catalyst, for instance the 2007–2011 Ram 6.7L Cummins. Act promptly: repeated overheating ruins the storage coating and leads to P2000.

Reduced power while the engine protects the catalyst
Strong smell or heat from the exhaust

title: DTC P21C2 - Reductant Heater Relay Control Circuit/Open
problem_description: P21C2 concerns the control line of the relay that supplies current to the DEF heaters. The control module drives the relay coil through an output stage and checks whether the circuit reacts; an open circuit means the coil, its wiring or a connector has lost continuity, so the heaters cannot be energised. Ford documents the code in its 2023 diesel summary: the check runs continuously while heating is requested, and with the relay stage on and every heater switched off, a heater current below 0.2 A sets P21C2 within at most 5 s. P21C3 and P21C4 are the low and high faults of the same line, P21C7 covers the power relay of the module itself. In frost the fluid may stay frozen, so dosing starts late and DEF warnings can follow.

problem_description: P21C3 is the low-side fault on the control line of the DEF heater relay: the signal is pulled toward ground, for example by a chafed wire touching the frame or a shorted relay coil, so the relay no longer follows the command. Ford's 2023 diesel summary uses the same continuous check as for P21C2, but here the relay stage is on, every heater has been told to stay off, and still more than 6 A of heater current is measured; the fault is confirmed within 5 s. Such a reading means power reaches the heater circuit by a path the module never requested. Whether the heaters then stay dead or run without control depends on how the relay is wired. P21C2 is the open-circuit counterpart, P21C4 the high-side fault, P21C7 the module power relay.

DEF heating inactive or running when not commanded
Blown fuse in the heater supply

Water or salt in the relay or heater connector (likelihood: medium)
Output stage of the controlling module faulty (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P21C5 - Reductant Level Sensor A Stuck

title: DTC P21C6 - Reductant Level Sensor B Stuck

It is stored when that second reading is electrically fine but stays frozen at one value although the module expects it to change. No manufacturer documents P21C6 publicly. title: DTC P21C7 - Reductant Control Module Power Relay/Relays Control Circuit/Open

title: DTC P21C8 - Reductant Control Module Power Relay/Relays Control Circuit Low
problem_description: P21C8 means the control line of the DEF module's power relay, or relays, sits too close to ground. No manufacturer documents P21C8 publicly. The engine module pair P0685/P0686 is the closest analogy. P21C9 is the high-side fault.

title: DTC P21CB - Reductant Control Module Supply Voltage Low

title: DTC P21CC - Reductant Control Module Supply Voltage High
problem_description: P21CC is the overvoltage counterpart of P21CB: the DEF control module sees a supply above what its electronics are designed for. Ford's 2023 diesel summary checks the reductant pump controller in a continuous loop and sets P21CC once its supply exceeds 19 V, deciding within 5 s. problem_description: The DEF quality module measures the urea concentration in the tank and, on many tanks, shares a housing with the level sensor. P21CD reports that its supply voltage is too low. title: DTC P222E - Barometric Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

title: DTC P223C - O2 Sensor Pumping Current Range/Performance (Bank 1)

CARB requires circuit and out-of-range faults of fuel-control sensors to be detected and, where feasible, stored as separate codes. P2252 is the bank 1 counterpart, P2256 the high-side fault. title: DTC P2257 - AIR System Control A Circuit Low

title: DTC P225A - NOx Sensor Calibration Memory (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
problem_description: P225A concerns the front NOx sensor of bank 1, the one ahead of the SCR catalyst. Modern NOx probes come with their own control unit that holds a sensor-specific calibration and reports finished values over CAN; this code means the stored calibration data of that unit cannot be read or fails its check. Ford's 2014 PCM code table carries P225A as a MIL code, but no manufacturer publishes the test or a threshold. Ford's 2023 diesels report memory errors inside the NOx sensor module under P2200 instead. CARB requires NOx sensor faults to be caught when the sensor can no longer serve as a feedback or monitoring input. P225B is the same fault on the downstream sensor. Usually the sensor assembly is replaced, as its memory cannot be repaired.

SCR dosing runs without valid feedback, so NOx emissions may rise

title: DTC P2260 - AIR System Control B Circuit High

title: DTC P2261 - Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A - Mechanical

A flutter or rattle on lift-off is typical.

title: DTC P2262 - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Pressure A Not Detected - Mechanical
problem_description: P2262 says boost pressure A does not appear at all although the charging system should be producing it, and the cause appears to be mechanical rather than a sensor fault. The control unit sees the pressure after the compressor stay near ambient or close to manifold pressure. VW's 2014 book for the supercharged Touareg 3.0 TSI uses the ratio of boost to manifold pressure and flags it below a band of 1 to 1.25. Volvo technical journal 31319 (2016 four-cylinder B4204T23) traced P2262 together with P02CD to a fresh-air hose that had slipped off the air filter housing at the MAF; a spring clamp prevents a repeat. Unlike P0299, which measures a shortfall against the target, P2262 stands for boost missing altogether; P2263 rates overall control performance and P226B the opposite extreme. Acceleration feels flat, and many engines limit torque.

title: DTC P226A - Water in Fuel Lamp Control Circuit

title: DTC P2271 - O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 1, Sensor 2)

title: DTC P2280 - Air Flow Restriction/Air Leak Between Air Filter and MAF (Bank 1)
problem_description: P2280 is the bank 1 code for restricted airflow or an air leak between the air filter and the MAF sensor. A blocked filter lowers the pressure ahead of the sensor and limits the air the engine can take in. A leak in this section matters less for fuel metering, since the air still passes the MAF, but it lets unfiltered air and dust reach the engine. FCA's heavy-duty Ram trucks with the 6.7 L Cummins diesel are the documented users: with 2016 software, bulletin 18-027-16 made P2280 wait for two trips instead of one before the MIL, and FCA tech tip 9003821 (2017) notes MIL events where oil-soaked intake filters were being replaced. FCA's older wording names the code without a bank. P227F is the bank 2 counterpart, P2281 covers the stretch from the MAF to the throttle.
symptoms: MIL on
Less power and slower boost build-up under load
More smoke from diesel engines when accelerating
possible_causes: Air filter clogged or soaked with oil (likelihood: high)
Snow, ice or debris in the air inlet, or a collapsed intake duct (likelihood: medium)
Cracked duct or loose clamp between filter box and MAF (likelihood: medium)
Early software that flags the condition too readily (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2280 (Air Flow Restriction/Air Leak Between Air Filter and MAF (Bank 1)).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: air filter, intake duct, mass air flow sensor.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.2-1.5 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Air filter clogged or soaked with oil (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Snow, ice or debris in the air inlet, or a collapsed intake duct (likelihood: medium).
Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.

title: DTC P2281 - Air Leak Between MAF and Throttle Body
problem_description: P2281 points to air that escapes or enters between the MAF sensor and the throttle body, so the airflow the sensor reports no longer matches what reaches the cylinders. On turbocharged engines this section includes the compressor, the charge air cooler and their hoses: a loose clamp or split boot can blow off charge air under boost or draw in unmeasured air at idle. FCA is the documented user: across 2013 to 2026 Ram trucks with the 6.7 L Cummins diesel, flash bulletins such as 18-053-14 and 18-027-16 bring software meant to stop unwarranted MIL events for P2281. No manufacturer publishes the detection method or a threshold; an air-model comparison like Ford's speed-density check for P2282 is the likely principle. A real leak costs boost and power and leads to smoke on diesels. P2280 sits before the MAF, P2282 after the throttle.
symptoms: MIL on
Hissing under boost and less power
Black smoke on diesels or rough idle on petrol engines
possible_causes: Loose clamp, split hose or leaking charge air cooler between MAF and throttle (likelihood: high)
Contaminated or drifting MAF sensor that misreports airflow (likelihood: medium)
Engine software that sets the code without a real leak (update available) (likelihood: medium)
Disconnected crankcase vent or other hose joined to this section (likelihood: low)

Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: intake duct, throttle body, mass air flow sensor, charge air pipe.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.3-3 hours

title: DTC P2282 - Air Leak Between Throttle Body and Intake Valves
problem_description: P2282 means air enters the intake behind the throttle, so it reaches the cylinders without passing the throttle. Ford uses it as its PCV monitor on turbo engines with speed density: airflow worked out from manifold pressure is compared with airflow through the throttle, and a calculated leak of 1 lb/min or more for at least 5 s, with the throttle at 4 degrees or less, sets the code (2012, 2020-2023 and 2024 summaries). Ford designed the PCV inlet tube so that pulling it off leaves a large, detectable opening. Ford bulletins blame a stuck-open brake vacuum valve or tube on the 2.0 EcoBoost in the 2019-2020 Edge and Nautilus (TSB 20-2151), ice in the manifold of the 2020-2021 Escape hybrid (SSM 49654) and PCM software on the 2023 Maverick hybrid (TSB 23-2193). Land Rover found a detached brake vacuum pipe (LTB01186).
symptoms: High or unstable idle speed
MIL on, sometimes with a hissing noise from the engine bay
Harder brake pedal if the brake vacuum line is affected
possible_causes: Brake booster vacuum pipe detached or its check valve stuck open (likelihood: high)
Crankcase ventilation hose disconnected or cracked (likelihood: high)
Leaking intake manifold gasket, throttle body seal or vacuum hose (likelihood: medium)
Iced manifold pressure sensor or software miscalculating the leak (likelihood: low)

Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.

title: DTC P2283 - Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit
problem_description: P2283 is the general circuit code for the injector control pressure (ICP) sensor. ICP describes the high-pressure engine oil that hydraulically actuated unit injectors (HEUI) use to pressurise fuel, as on Navistar-built Ford Power Stroke diesels; the sensor reports rail pressure so the injection pressure regulator can be closed-loop controlled. No manufacturer documents P2283 publicly. Ford's 6.0L summaries for 2003 and 2004 split the electrical check into P2285 (below 0.03 V) and P2286 (above 4.83 V), and Ford's 2014 PCM code table lists those two but not P2283. CARB requires diesel fuel-pressure control, explicitly including hydraulic fluid, to be monitored. Without a valid ICP signal the PCM substitutes a default value, so power and starting suffer.

Hard or long cranking, especially when hot
MIL on
possible_causes: Failed ICP sensor, often with oil inside the connector (likelihood: high)
Damaged signal, reference or ground wire of the sensor (likelihood: medium)
5-volt reference circuit pulled down by another sensor (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2284 - Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
problem_description: P2284 means the measured injector control pressure does not follow what the PCM commands. Ford's 6.0L Power Stroke summaries (2003 and 2004) run the check continuously every 8 ms with the engine running: a fault is recorded once measured pressure stays more than 3.0 MPa above the target for longer than 7 s, the reverse case being P2290. Because the high-pressure oil pump is regulated through the IPR valve against the sensor reading, a biased sensor, a sticking regulator or an air-entrained oil supply can all open this gap. Ford also ran a 2003 owner programme replacing ICP sensors whose O-ring could shift and cause reduced power and rough idle. Unlike P2285/P2286 the circuit voltage is valid here; only its relation to the command is wrong.

Engine runs on a substitute pressure value
MIL on
possible_causes: ICP sensor reading offset, including a shifted internal O-ring (likelihood: high)
Injection pressure regulator valve sticking or contaminated (likelihood: medium)
Wrong, aerated or low engine oil disturbing pressure control (likelihood: medium)
Oil wicking into the sensor connector (likelihood: low)

Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: icp sensor, high pressure oil pump, icp wiring.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-4 hours

title: DTC P2285 - Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
problem_description: P2285 is set when the ICP sensor voltage falls almost to zero. Ford's 6.0L Power Stroke summaries for 2003 and 2004 define it precisely: below 0.03 V, checked every 8 ms without entry conditions, decided in under one second. Such a value cannot come from a working sensor on a 5-volt reference, so it points to an open signal wire, a short to ground, a lost reference voltage or an unplugged sensor. Ford lights the MIL for P2285 even on heavy federal trucks over 8,500 lb that otherwise run a reduced OBD calibration. On a HEUI engine the PCM then has to estimate rail pressure, so starting and response deteriorate. P2286 is the high-voltage counterpart; P2284 covers a valid signal that disagrees with the commanded pressure.

Hard starting and reduced power
possible_causes: Signal wire open or shorted to ground (likelihood: high)
Sensor disconnected or failed internally (likelihood: medium)
Missing 5-volt reference supply (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P2287 - Injector Control Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
problem_description: P2287 covers an ICP sensor signal that drops out or jumps for brief moments, too short or too irregular to be judged as a steady low or high fault. No manufacturer documents P2287 publicly; Ford's 6.0L summaries and its 2014 PCM table contain the steady electrical codes P2285 and P2286 but not this one. On HEUI diesels the sensor is mounted on the engine in a hot, oily environment, so oil creeping into the connector, fretting terminals and harness rubbing are the usual reasons for an unstable signal. Since the PCM regulates high-pressure oil from this reading, short dropouts can make the engine stumble or surge before a substitute value takes over. CARB counts such inputs among the components whose circuit faults must be monitored.

title: DTC P2288 - Injector Control Pressure Too High
problem_description: P2288 reports that the injector control pressure itself, not just its reading, has climbed above the allowed maximum while the engine runs. Ford's 6.0L Power Stroke summaries put the limit at 27.5 MPa in the 2003 edition and 29.5 MPa in 2004, sustained for more than 3 s. For comparison, Ford's high-pressure oil pump normally works between about 3 and 25 MPa on that engine. Excessive pressure means the injection pressure regulator fails to release enough oil to drain, because it sticks, its coil is driven wrongly or the control signal is stuck; a sensor reading high but still within circuit limits can also mislead. The PCM limits fuelling to protect the injectors and oil system. P2290 is the too-low case; P2289 the same check with the engine off.

title: DTC P2289 - Injector Control Pressure Too High - Engine Off
problem_description: P2289 is a plausibility test carried out with the engine stopped. On a HEUI diesel the high-pressure oil pump is driven by the engine, so once it stops, injector control pressure should drop to almost nothing. Ford's 6.0L Power Stroke summaries check this in engine-off mode: if the ICP reading stays above 10 MPa for more than 10 s (2003) or 12 s (2004), P2289 is stored. A real pressure that high without a running pump is unlikely, so the code mainly points to an ICP sensor with an offset or contamination, or to a signal circuit pulled up by a fault that stays within the electrical limits of P2286. Ford's 2014 PCM table marks it as a MIL code. P2288 is the counterpart with the engine running.

title: DTC P228A - Fuel Pressure Regulator A - Forced Engine Shutdown
problem_description: P228A is a protective shutdown code: the engine computer has stopped the engine because rail pressure could not be held even with fuel pressure regulator A at full authority. In GM's 2018 diesel tables regulator 1 (A) is the fuel metering unit on the high-pressure pump; the fault is logged when actual pressure lags the setpoint by more than 40 MPa while the commanded pump flow is already at its maximum, in 640 of 800 samples taken every 12.5 ms (about 8 s), as a Type A code. GM bulletin 18-NA-103 lists P228A and P228B next to P0087 when gelled winter diesel starves the in-tank pump. P228B is the same reaction for regulator B, P228C the milder control-limit warning. Expect a stall or no restart until supply is restored.
symptoms: Engine stalls while driving or shuts off shortly after starting
Long cranking or no restart
Check engine light on, often with P0087
Whining in-tank fuel pump in cold weather

Fuel metering unit on the high-pressure pump sticking or worn (likelihood: medium)
High-pressure pump no longer reaching the required delivery (likelihood: medium)
Leak in the high-pressure circuit or injector return (likelihood: low)
