title: DTC P228B - Fuel Pressure Regulator B - Forced Engine Shutdown
problem_description: P228B mirrors P228A but concerns fuel pressure regulator B, which in GM's 2018 diesel calibration is the rail pressure regulator valve that spills surplus fuel from the rail. The ECM shuts the engine down when rail pressure stays more than 40 MPa below target although it already commands that valve fully closed, judged over 640 of 800 samples at 12.5 ms and stored as Type A. A fully closed spill valve should trap everything the pump delivers, so a remaining deficit points to a valve leaking internally, a weak pump, a starved supply (GM bulletin 18-NA-103: gelled diesel, together with P228A and P0087) or excessive injector leakage. P229A is the non-shutdown deviation check of the same regulator.

title: DTC P228C - Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low
problem_description: P228C means rail pressure has stayed below target long enough that regulator A, the path that sets pump delivery, is judged to have used up its correction. title: DTC P228E - Fuel Pressure Regulator A Exceeded Learning Limits - Too Low
problem_description: P228E reports that the self-learned correction of fuel pressure regulator A has reached its lower bound. Ford, which still calls the part regulator 1, explains the logic in its 2023 diesel summary for the 3.0 L and 6.7 L Power Stroke: whenever requested rail pressure is at least 600 bar, the PCM keeps adapting the pressure controller, and if the adaptation factor drifts beyond a limit equivalent to roughly a 20 % error in rail pressure sensor slope, it stores P228E or P228F after about 10 s. Ford's 2014 PCM code table marks both as MIL codes. A learned value at the floor suggests a pressure sensor whose characteristic has shifted or a pump and regulator no longer matching their model. P228F is the upper bound, P229C the same test for regulator B.

title: DTC P2294 - Fuel Pressure Regulator B Control Circuit/Open

title: DTC P2295 - Fuel Pressure Regulator B Control Circuit Low
problem_description: P2295 stands for the control line of fuel pressure regulator B touching ground. title: DTC P2296 - Fuel Pressure Regulator B Control Circuit High

title: DTC P22C8 - Turbocharger Compressor Outlet Valve Stuck Open
problem_description: P22C8 is a functional fault: the compressor outlet valve stays open at a moment when the control strategy expects it shut, so pressure or airflow in the boost path does not follow the command. Mercedes-Benz uses it on the M256.8 inline six with its 48-volt electric auxiliary compressor. Bulletin LI09.41-P-078735 in its second version (March 2025) added P22C800 next to P22C900 for E, CLS, GLE and GLS 450, S 500/580 e and AMG 53 models and blames a jammed check valve in the charge-air pipe; the fix is a new charge-air line with integrated check valve. problem_description: Open-circuit code for the gas injector of cylinder 8. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. In the two manufacturer-side lists found, the Ford overview from 2014 and TransEco's sheet for gas-converted Ford V8 and V10 trucks, cylinder 8 has only P22F6 and P22F7, and the TransEco table explicitly assigns an open line to P22F6. CARB permits this shortcut for output circuits. Where P22F5 is used, the module would flag it when no current flows through the cylinder 8 valve after it is commanded on. Typical findings are a pulled or corroded plug at the rear of the bank, a wire broken by engine movement or an internally open coil. That cylinder then gets no gas, while gasoline mode stays usable on bi-fuel trucks.

Coil of the cylinder 8 gas valve open (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P22F6 - Cylinder 8 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit Low
problem_description: Cylinder 8 is the last cylinder with a generic gas injector code; beyond it the Altech-Eco/TransEco table for the Ford 6.8 V10 switches to manufacturer codes. title: DTC P22F7 - Cylinder 8 Alternative Fuel Injector Control Circuit High
problem_description: P22F7 means the drive line of the cylinder 8 gas injector cannot be pulled down and stays near supply voltage. title: DTC P22F9 - NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response Low to High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)

GM's 2025 diesel table starts both timers at 30 ppm and stops them at 220 ppm; a lag beyond 2 s or a relative delay above 10 % fails the check, rated Type B with the MIL after two trips. P22FA covers the falling direction, P22FC the rear sensor. A sluggish front sensor feeds the urea dosing late information, so NOx output may climb.

title: DTC P22FC - NOx Sensor Performance - Slow Response Low to High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)

title: DTC P2300 - Ignition Coil A Primary Control Circuit Low

title: DTC P2302 - Ignition Coil A Secondary Circuit
problem_description: P2302 looks at the high-voltage side of coil A – the secondary winding, the boot and the spark plug of cylinder 1 – rather than at the control line covered by P2300 and P2301. Only a few makers use it. FCA does on the 3.6-litre Pentastar V6 in 2015–2016 Dodge Caravan and Chrysler Town & Country vans, where the code name speaks of too little ionization on the secondary side of coil 1: the module judges combustion from the ion current across the plug gap, and a weak signal means the spark did not light the mixture properly. Bulletin 18-069-16 replaced the PCM on vans built between 27 July and 11 September 2015. Ford, by contrast, leaves even primary winding faults of its coil-mounted drivers to the misfire monitor, so they show up as P0301 or P0300. If misfire reaches a catalyst-damaging rate, CARB requires a flashing MIL.

title: DTC P230A - Cylinder 1 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance - Adjustment At Limit During Balance

title: DTC P232A - TCM Request - Forced Engine Shutdown

title: DTC P232B - Cylinder 11 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Min Limit

problem_description: The offset-learning codes for injector A of cylinders 1 to 10 sit at P02CC to P02DF; cylinders 11 and 12 were placed separately at P232B to P232E, and P232D is the lower limit for cylinder 12, the last cylinder of a V12. The engine module calibrates each injector in overrun with small test injections and crankshaft-acceleration feedback (GM: test quantity around 1.5 mm³, values kept per rail pressure level). At the lower bound the injector reaches the expected torque with clearly shorter energizing than nominal – a sign of over-delivery or leakage. CARB counts an exhausted fuel feedback correction as a malfunction. Twelve-cylinder diesels are very rare in OBD-regulated vehicles – Audi sold a V12 TDI Q7 from 2008 to 2012 – and no maker documents P232D publicly; the second injector per cylinder has its own B series from P2C52.

Possibly harsher combustion noise or knocking at idle
Possibly more smoke or consumption

Correction code not programmed after fitting a new injector (likelihood: medium)
Crankshaft signal disturbed (tone wheel, sensor, flywheel) (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P232E - Cylinder 12 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Max Limit
problem_description: P232E closes the row of injector A offset-learning codes: cylinder 12, upper limit. The learned extra energizing time for this injector has run to the top of its range for at least one rail pressure level, meaning the injector needs much longer activation than its nominal map to give the expected small-quantity torque – it under-delivers or opens late, often from coking or wear. The lower limit is P232D, cylinder 11 uses P232B/P232C.

title: DTC P232F - O2 Sensor Out of Range During Deceleration (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
problem_description: P232F checks the downstream oxygen signal of bank 1 while fuel is cut on deceleration and the exhaust holds almost pure air. Ford tests its rear petrol sensor in overrun too but files results under P013A, P013E or P2270. Code lists give P239E the same title. Causes are a drifting sensor, an exhaust leak or wiring faults.

title: DTC P2332 - Ignition Coil K Secondary Circuit
problem_description: P2332 reserves a code for trouble between coil K and the plug of cylinder 11. No manufacturer documents it publicly: the only published secondary-circuit series, FCA's ion-current codes, covers coils 1 to 8, and twelve-cylinder makers do not release their code lists. Ion-current sensing, known from Saab's Direct Ignition, would be one way to detect such a fault; another is evaluating the secondary voltage. On a V12 with coil-on-plug, the high-voltage path is short – coil tower, boot, plug – so the usual faults are a perforated boot, oil in the plug well or an eroded plug. Whatever the source, CARB still demands cylinder-specific misfire detection, so P0311 is the more likely code to appear. P2330/P2331 cover the primary wiring of the same coil.

GM and Saab file a single knocking cylinder under P0324 instead (more than 8 s). Lasting knock can damage pistons, so the code should be followed up soon.

title: DTC P233B - Fuel Pressure Regulator C Control Circuit Low
problem_description: P233B points to the ground side of fuel pressure regulator C: the line between valve and low-side driver has contact with ground. In GM's 2025 diesel table 25OBDG04B, regulator C is the second fuel metering unit valve, and the ECM checks this line while the driver is switched off. If the voltage there is too low, meaning less than about 0.5 Ohm towards ground, the sample counts as failed; sampling runs at 100 ms with more than 11 V supply and the engine not cranking, and the code is Type A with the MIL in the first trip. A grounded low-side line can energise the valve permanently, so pump delivery no longer follows the command. GM bulletin 21-NA-149 names P233B for the 3.0L LM2 diesel after harness chafing. The open-circuit test is P233A, the opposite short P233C.

Rail pressure too high or unstable, rough running
Reduced engine power possible

Moisture or corrosion bridging pins in the valve connector (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P234A - Cylinder 9 Pressure Sensor Circuit Low

title: DTC P2369 - Cylinder 12 Pressure Sensor Circuit High
problem_description: P2369 means the cylinder 12 pressure input reads above its upper limit. Like the rest of the cylinder-12 family, it is not documented publicly by any maker. On Saab's 9-5 diesel the matching cylinder-1 code P0398 is set after more than 2 s above the threshold and is evaluated once per operating cycle. An unplugged sensor drives the value past 10,000 kPa, so to the ECM an open signal or open low-reference wire looks the same as a short to voltage. Saab tells the cases apart with a fused jumper between signal and low reference: the reading should then drop below 50 kPa; if it stays high, the fault lies in the wiring towards the ECM, otherwise in the plug. While the code is active, the ECM has no usable pressure feedback from this cylinder.

title: DTC P236B - Cylinder 12 Pressure Too Low

title: DTC P2396 - Diesel Intake Air Flow B Position Sensor Circuit
problem_description: P2396 is the general electrical fault of the sensor that reports the angle of the B intake throttle, a potentiometer or, on newer units, a contactless Hall sensor with analogue or SENT output. The code says only that the signal is electrically implausible, without telling whether the reading sits under or over its window; makers that separate the two would set P2398 or P2399 instead. No manufacturer was found that uses P2396. On the A side the LML 6.6 L Duramax tables from GM accept 0.40 to 4.72 V and Ford's 2023 diesels 0.08 to 4.92 V before they set their split codes. Without a valid position the module cannot run closed-loop control and usually de-energises the flap. Check the 5 V reference, ground and signal wire and the connector before replacing the throttle unit, which normally contains the sensor.
symptoms: MIL on
Flap switched off, EGR runs with limited control
Regeneration postponed
possible_causes: Corroded or loose sensor connector (likelihood: high)
Damaged reference, ground or signal wire (likelihood: medium)
Failed position sensor in the throttle unit (likelihood: medium)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2396 (Diesel Intake Air Flow B Position Sensor Circuit).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: diesel intake throttle position sensor, diesel intake throttle valve, sensor wiring.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.5-2 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Corroded or loose sensor connector (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Damaged reference, ground or signal wire (likelihood: medium).
Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.
source: OBDex / SAE J2012 & ISO 15031-6 Open Diagnostic Standard

title: DTC P2397 - Diesel Intake Air Flow B Position Sensor Range/Performance
problem_description: P2397 covers a B-throttle position signal that stays inside its electrical window but does not make sense, for instance a reading that does not move when the motor is driven, or one that disagrees with the commanded angle. CARB asks for such rationality checks on inputs wherever feasible. No published manufacturer table covers P2397. The 6.6 L LML calibration from GM handles the A valve this way under P02E7 and flags a control deviation beyond ±10 % lasting 10 s. Because a sticking flap and a drifting sensor produce the same pattern, compare the scan-tool angle with the real flap position and check the sensor's contact resistance before blaming the actuator. The MIL and reduced EGR control are the main effects; some engines also cut power.

Occasionally reduced power

title: DTC P2398 - Diesel Intake Air Flow B Position Sensor Circuit Low
problem_description: P2398 is logged when the position signal of the B intake throttle falls below its lower limit. Likely reasons are a signal lead shorted to ground, a lost 5 V supply, or a broken signal wire that the module input pulls low; on SENT sensors the transmitted raw value can also leave its range. No manufacturer documents P2398 itself. For the A valve, GM's LML reacts to less than 0.40 V persisting 5 s, its SENT-equipped 2017 diesels to under 1 % of 5 V in 200 of 250 checks (two trips), while Ford's 2023 diesels flag readings under 0.08 V lasting 3 s. If several 5 V sensors fail at once, suspect a shorted shared reference circuit. The flap is normally switched off, leaving the EGR loop with less control.

Regeneration suspended

Internally failed position sensor (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2399 - Diesel Intake Air Flow B Position Sensor Circuit High
problem_description: P2399 is the upper-limit counterpart of P2398: the B-throttle position signal reads higher than any real flap angle can produce. That usually points to a lost sensor ground, a signal wire touching the 5 V reference or battery voltage, or water bridging the terminals in the connector. No manufacturer is known to publish P2399. For the A valve the LML Duramax from GM uses P02E9 once the voltage exceeds 4.72 V during 5 s; Ford's 2023 diesels react when 4.92 V is passed for 3 s. Measure the ground lead back to the module first, since a weak ground lifts the signal without the sensor itself being damaged. The consequences resemble those of the other sensor codes: flap de-energised, MIL, EGR and regeneration compromised.

title: DTC P239B - Diesel Intake Air Flow B Control Motor Current Range/Performance
problem_description: P239B checks the current the B-throttle motor draws while its H-bridge is switched on. A blocked or very stiff flap, a partly shorted winding or the two motor leads touching each other push the current beyond what the module expects. No manufacturer publishes P239B with values. GM's 2017 diesels set the A-motor code P02EB once more than 5.5 A is seen in 160 out of 200 evaluations while the powertrain relay delivers over 11 V; the MIL follows on the second trip. What sets it apart from P2393 is the origin of the excess current: here it comes from the load itself rather than from a lead touching battery voltage. Checking whether the flap moves freely, with the unit removed if necessary, shows whether it binds. Once the driver shuts down, the spring opens the flap; the engine keeps running with restricted EGR control.

Flap switched off and resting at spring position
Often stored together with P2391 or the stuck codes

title: DTC P239C - Diesel Intake Air Flow B Control System - High Air Flow Detected
problem_description: P239C belongs to the air-mass control loop rather than to the throttle alone: with the B intake throttle taking part in that control, the module sees more fresh air than its target and cannot bring the reading down even at the limit of its authority. Too little recirculated exhaust gas is both the usual cause and the consequence, from an EGR valve stuck shut, a blocked EGR cooler, a flap that cannot close or an air-mass meter reading high. No manufacturer was found that uses P239C. Ford's 2023 diesels run this test for their single intake throttle under P02EC, comparing desired and measured air mass against a speed/torque map; the 6.7 L needs 10 s, the 3.0 L 5 s. NOx emissions rise; driveability normally stays unchanged.

No noticeable driving change in most cases
Often stored together with EGR flow codes

Air-mass meter reading too high (likelihood: medium)
Boost higher than intended (likelihood: low)

Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: egr valve, diesel intake throttle valve, mass air flow sensor.

title: DTC P239D - Diesel Intake Air Flow B Control System - Low Air Flow Detected
problem_description: P239D is the mirror image of P239C: the measured fresh-air mass remains below target although the control loop involving the B intake throttle is already at its limit. Candidates are an EGR valve that will not close and floods the intake with exhaust gas, a B flap stuck partly shut (often together with P2395), a restricted air filter or charge-air path, a turbocharger delivering too little, or an air-mass meter reading low. No manufacturer is known to publish P239D. Ford's 2023 diesels check the same condition for their one intake throttle as P02ED, with a detection time of ten seconds on the 6.7 L engine and half that on the 3.0 L. As the engine is short of air, black smoke, rapid soot loading of the DPF and a loss of power are typical; limp mode is possible.

Black smoke
Frequent particulate filter regenerations

title: DTC P23A2 - Exhaust Heat Exchanger Exhaust Bypass Valve B Control Circuit/Open

CARB requires emission-related output components to be checked for circuit faults. P23A3 and P23A4 narrow the fault to low or high; P237C is valve A.

title: DTC P23F0 - Camshaft B Position Signal Output Circuit Low (Bank 2)

title: DTC P240D - Alternative Fuel Low Pressure System Leak
problem_description: P240D applies only to vehicles running on a gaseous alternative fuel such as CNG or LPG, which CARB counts as alternate-fueled. How P240D is detected is not published by any manufacturer; a plausible approach is watching how pressure behaves with the shut-off valves closed. P240E is the matching code for the high-pressure side. A gas leak is a safety issue: stop using the gas system and have it inspected.

title: DTC P2413 - EGR System Performance
problem_description: P2413 is a broad EGR performance code, and makers fill it in different ways. Typical results are higher NOx, a failed emissions test and, on diesels, reduced power. Narrower flow faults are P0401 and P0402, slow response P240F.

title: DTC P241A - O2 Sensor Signals Swapped (Bank 1 Sensor 1 / Bank 1 Sensor 2)

title: DTC P242A - Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 3)

title: DTC P242F - Particulate Filter Restriction - Ash Accumulation (Bank 1)
problem_description: P242F reports that so much incombustible ash has collected in the bank 1 particulate filter that it restricts flow and no regeneration can clear it. GM's 2018 diesel tables watch for the same condition but file it under P24A4, which GM labels ash accumulation: a filtered flow resistance from differential pressure and exhaust flow, 5 failures in 10 samples, Type A. GM mentions P2438 next to P2437 among the codes that block its AIR sensor and flow tests in the 2018 tables, but publishes no row of its own for it, because the engines described there have one air path. For comparison, GM's bank 1 sensor fails above 94–95 % of the 5 V reference. Typical triggers are a signal shorted to supply voltage, an open ground or an internal sensor defect; Audi's R8 V10, which carries a separate bank 2 sensor G610, shows where such a part sits. No public manufacturer document describes the conditions for P2438 itself. While it is stored, the pump and valve tests cannot be judged.

Secondary air readiness stays incomplete
possible_causes: Signal wire shorted to reference or supply voltage (likelihood: high)
Open ground circuit of the bank 2 sensor (likelihood: medium)
Bank 2 pressure sensor failed internally (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P243A - Particulate Filter Restriction - Ash Accumulation (Bank 2)
problem_description: P243A is the bank 2 counterpart of P242F: the ash load in the second particulate filter has grown so large that the filter chokes the exhaust and must be cleaned or replaced. A bank 2 filter only exists where each cylinder bank of a V engine feeds its own filter strand. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Bank 1 monitoring shows how such a check works: GM's 2018 diesels judge ash by a filtered flow resistance derived from differential pressure and exhaust flow (Type A), and Deutz raises a warning once a modelled ash load limit is passed. Since ash does not burn, extra regenerations will not help and only waste fuel. If only one strand shows high back pressure or regenerates more often, the problem is confined to that side.

Reduced power at high load

title: DTC P243B - Particulate Filter Restriction - Forced Limited Power (Bank 2)
problem_description: P243B means the second particulate filter is so restricted that the engine controller cuts power to protect engine and filter. Ford documents the code in its 2024–2025 OBD summary for gasoline engines, as part of the petrol particulate filter monitor next to P246C for bank 1. Once the filter has been above 250 °C for 30 s and exhaust flow lies between 400 and 850 m³/h, a normalised back pressure above 1.0 for 5 s sets the fault. That makes it one of the few bank 2 filter codes with public thresholds, and it shows the code is not limited to diesels. Likely causes are a filter overloaded with soot or ash, a dented pipe, or a pressure sensor or hose reading too high. Until the restriction is cleared the engine stays in reduced power. A high soot load on this bank without the power limit is P243F.

title: DTC P2440 - AIR System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1)

title: DTC P244C - Exhaust Temperature Too Low For Particulate Filter Regeneration (Bank 1)

title: DTC P2452 - Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor A Circuit
problem_description: The pressure sensor A of the particulate filter, usually a differential sensor with hoses to the filter inlet and outlet, tells the ECM how loaded the filter is. title: DTC P2453 - Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance

title: DTC P2454 - Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low

Audi (Q7 TDI 2009 to 2011) saw P2454 from moisture inside sensor G505, and Chrysler lists it on the 2.8 diesel Town and Country with a sensor and connector check. title: DTC P2455 - Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
problem_description: P2455 means the particulate filter pressure sensor signal sits above the highest plausible value, at the top of the 5 V range. Ford's 2023 diesels and the Opel/GM 2.0 CDTi in the Saab 9-5 (2010) both use 4.9 V as the limit, Ford within 2 s and Saab after 1 s; on Ford's 6.7 L the signal follows roughly 0.082 V per kPa above 0.45 V, so 4.9 V would be about 54 kPa. Typical faults are a signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or to battery voltage, or an open low-reference (ground) circuit, which Saab lists among the circuit faults for this code. A real pressure that high from a blocked filter is unusual and would normally first raise soot codes such as P2463. Chrysler lists P2455 on the 2.8 diesel Town and Country with a sensor and connector check. The ECM falls back to a modelled soot load and may limit regeneration.

DPF warning or regeneration inhibited

title: DTC P2457 - EGR Cooler A Efficiency Below Threshold
problem_description: The EGR cooler is supposed to bring recirculated exhaust close to coolant temperature; P2457 says cooler A no longer removes enough heat, as CARB requires diesel systems to detect. title: DTC P2458 - Diesel Particulate Filter Regeneration Duration
problem_description: During a regeneration the engine raises exhaust temperature, mostly by late post-injection burned in the oxidation catalyst, until the soot in the particulate filter oxidises. Otherwise the regeneration is slowed by low exhaust temperature, a weak oxidation catalyst, faulty temperature or pressure readings, or trips too short to finish. P2459 covers regenerations that happen too often.

title: DTC P2459 - Diesel Particulate Filter Regeneration Frequency

title: DTC P245C - EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Low (Bank 1)
problem_description: P245C reports that the control line of the bank 1 bypass actuator is pulled toward ground. GM documents this in its diesel tables: in 2014 the driver stage detects low voltage while it is switched off and treats it as a ground short, and in the 2017 tables the vacuum-switched bypass fails when the resistance to ground drops below 0.5 Ohm in 24 of 30 samples, rated Type B. title: DTC P245E - Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor B Circuit
problem_description: Which sensor is B depends on the maker. Ford's 2013 6.7 L Power Stroke has an exhaust pressure sensor ahead of the filter as A and a two-port differential sensor across it as B. Despite its circuit title, P245E is there an offset test during after-run, with the key off and the controller still awake: since no gas flows, the differential reading should be zero, and more than 1 kPa for one second sets the code. On Ford's 2024 gasoline particulate filters with digital SENT sensors, P245E is the general circuit fault, detected within 5 s, while lost communication with the same sensor is U0602. So a sensor that drifted, a hose still holding pressure or water inside the sensor can set it as easily as a wiring fault. Low and high signals have their own codes, P2460 and P2461, and erratic signals P2462.

title: DTC P2460 - Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
problem_description: P2460 means the analog output of pressure sensor B has fallen below the lowest voltage a working sensor can deliver. The soot estimate loses one input and regeneration planning gets less accurate. The high case is P2461, erratic signals P2462.

title: DTC P2461 - Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor B Circuit High

title: DTC P2463 - Diesel Particulate Filter Restriction - Soot Accumulation (Bank 1)
problem_description: P2463 means the soot load in the particulate filter has passed the level at which the engine still regenerates it on its own. GM's 2009 Duramax sets it at 70 g or more for 5 minutes, the 2014 Cruze 2.0 diesel at more than 32 g for 30 s, both as Type A codes; GM's 2018 diesels use the pressure-based soot model with 120 failures in 150 samples. On the Cruze the ECM then turns on the MIL, reduces engine power and blocks normal regeneration, so a dealer service regeneration is needed. GM's bulletin on the related driver messages notes that the filter cleans itself about once per tank and needs driving above 50 km/h; extended idling and stop-and-go traffic keep it from finishing. The underlying cause is not always the driving: Stellantis traced P2463 with P2453 to broken differential pressure sensor wiring and PCM grounds, Mack to a failed aftertreatment fuel doser. Check those before regenerating, or the code returns.

title: DTC P249C - Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Reductant Injection Control

title: DTC P24A1 - Closed Loop Particulate Filter Regeneration Control At Limit - Temperature Too High
problem_description: Here the regeneration loop has reduced its heat input as far as possible, but the temperature ahead of the filter still runs above target. CARB requires inputs to be checked for erratic behaviour. Wiggling the harness while watching live data usually reproduces the fault.

title: DTC P24DE - Reductant Purge Control Valve B Circuit High
problem_description: With P24DE the control line of purge valve B stays at high voltage while the controller is actually pulling it to ground to switch the valve. That points to a short to the battery feed on the wire between valve and controller, or a valve coil with too little resistance, so that the driver protects itself and the valve never shifts. No manufacturer documents P24DE publicly. For valve A, GM runs the equivalent P20A3 check while the driver is switched on (6.6 L Duramax). title: DTC P2510 - ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Range/Performance

title: DTC P2517 - A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
problem_description: P2517 means the signal of refrigerant pressure sensor B has dropped below its usable floor. GM's hybrid tables, where B is the low-side sensor, compute the ratio of signal to the 5 V reference and fail it below 2 % (0.10 V): in 2019 if that holds for 1.6 s of a 2 s window, in 2016 for 16 of 20 samples, in 2011 for 40 of 50 samples taken every 100 ms; each time type B, so the lamp comes on after two drives. title: DTC P251B - PTO Enable Switch Circuit Low
problem_description: With P251B the module reads the PTO enable switch input as stuck at a low level, below what either switch position should produce. No maker publishes P251B with thresholds; the closest documented case is P251A on GM medium-duty Silverado trucks, where bulletin PIP6108 traces PTO faults back to ground points, which shows how sensitive this switch circuit is to its reference. CARB lets OBD systems suspend selected monitors while a PTO unit is active, so a false PTO state also affects readiness. Depending on how the input is wired, a low reading may mean PTO is permanently refused or permanently requested. P251A is the open circuit, P251C the high side.

title: DTC P252B - Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Range/Performance

title: DTC P252D - Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit High
problem_description: P252D means the oil quality sensor reports a voltage above its valid window. A short of the signal line to a positive conductor, a broken sensor ground or, with pull-up inputs, an interrupted signal wire can all push the value to the upper stop. title: DTC P253A - PTO Sense Circuit/Open
problem_description: The PTO sense circuit tells the powertrain modules whether the power take-off is really engaged, usually through a pressure or limit switch on the PTO unit. title: DTC P253C - PTO Sense Circuit Low

title: DTC P2542 - Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit High

title: DTC P2561 - A/C Control Module Requested MIL Illumination

The engine module stores P2561 as a pointer; the actual fault code sits in the A/C module and must be read there. GM's 2012 hybrid table 12OBDG06 illustrates this split: the ECM is the master that controls the lamp, while other controllers store their own codes. CARB's section (e)(12) explains why A/C faults can be emission-relevant at all: wherever the A/C changes fuel or spark control, its electronic parts must be monitored. title: DTC P2577 - Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold
problem_description: P2577 means the OBD system has concluded that the direct ozone reduction (DOR) catalyst - usually a radiator coated with an ozone-destroying catalyst such as BASF's PremAir - no longer converts enough ozone. title: DTC P2586 - Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit
problem_description: P2586 covers a general electrical fault at position sensor B, which reports where the second boost control actuator stands - the vane mechanism or electric wastegate of a second turbocharger on engines that regulate two of them separately. The engine computer cannot use the feedback, without the fault being pinned down as low (P2588), high (P2589) or sporadic (P2590); P2587 is a position mismatch with a working circuit. No manufacturer documents P2586 publicly. CARB requires the sensors of the boost control system to be monitored as comprehensive components. For sensor A, Kia service action SA078 on the 2011 Optima 2.0 T-GDI pairs the circuit code P2562 with an electric wastegate actuator whose rod length must be reset. Boost is usually limited.
symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Reduced power because boost is capped
No valid position value for actuator B in live data
possible_causes: Connector or terminal fault at the actuator B position sensor (likelihood: high)
Harness to actuator B damaged by exhaust heat (likelihood: medium)
Position sensor inside actuator B failed (often replaced as a unit) (likelihood: medium)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2586 (Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: turbo actuator position sensor b, sensor wiring.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-4 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Connector or terminal fault at the actuator B position sensor (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Harness to actuator B damaged by exhaust heat (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.
source: OBDex / SAE J2012 & ISO 15031-6 Open Diagnostic Standard

title: DTC P2587 - Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
problem_description: P2587 is a plausibility fault: position sensor B gives an electrically valid reading, but the reported position of the second boost actuator does not follow the command, or the value lies outside what the mechanism can physically reach. No manufacturer documents P2587 publicly, so the logic is known only from sensor A. GM's 2009 Duramax table sets P2563 when vane position misses the target by 15 % or more for 5 s once the engine has run 30 s, and VW bulletin 21-15-06 traces P2563 on 2.0 L TDI engines to kinked vacuum hoses, a leaking diaphragm or a broken adjusting stud. Sticking vanes or wastegate linkage are therefore as likely as the sensor. Circuit faults of sensor B are P2586 and P2588-P2590.
symptoms: Noticeable loss of power or overboost cut
Malfunction indicator lamp on
Commanded and actual position of actuator B diverge in live data

Kinked or leaking vacuum line or diaphragm on pneumatic actuators (likelihood: medium)
Actuator rod or adjusting stud out of adjustment or broken (likelihood: medium)
Drifting position sensor B (likelihood: low)

Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.

title: DTC P2588 - Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit Low
problem_description: P2588 is stored when the voltage from position sensor B of the second boost actuator drops below the lowest value a working sensor can deliver - most often a grounded signal line or a missing 5 V reference. No manufacturer documents P2588 publicly; the thresholds known for sensor A give the order of magnitude. Ford's 2023 diesel OBD summary flags P2564 below 0.15 V, and GM's 2009 Duramax table uses 0.277 V for 1 s once the engine has run 3 s. A shorted reference may also upset other sensors on the same supply. P2589 is the high-side fault, P2587 a position error with a usable signal, and P2564 the same low fault on sensor A. Power is normally reduced.
symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Power reduced, boost held low
Further sensor codes if a shared reference is shorted
possible_causes: Signal wire of position sensor B shorted to ground (likelihood: high)
Lost or shorted 5 V reference supply (likelihood: medium)
Failed position sensor B in actuator B (likelihood: medium)

Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: turbo actuator position sensor b, sensor wiring.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.

title: DTC P258A - Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A/Open
problem_description: P258A stands for an open or otherwise faulty control circuit A of an electric vacuum pump, which supplies the brake booster on engines that provide too little manifold vacuum, such as hybrids, downsized turbo petrol engines and diesels. Ford's 2018-2019 hybrid OBD summary assigns it to the brake system module: with the pump relay commanded off, a monitoring line voltage outside 1.3-5.0 V for 100 ms sets the code (legacy brake code C1035). Stellantis case S2209000006 explains that the PCM can log P258A after a crank longer than 2.5 s because the pump is unpowered while cranking; in that case the code may simply be cleared, but a P258B alongside points to the pump itself. P258B to P258D cover performance, low and high faults, P25EE the open fault of circuit B. Braking assist can be reduced.
symptoms: Engine or brake warning lamp on
Harder brake pedal at low speed or after several stops
Start-stop function disabled
possible_causes: False entry after a long engine crank while the pump is unpowered (likelihood: medium)
Faulty pump relay, blown fuse or poor relay contact (likelihood: high)
Open wire or loose connector between module, relay and pump (likelihood: medium)
Failed electric vacuum pump (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P258A (Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A/Open).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: vacuum pump, wiring harness.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.3-2.5 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: False entry after a long engine crank while the pump is unpowered (likelihood: medium).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Faulty pump relay, blown fuse or poor relay contact (likelihood: high).

Audi's Q3 bulletin 2072305 (2021-2024) traces P258B00 to a blown pump fuse after the ABS connector had been unplugged while the engine was running. The brake pedal may feel hard.

title: DTC P258E - PTO Enable Switch Performance
problem_description: P258E is the plausibility check of the power take-off enable switch. The line is not open or shorted – those faults are P251A to P251C – but the state of the switch does not fit the other PTO inputs, for instance an enable request without a valid arming step or contact signals that contradict each other. GM lists P258E among the PTO module codes in UI Bulletin 80C for Silverado and Sierra chassis cabs: the in-cab rocker delivers three mode signals that the module decodes so that every press is cross-checked, and an upfitter's remote enable switch only works if the arming button was pressed within five seconds before. GM warns upfitters against load-engage switches because they defeat these diagnostics. The truck still drives; the PTO refuses to engage or drops out.

Driver information message about PTO conditions
possible_causes: PTO switch contacts worn or contaminated, mode signals disagree (likelihood: high)
Upfitter wiring or load-engage switch interfering with the enable input (likelihood: medium)
Remote enable used without arming sequence or with wrong switch type (likelihood: medium)
PTO module configuration not matching the installed switches (likelihood: low)

Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: pto enable switch.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.

title: DTC P258F - Torque Management Request Output Signal
problem_description: P258F concerns the sending side of a torque management link. One controller – for example the engine module talking to a transmission or hybrid controller, or the reverse – transmits torque requests and finds that its own output is faulty, missing or not accepted by the receiver. The receiving side is better documented as P2544 and following: GM's 2020 table 20OBDG04 checks incoming torque requests from the TCM for a wrong protection value, a broken rolling counter and implausible magnitudes, Type B. No manufacturer documents P258F publicly. CARB's rule requires output components driven by a computer to be checked for correct functional response where feasible, which is the logic behind such a code. Typical causes are CAN wiring, mismatched software after programming or a faulty module. Harsh shifts or reduced power can follow.

Harsh or delayed shifts
Reduced engine power
possible_causes: CAN wiring or connector fault between the modules (likelihood: high)
Software levels of sending and receiving module do not match (likelihood: medium)
Low voltage or poor ground at one of the modules (likelihood: medium)
Sending control module internally faulty (likelihood: low)

Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: torque management output.

title: DTC P2591 - Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Left

problem_description: P2595 is logged when the signal of turbocharger speed sensor B stays below the range the engine computer accepts, as with a short to ground or a sensor whose output has collapsed. Bentley names it for the W12 in Continental GT, GTC and Flying Spur from 2018 and later also in the Bentayga, stored in engine control unit 1 or 2. Unlike the plausibility code P2594, which may first be cleared and retested, the bulletin goes straight to the replacement of the affected sensor (G688 or G689) once wiring tests for opens and shorts pass; on the Bentayga the bank 1 sensor is much harder to reach. The opposite electrical fault is P2596, sensor A reports the same condition as P2580.
symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Speed of the second turbo shown as zero or very low
Possible reduction of boost
possible_causes: Speed sensor B with collapsed output (likelihood: high)
Signal wire of sensor B shorted to ground (likelihood: medium)
Corroded or contaminated connector at sensor B (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2595 (Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit Low).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: turbo speed sensor b, sensor wiring.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 1-8 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Speed sensor B with collapsed output (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Signal wire of sensor B shorted to ground (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

No manufacturer publishes thresholds for P259C. Ford's 2023 diesel summary shows why it matters: its underboost check for turbocharger A runs only while boost feedback control is active. Typical root causes are inputs the loop needs, such as a faulty boost or position sensor, or a stored actuator fault. P259D is the turbocharger B equivalent.

title: DTC P25A3 - Engine Hood Open
problem_description: P25A3 is a state code, not a wiring fault: the hood is reported open at a moment when the control strategy expects it closed, for example while an automatic restart, a remote start or a hybrid engine pull-up is pending. No manufacturer documents P25A3 publicly. A Stellantis STAR case on hood switch 2 explains the background: the PCM reads that switch directly, cross-checks it against the latch switch state sent by the body module over CAN, and if either reads open it disables stop-start until the trip ends and blocks remote start. CARB's OBD rule cites an override of start-stop disablement as an emissions-neutral diagnostic. Circuit faults of the switch itself are P254F and P257D–P257F. A hood not fully latched or a misadjusted switch striker is the usual reason.

Auto stop-start and remote start locked out

Hood switch or striker misadjusted after body work (likelihood: medium)
Latch-integrated switch sticking in the open position (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P25B1 - Fuel Level Sensor B Stuck

problem_description: P25B3 says the wastegate of turbocharger A stays further open than the module commands, so exhaust bypasses the turbine and boost falls short. Toyota lists P25B3-72 on the 2022 Tundra V35A and released new ECM software for it on the 2023 GR Corolla. Expect lack of power.

title: DTC P25B8 - Auxiliary Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit Low

title: DTC P25B9 - Auxiliary Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit High

title: DTC P25BA - Regeneration Control Switch Circuit/Open

GM's L5P trucks with option FPF instead use the exhaust brake switch for the same job (bulletin 20-NA-203). No manufacturer documents P25BA publicly. Automatic regeneration while driving continues, but a requested parked regeneration cannot be started and soot can build up.

title: DTC P25BB - Regeneration Control Switch Circuit Low
problem_description: P25BB reports that the regeneration switch input reads a low level the switch itself cannot produce. title: DTC P25BC - Regeneration Control Switch Circuit High
problem_description: P25BC is the high-voltage counterpart: the regeneration switch line carries a level near supply voltage that no switch position can produce. title: DTC P25BD - Unmetered Fuel - Forced Engine Shutdown
problem_description: P25BD protects against engine runaway, where the engine keeps speeding up although the controller injects no fuel, for instance because oil from a failed turbocharger seal or combustible vapour drawn into the intake is being burned. GM documents the monitor in its diesel ECM tables. In 14OBDG04 the speed must pass 5,400 rpm for 0.01 s, after which the controller cuts the air supply with its intake air valve and disables the injectors; 18OBDG04 uses 5,500 rpm for 0.5 s and 20OBDG04 5,200 rpm for 0.1 s, both enabled above 1,500 rpm. Each table rates it Type A, so the MIL comes on in the first trip. Unlike P0219, which merely records an overspeed, P25BD means the engine was forcibly stopped. Before a restart, turbo, crankcase ventilation and intake tract should be checked for oil.

title: DTC P25C1 - Alternative Fuel Disable Signal Circuit
problem_description: P25C1 relates to the incoming side of the alternative fuel disable function: a signal line on which the engine controller reads whether gas operation is blocked, either as feedback from the gas system or as a request from it, for example when a CNG or LPG controller detects low tank pressure or its own fault. The code says the signal is missing or unusable without naming a direction. In GM's bi-fuel Silverado and Sierra the system changes back to gasoline by itself when the gas tank runs empty and stops toggling after 20 transitions in one key cycle, which shows how much the engine controller depends on knowing the gas system's state. No manufacturer documents P25C1 publicly. P25C2 and P25C3 are the high and low variants; P25BE to P25C0 cover the control output.

Fuel mode indicator flashes
Check engine lamp

title: DTC P25EE - Vacuum Pump Control Circuit B/Open
problem_description: P25EE covers the second control circuit of an electric brake vacuum pump, the part of the wiring that should carry voltage while the pump is switched on. title: DTC P25FD - Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve C Temperature Too High
problem_description: This code says bypass valve C has become too hot. Recirculation valves are placed in the charge air path close to the compressor and thus near the hot turbine side, and an electric valve's coil adds its own heat when energised for long periods. title: DTC P260C - PTO Control Circuit High
problem_description: P260C signals that the PTO control output reads too high, usually because the relay control line touches a powered wire or the relay coil draws too much current. GM lists it as P260C.00, a high voltage on the PTO relay control line, in the diagnostic table of the PTO module that GM fitted to Silverado and Sierra 3500 HD chassis cab trucks from 2008 to 2014. Since that module switches the relay on both its feed and its ground side, a short to voltage can leave the relay pulled in when it should have dropped out. Body builders splice into this circuit, so their added wiring is the likely suspect. CARB lets the OBD system pause selected monitors while a PTO runs, so a wrong PTO state matters beyond the work equipment. P260B is the low-side code, P260A the open circuit.
symptoms: PTO will not engage or will not release
PTO indicator behaves abnormally
possible_causes: Relay control wire shorted to a powered circuit (likelihood: high)
Relay or solenoid coil with too low resistance (likelihood: medium)
Faulty splice or add-on wiring from the body installation (likelihood: medium)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P260C (PTO Control Circuit High).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: pto engagement solenoid, pto relay, wiring harness.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.5-2.5 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Relay control wire shorted to a powered circuit (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Relay or solenoid coil with too low resistance (likelihood: medium).
Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.
source: OBDex / SAE J2012 & ISO 15031-6 Open Diagnostic Standard

title: DTC P260D - PTO Engaged Lamp Control Circuit
problem_description: P260D concerns the output that drives the lamp or LED telling the operator that the power take-off is engaged; the module has found a fault in that lamp circuit. For GM's heavy-duty pickup chassis cabs, upfitter bulletin UI 80c explains how such an indicator behaves: the LED in the PTO switch blinks quickly while the relay is energized, turns steady once load feedback confirms engagement or after 3 s without feedback, and blinks slowly when a memory speed is stored. A remote PTO indicator can be wired as well. GM's PTO code table does not list P260D, and no other maker documents it publicly. The PTO itself may work normally, but the operator loses the visual confirmation, which matters for safe work with tippers, cranes or pumps. P260A to P260C cover the control circuit itself.
symptoms: PTO indicator stays dark or lit regardless of PTO state
PTO itself works normally
possible_causes: Failed indicator lamp or LED (likelihood: high)
Open or shorted wire to the indicator, often in add-on wiring (likelihood: medium)
Fault in the PTO switch assembly with integrated LED (likelihood: low)

Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: pto indicator lamp, instrument cluster, wiring harness.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.3-1.5 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Failed indicator lamp or LED (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Open or shorted wire to the indicator, often in add-on wiring (likelihood: medium).
Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.

title: DTC P260E - Particulate Filter Regeneration Lamp Control Circuit
problem_description: Diesel machines often have a separate dashboard lamp that tells the operator a particulate filter regeneration is needed or running. P260E covers the circuit that switches this lamp. Deutz documents it for its EMR5/MD1 engine controllers: fault type 11 (J1939 SPN 3697, FMI 4) means the lamp output reads below normal or is shorted to ground, type 12 (FMI 3) means it is too high or shorted to the supply. Deutz engines go into tractors, construction and other off-road equipment, so the code is mostly met there. For on-road heavy-duty engines CARB section 1971.1 requires electrical checks of such output components. A failed lamp output does not affect the filter itself, but the operator may miss a request for a parked regeneration, letting soot load build up until power is reduced.

Missed regeneration requests leading to high soot load
Later power reduction by the engine controller

Lamp or bulb holder open, or lamp not fitted on this machine (likelihood: medium)
Corroded connector at dashboard or engine controller (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P260F - EVAP System Monitoring Processor Performance
problem_description: Some evaporative leak tests run long after the engine is switched off, so Ford gives them a small dedicated processor that works during the soak. P260F is set when that monitoring processor does not behave as intended. In Ford's 2020–2023 gasoline OBD summary it belongs to the engine-off natural vacuum (EONV) test for 0.020 inch leaks, which may run at most twice a day after the vehicle has soaked for 3.5–6 hours; the processor check itself is continuous and takes about 5 seconds. Ford marks the code with a MIL in its 2014 list. Because the module also relies on CAN communication, tank pressure sensing and the vent solenoid, wiring or supply faults can trigger it as well as an internal fault. Without a working processor the small leak test (P0456) cannot complete, so readiness may stay incomplete.

EVAP readiness not set, small leak test not completed
possible_causes: Internal fault in the EVAP monitoring processor or module (likelihood: high)
Supply, ground or CAN wiring fault at the monitoring module (likelihood: medium)
Software level requiring an update (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2610 - ECM/PCM Internal Engine Off Timer Performance
problem_description: Several emission monitors need to know how long the engine was off, for example to judge a cold start or an evaporative test after a soak. P2610 reports that the module's engine-off timer gives implausible values. Ford's 2020–2023 gasoline summary flags an engine-off time under 30 s after an inferred soak, an error above 15 s or a missing CAN timer message at start; its 2023 diesel compares 30 degrees of coolant cooling with at least 1200 s counted and checks an 8 s afterrun window (7.52–8.48 s). GM's 2013 tables test the initial value (below 0 or above 10 s) and tick spacing (0.8–1.2 s), Type B. Toyota and Lexus fixed false sets on 2014–2018 models by ECM reprogramming (T-SB-0146-16, T-SB-0336-17); Mazda keeps the timer in the cluster and logs P2610 with P2507 after short restarts in transport mode.

title: DTC P2611 - A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit/Open
problem_description: A refrigerant distribution valve is an electrically switched valve in the A/C circuit that opens or blocks the refrigerant path to one branch, for example a rear evaporator or a battery chiller. P2611 tells you the engine or powertrain module can no longer drive valve A because its control line or coil is open. Ford's 2014 PCM code list for spark-ignition engines includes P2611, testable with key on, engine running and in continuous mode, but without a MIL mark. Audi uses the same valve naming in its thermal management module (valve B, P0EE2, A7 plug-in hybrid). P2612 and P2613 are the low and high faults of the same circuit. Typically the affected A/C branch stays shut or open, so cooling in one zone or of the battery suffers; engine operation is not affected.
symptoms: One A/C zone (e.g. rear) blows warm or cannot be shut off
Reduced battery cooling on hybrids or EVs, possibly limited charging power
Stored code, often without warning lamp
possible_causes: Valve solenoid coil burnt out or internally open (likelihood: high)
Corroded or loose connector at the valve, often near condensation (likelihood: medium)
Broken control wire between module and valve (likelihood: medium)
Faulty output stage in the controlling module (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2612 - A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit Low
problem_description: P2612 is stored when the voltage on the drive line of refrigerant distribution valve A stays lower than the module expects, which normally points to a ground fault in the wire or inside the valve. title: DTC P2613 - A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit High
problem_description: P2613 means the control circuit of refrigerant distribution valve A reads too high: the wire has a short to the supply side, or the driver stage senses excessive current when it switches the valve. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Ford lists only the open-circuit code P2611, and the VW use of P2612 refers to the compressor regulator valve. Valves of this kind are simple solenoid shut-off valves, as suppliers such as Egelhof build them for systems that must close off one evaporator or the chiller completely. With the circuit shorted high the valve may stay energised, so refrigerant keeps flowing into a branch that should be idle, or the module switches the output off for protection. P2611 and P2612 cover the open and low faults.

Valve output switched off, so the branch does not work at all
Code stored without engine symptoms
possible_causes: Control wire shorted to a battery-voltage feed (likelihood: high)
Valve coil with shorted windings drawing too much current (likelihood: medium)
Defective driver in the controlling module (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2614 - Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit/Open (Bank 1)
problem_description: Some engine computers pass a copy of the camshaft position signal on to another module, for example an injector driver unit or a valve timing controller. P2614 means that this outgoing line for camshaft A on bank 1 is broken or its pulses never reach the receiver. On the 2003 Ford 6.0 L Power Stroke diesel the PCM forwards the CMP pulse to the fuel injector control module (FICM); a counter in the FICM rises when that pulse is missing or out of step with the crank signal, checked above 90 rpm with 5 errors while cranking or 10 while running, and Ford lists the code with MIL. Mitsubishi names P2614 to P2616 for the 2022 Outlander, whose ECM feeds an electric intake valve timing module. P2615 and P2616 cover the shorted cases. Expect hard starting, stalling or a no-start.

Long cranking or no-start
Engine stalls or misfires intermittently

Receiving module (e.g. injector control module) not reading the signal (likelihood: low)
Defective output stage in the engine control module (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2615 - Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit Low (Bank 1)
problem_description: P2615 points to a camshaft A (bank 1) position output line that the engine module finds pulled to ground. GM documents it for the Cadillac CT6 in its 2018 tables: with the driver switched off and the line commanded high, the ECM measures the voltage and flags a short at an impedance to ground of 0.5 ohm or less; at 200 kilohm or more it treats the circuit as open, and some controllers then log P2614 instead. It takes 40 failing samples out of 50, read every 100 ms outside cranking and relay voltage is at least 11 V, and GM classes the code Type C without MIL. Mitsubishi lists it for the 2022 Outlander's valve timing module feed. The receiving module may lose cam phase information, so rough starts or a fallback timing strategy are possible.

Rough or delayed starting
Valve timing control in fallback mode

Internally shorted input in the receiving module (likelihood: low)
Faulty output driver in the engine control module (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2616 - Camshaft A Position Signal Output Circuit High (Bank 1)
problem_description: P2616 is the opposite fault to P2615: the outgoing camshaft A position line on bank 1 stays at supply potential although the module has switched its low-side driver on and wants the line low. A chafed wire touching a battery feed or a failed output stage are the usual suspects. Mitsubishi also lists P2616 for the 2022 Outlander. The downstream controller sees a steady level instead of pulses, which can upset cam phasing or starting.

title: DTC P2619 - Crankshaft Position Signal Output Circuit High
problem_description: P2619 is set when the crankshaft position output line is held at supply voltage while the module's low-side driver is switched on and expects it to be pulled down. GM also carries the code in its 2011, 2012, 2016 and 2023 tables, and Mitsubishi lists it for the 2022 Outlander. The usual cause is insulation damage that lets the line touch a positive feed, less often a defective output stage in the module. The listening controller then receives a constant level rather than teeth and may limit operation.

title: DTC P261A - Coolant Pump B Control Circuit/Open
problem_description: P261A reports an open circuit in the drive of an auxiliary electric coolant pump labelled B. Ford's gasoline OBD summaries for 2020-2023 and 2024 define pump B as the high-temperature loop pump for component cooling and check it continuously over 5 s with at least 11 V on board. Ford's EcoSport 1.0 EcoBoost of 2018 (SSM 47359) set P261A because connector C1450 at that pump could not latch fully; a pigtail kit cures it. Audi bulletin 2043142 for 2012-2016 2.0 TFSI engines (CAE, CPM) links P261A to P261C to a failing after-run circulation pump and fits an updated pump. VW's 2014 Touareg book flags it at 4.8-5.3 V on the line. P261C/P261D are the shorts, P261B the performance fault.

Auxiliary pump with internal open (electronics or motor) (likelihood: medium)
Broken supply or control wire, or failed relay where fitted (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P262A - Fuel Injector - Pilot Injection Not Learned
problem_description: Common-rail diesels learn how long each injector must be energised to deliver its tiny pilot shot. Ford's 6.7 L Power Stroke does this with Zero Fuel Calibration: during overrun with rail pressure set to 300 bar, one injector fires small test pulses and the resulting rise in crankshaft speed tells the module the real quantity; the learned offset then corrects every pilot injection of that injector. P262A means the routine kept failing to learn. The 2013 Ford summary sets it after 100 s of valid conditions without a learned value (890-1,610 rpm, gears 4-6, converter locked, coolant at least 50 °C); the 2017 edition counts 30 attempts of 0.8 s or more. P02CC-P02DB cover offsets at their limits. CARB requires faults in pilot-quantity feedback control to be detected.

Louder combustion knock, especially at idle and light load
Often no noticeable change in driveability

Non-original engine calibration interfering with the learning routine (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P262B - Control Module Power Off Timer Performance

title: DTC P262D - Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit Low

title: DTC P262E - Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit High
problem_description: With P262E the 5 V supply G that the engine module feeds to a sensor group sits above its upper limit. title: DTC P262F - Sensor Reference Voltage G Circuit Range/Performance

title: DTC P2637 - Torque Management Feedback Signal A
problem_description: Many automatic transmissions ask the engine to cut torque briefly during an upshift and then check whether the engine actually did so. P2637 is stored by the transmission controller when that feedback for request A shows the engine did not follow. Allison names it Shift Energy Management (SEM) on its 3000/4000 series: behind Cummins L9 and X15 engines (EPA17 version) the engine failed to track the torque request closely enough, the CHECK TRANS lamp came on and Cummins fixed it with an ECM recalibration (TSB210020), with no change to Allison hardware or software. Cummins found the same on B6.7 engines in 2017 (J1939 SPN 513, FMI 7), and Navistar linked P2637 to Allison 1000/2000 calibrations causing quick, harsh upshifts. P2641 covers request B. Expect firm shifts or limited gears.

Harsh or too quick upshifts
Gear range limited

title: DTC P263C - Glow Plug Control Driver Performance

title: DTC P263D - Reductant Heater Driver Performance
problem_description: DEF turns solid at about -11 °C, so SCR systems heat the tank, pump and lines electrically. P263D concerns the power stage that switches these heaters rather than a heater element. On Ford's 6.7 L Power Stroke the heaters are switched by the glow plug module; the plausibility test runs once per trip at peak heater power and sets P263D when the driver circuits exceed 125 °C. Deutz uses P263D-00 differently on its EMR engine controllers, namely when defrosting the AdBlue system fails. If the fluid cannot thaw, dosing starts late or not at all, NOx rises and the SCR warning sequence toward a speed or power limit can begin.

title: DTC P2665 - Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit/Open
problem_description: Engines that can burn a second fuel such as compressed natural gas use electric shut-off valves to keep that fuel locked in when it is not wanted. GM's 2015 Impala Bi-Fuel has two of them, both normally closed: a high-pressure cut-off at the tank and a low-pressure cut-off at the regulator, which the ECM energises only in CNG mode while the engine cranks or runs. P2665 means the control circuit of shut-off valve B is open, so the module cannot energise that valve. Ford's 2014 spark-ignition code list includes P2665 as a continuous test without MIL. Which physical valve carries the letter B is not published by either maker. With the valve unpowered, the gaseous fuel stays shut off and the engine typically falls back to gasoline. P0005 is the same fault on valve A.
symptoms: Engine runs only on gasoline, gas mode not available
Fuel mode lamp flashes or shows an error
possible_causes: Open valve coil (likelihood: high)
Loose or corroded connector at the valve (often exposed under the vehicle) (likelihood: medium)
Broken wire in the control circuit (likelihood: medium)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2665 (Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit/Open).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: fuel shutoff valve b, solenoid, wiring harness.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-2.5 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Open valve coil (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Loose or corroded connector at the valve (often exposed under the vehicle) (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.
source: OBDex / SAE J2012 & ISO 15031-6 Open Diagnostic Standard

title: DTC P2666 - Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit Low
problem_description: P2666 is stored when the control line of fuel shut-off valve B sits at too low a voltage, the typical sign of a short to ground between module and valve or inside the coil. Depending on how the driver is built, the valve may then open whenever the ignition is on, or the module switches the output off for protection. No manufacturer documents P2666 publicly. In bi-fuel vehicles such as GM's CNG Impala, the ECM controls normally closed cut-off valves on the gas side and changes over to gasoline as soon as it detects a problem in one fuel system; GM's Silverado and Sierra CNG models signal such errors with a rapidly flashing fuel indicator. P2665 is the open circuit and P2667 the short to voltage on the same valve, P0006 the low fault of valve A.

title: DTC P2667 - Fuel Shutoff Valve B Control Circuit High
problem_description: With P2667 the module measures excess voltage on the wire that drives shut-off valve B, usually because the wire touches a supply circuit. Safety matters here: on a low-side driven valve a short to voltage can keep the coil energised even when the module wants the valve closed, so the gaseous fuel may not be shut off reliably. No manufacturer explains P2667 publicly. GM's bi-fuel Impala relies on two normally closed cut-off valves that the ECM opens only while the engine runs on CNG, and falls back to gasoline whenever either fuel system reports a problem; Ford lists the open-circuit sibling P2665. P2665 and P2666 cover the open and grounded circuit, P0007 the high fault on valve A. Have it checked promptly and use the manual tank valve if gas can be smelled.

title: DTC P2668 - Fuel Mode Indicator Lamp Control Circuit
problem_description: Bi-fuel vehicles tell the driver which fuel is in use through a small indicator, often built into the fuel selector button. P2668 indicates that the module driving this lamp has found a fault in its control circuit, such as an open wire or a failed bulb or LED. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. Fuel switching itself is unaffected, but the driver loses the fuel mode display and the error warning. P26E2 and P26E3 are the low and high variants.

title: DTC P2669 - Actuator Supply Voltage B Circuit/Open
problem_description: Many transmission controllers feed their solenoids through internal high-side switches, called actuator supply A and B. Ford's 6R140 splits its Transmission Solenoid Power Control into two wires: TSPC-A powers shift solenoids A, C and E (fault P0657), TSPC-B powers SSB, SSD, TCC and line pressure control (P2669). Because both share one internal switch, any fault switches off all seven solenoids, leaving park, reverse, neutral and 5th gear with full line pressure; Ford lists P2669 with MIL. In GM's 16OBDG08 tables for Silverado/Sierra the TCM flags an open supply 2 when several solenoids on it read open at once while the supply line stays high; GM's 2023 TCM test checks at power-down and logs it as Type A. P2670 and P2671 cover low and high faults.

Harsh engagements due to maximum line pressure
MIL or transmission warning on

Damaged internal transmission harness or lead frame (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P266A - "A" Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit (Bank 2)
problem_description: P266A is the basic circuit fault for the bank 2 position sensor of rocker arm actuator A. It only applies to engines that have a lift actuator with position feedback on each cylinder bank, which is rare; most switching rocker systems on V engines rely on oil pressure switches or none at all. No manufacturer documents P266A publicly, and even Toyota's Valvematic, which does use such feedback, is an inline design whose bulletins list a B code for its sensor. CARB still requires every electrical component of a lift system to be checked. If the controller loses this signal, it typically stops varying lift on bank 2, so power and refinement suffer.

title: DTC P266C - "A" Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 2)

title: DTC P266D - "A" Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High (Bank 2)
problem_description: P266D is logged when the bank 2 position feedback of rocker arm actuator A climbs above its upper limit. Typical reasons are an interrupted sensor ground, a signal wire chafed through onto a supply line, or corrosion that raises resistance. title: DTC P266F - A/C Refrigerant Distribution Valve A Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
problem_description: Refrigerant distribution valve A is a solenoid that opens or closes one branch of the A/C circuit, for instance a rear evaporator or a battery chiller. Its driver stage in the control module protects itself: when the output current rises above its limit or the chip overheats, it switches off and reports P266F. That usually means the load draws too much, through a shorted coil, a short in the harness or a valve that is mechanically stuck. No manufacturer documents P266F publicly; Ford lists only the open-circuit code P2611 for the same valve, and suppliers such as Egelhof build these shut-off valves as simple on/off solenoids. Unlike P2611 to P2613, which flag open and shorted wiring, P266F concerns the protection of the driver itself. The affected branch then stays closed.

title: DTC P2670 - Actuator Supply Voltage B Circuit Low
problem_description: P2670 is set when the second high-side actuator supply delivers too little voltage while it is switched on, which nearly always means a short to ground somewhere on the supply line or in a load connected to it. GM documents it in several controllers. In the 16OBDG08 TCM tables for Silverado and Sierra a ground short is recognised at an impedance of 0.43 ohm or less, confirmed after three events, Type A. GM's 2023 TCM compares the supply voltage with battery voltage and also watches the average current, 60 ms to fail, Type A. In GM's hybrid tables (Volt THPC in 16OBDG01, HPC1 in 19OBDG01) high side driver 2 reports the short within about 0.13 s, again Type A after one trip. Solenoids on that supply drop out, so the transmission enters a failsafe mode.

title: DTC P2671 - Actuator Supply Voltage B Circuit High
problem_description: P2671 points to voltage on the second actuator supply when the controller has switched it off, so the line is fed from outside or the switch inside the module no longer opens. title: DTC P2672 - Injection Pump Timing Offset
problem_description: On diesels with an electronically controlled rotary or distributor pump, the controller needs to know how far the pump's actual delivery start sits from its nominal position relative to the crankshaft. Dodge listed P2672 among the codes activated by the engine-controller update in emissions recall T21 for the 2004–2006 Sprinter; no public maker text gives a threshold. P2673 instead means the timing value was never learned. A driver may notice hard starting, knocking, smoke or reduced power.

title: DTC P2673 - Injection Pump Timing Calibration Not Learned
problem_description: This code says the engine controller holds no valid learned value for the start of delivery of its injection pump. Such a value is usually taught after the pump or the controller is replaced, or after a software reflash, and lets the controller correct the pump's individual timing tolerance. The same Dodge campaign (T21, new engine software for 2004–2006 Sprinter vans) also lists P2673 beside P2672; no public maker document explains its logic. CARB asks for tolerance compensation to be monitored on parts that are matched to the controller. Unlike P2672 the timing itself need not be wrong; the learning step is simply missing. A relearn with a scan tool is the usual cure.

title: DTC P2674 - Injection Pump Fuel Calibration Not Learned
problem_description: Electronically governed diesel injection pumps meter the quantity per stroke themselves, and each unit differs slightly in how much it delivers for a given command. P2674 reports that the quantity correction for the installed pump has not been learned or stored in the controller. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; P2672 and P2673 cover the timing side of the same pump. CARB requires 2015-on vehicles whose fuel pumps or injectors carry production tolerance compensation, such as coded parts or trim resistors, to verify that the right compensation is in use. Without it, fuelling can drift, giving smoke, uneven idle or a shortfall of power until the learn routine is run.

Smoke or uneven idle
Reduced power
possible_causes: Quantity learn not run after pump or controller replacement (likelihood: high)
Pump calibration data missing, wrong or not matching the installed pump (likelihood: medium)
Fuel metering actuator fault preventing the learn from completing (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2684 - Actuator Supply Voltage C Circuit/Open
problem_description: Some transmission controllers power groups of solenoids through several internal high-side outputs; supply C is the third of these rails, after A (P0657) and B (P2669). P2684 reports an open load on it. GM's 2023 and 2024 TCM tables tie the code to high-side output 7 and test it while the module powers down: with the output off and a low-side driver on, the load should drag the line low, so a level above 40 % of battery voltage is remembered as an open load and reported after the next start, Type A. Ford's 2024 summary assigns P2684 to high side driver 7 of the TR9070 dual-clutch gearbox, and Ford's 2014 Boss 302S code list carries it as well. Whatever hangs on that rail stops working, so a default gear or limp mode is likely.
symptoms: Transmission in default gear or limp mode
MIL on after restart
Several solenoid circuit codes stored together
possible_causes: Broken wire or loose terminal between the module output and the supplied solenoids (likelihood: high)
Corroded or unseated transmission connector or internal lead frame (likelihood: medium)
High-side output inside the controller defective (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2684 (Actuator Supply Voltage C Circuit/Open).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: actuator supply c, control module, wiring harness.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 1-5 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Broken wire or loose terminal between the module output and the supplied solenoids (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Corroded or unseated transmission connector or internal lead frame (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.
source: OBDex / SAE J2012 & ISO 15031-6 Open Diagnostic Standard
