title: DTC P2685 - Actuator Supply Voltage C Circuit Low
problem_description: P2685 means the third actuator supply rail sags while it is switched on, almost always because the line or one of the loads it feeds has a path to ground. Unlike the open and switch faults of this rail, GM's 2023 and 2024 TCM tables check this one continuously during operation: if the voltage at high-side output 7 falls below a share of the supply, or the averaged output current runs too high, a timer counts up and the fault is confirmed after 60 ms. Battery voltage must lie between 8.75 and 18 V, the engine must not be cranking, and the test is suspended when P0882 or P0883 is present; GM rates it Type A. Ford's 2024 summary lists P2685 as the shorted-load fault of high side driver 7 in the TR9070 dual-clutch unit. The protected output switches off and the transmission falls back to a failsafe mode.
symptoms: MIL on during the same trip
Failsafe gear, no normal shifting
Blown fuse possible on the transmission supply
possible_causes: Supply wire chafed through and touching ground (likelihood: high)
Shorted solenoid coil on this rail drawing excess current (likelihood: medium)
Weak battery or charging fault pulling the whole supply down (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2685 (Actuator Supply Voltage C Circuit Low).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: actuator supply c, charging system.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 1-5 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Supply wire chafed through and touching ground (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Shorted solenoid coil on this rail drawing excess current (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

title: DTC P2686 - Actuator Supply Voltage C Circuit High
problem_description: The high case of supply C concerns voltage that should not be there: the rail stays live although the controller has turned it off. Causes are an internal high-side switch that no longer opens or an outside wire touching battery positive. GM's 2023 and 2024 TCM tables run this check during shutdown. With output 7 disabled, a reading above 70 % of battery voltage counts as a shorted switch; the module keeps that finding in permanent memory and reports it once restarted. Battery voltage must stay within 1.5 V during the test, and GM files it as Type B: two failing trips before the lamp lights. Ford lists P2686 as the shorted-switch fault of high side driver 7 in its 2024 TR9070 table and also in the Boss 302S code list. The solenoids can no longer be switched off safely, so a limp mode is likely.
symptoms: MIL after a second trip with the fault
Limp mode or fixed gear after restart
Code returns after clearing once the key has been off
possible_causes: Internal high-side switch of the controller stuck conducting (likelihood: high)
Supply wire shorted to a battery-fed circuit in the harness (likelihood: medium)
Moisture in the transmission connector creating a leakage path (likelihood: low)

Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: actuator supply c, charging system.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 1-5 hours

title: DTC P2687 - Fuel Supply Heater Control Circuit/Open
problem_description: Diesel engines warm the fuel at the filter so that wax crystals do not block it in frost. P2687 says the control line of that heater is open. In GM's diesel ECM tables the engine computer switches the heater relay with a low-side driver and judges the off-state voltage; more than 200 kOhm between pin and ground means open. The 2014 version (14OBDG04) needed 11 V for 3 s and 2 s of fault, Type B with MIL; the 2017 and 2020 versions use 10 bad readings out of 20 at 100 ms and rate it Type C without lamp. Ford used the same code differently: its 2015 and 2016 diesel summaries apply P2687 to the vaporizer glow plug of the 3.2 L Transit's downstream injection, open if the line sits at 2.9 to 3.2 V for 5 s; from 2017 that fault moved to P269B.
symptoms: Hard starting or stalling in severe cold
Power loss from a waxed fuel filter
Often no warning lamp, depending on model year
possible_causes: Heater relay coil open or relay not seated (likelihood: high)
Broken control wire or corroded terminal at the filter housing (likelihood: medium)
Heater element open where it is switched directly without a relay (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2687 (Fuel Supply Heater Control Circuit/Open).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: fuel supply heater, heater relay, wiring harness.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.5-2 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Heater relay coil open or relay not seated (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Broken control wire or corroded terminal at the filter housing (likelihood: medium).

title: DTC P2688 - Fuel Supply Heater Control Circuit Low
problem_description: With P2688 the heater control line reads too low while the driver is off, which points to a grounded wire: the relay would then be energized all the time, and the filter heater runs even in summer and drains the battery after shutdown. GM's 2020 diesel table requires 0.5 ohm or less to ground and counts 10 failures in 20 samples taken every 100 ms; the code is Type C but, unlike its siblings, triggers a service-vehicle-soon message after one trip (the 2018 table matches). In 2014 GM still rated the same fault Type B with MIL. On the 2015 and 2016 Ford 3.2 L Transit diesel the code belonged to the vaporizer glow plug of the exhaust fuel system and was set after 5 s inside a 1.95–2.175 V window; later model years report that as P269D.

title: DTC P2689 - Fuel Supply Heater Control Circuit High
problem_description: P2689 is logged when the fuel heater control line stays high even though the controller has commanded it on, so the relay coil is fed from battery positive and cannot be pulled in; the heater never works. Ford's 2015 and 2016 diesel summaries give the code two jobs on the 3.2 L Transit: a vaporizer glow plug line held in the 10.9–12.32 V band for 5 s, and a relay status that contradicts the request for about 60 s, marked as provisional. In 2017 Ford split those into P269E and P26A0. Cold-weather starting is the main thing at risk.

title: DTC P268A - Fuel Injector Calibration Not Learned/Programmed
problem_description: P268A covers injector correction that relies on a learn routine rather than a printed code. GM's diesel tables 17OBDG04 to 19OBDG04A set it, Type A in one trip, when the small quantity learning (SQL) routine was not completed and stored before the vehicle left the assembly line. VW's 2014 Touareg 3.0 TDI (CNRB) lists it for a rail pressure deviation above 1,500–2,000 kPa lasting over 40 s. Audi's 2026 service note 2082225/1 reports it with the MIL on 2025–2026 A5 and Q5 2.0 TFSI petrol engines as a software issue. Deutz MD1 links it to a calibration fault of injector 1. Per-injector code faults use P268C–P2696. Symptoms range from none to rough idle and knock.

title: DTC P268B - High Pressure Fuel Pump Calibration Not Learned/Programmed
problem_description: Common rail and direct-injection petrol systems use a high pressure pump whose delivery is trimmed by a metering or volume control valve. Where the pump comes with individual correction data, or the controller has to learn its behaviour, P268B reports that this data is missing or was never taught. No manufacturer documents P268B publicly; GM's diesel tables, which carry P268A and the per-cylinder injector codes, do not list it. CARB names pumps corrected by in-line resistors as an example of parts whose compensation must be checked from 2015 on. Rail pressure control may then work with a generic pump model, so pressure faults such as P0087 or P0088 and weak starting can follow.

Long cranking or hard start
Reduced power with rail pressure deviations

title: DTC P268C - Cylinder 1 Injector Data Incompatible
problem_description: Every modern diesel injector carries a correction code from the factory flow test, and the controller must hold the code of the injector in cylinder 1. P268C sets when that code is missing, outside its range or fails the checksum. GM's 2014 four-cylinder diesel table (14OBDG04) checks the injector quantity adjustment (IQA) checksum once per drive cycle before driving, Type B. Later GM V8, six- and four-cylinder diesel tables rate it Type A, set if the code at DID $60 was never written. Ford's 2023 diesel summary (6.7 L and 3.0 L) runs the check continuously within about 0.5 s. Cylinder 1 exists on every engine, so this is the most widely used code of the series.

title: DTC P268D - Cylinder 2 Injector Data Incompatible
problem_description: P268D concerns the stored flow correction for the injector in cylinder 2. In GM's 2016 four-cylinder diesel table (16OBDG04) the test runs with ignition on and passes once the end-of-line injector adjustment (EIA) value has been written via DID $61; a missing value only counts as a failure when the manufacturer enable counter is zero, i.e. on a finished production controller. The code is Type A there and in GM's 2020 V8 diesel table. Where cylinder 2 physically sits depends on the maker's numbering. Ford's 2023 diesel summary also uses P268D. CARB wants the stored code to point to the injector with the wrong compensation, hence one code per cylinder.

title: DTC P268E - Cylinder 3 Injector Data Incompatible
problem_description: For cylinder 3 the controller compares the injector's correction value with what its software accepts. Ford's 2023 diesel OBD summary explains the idea well: each injector's code, kept in EEPROM, describes how far that unit departs from an idealised mean part, and a DTC is logged if the value is absent, out of range or its checksum is wrong. The monitor runs continuously and needs about half a second. GM's 2019 V8 diesel table 19OBDG04A rates P268E Type A, so the lamp lights in the first trip. Because only the data is checked, the injector itself may be perfect; the usual fix is to read the code off the injector head and program it into the controller.

title: DTC P2693 - Cylinder 8 Injector Data Incompatible
problem_description: P2693 completes the series on V8 engines and covers the injector in cylinder 8. It is set when the controller finds no valid flow correction code for that position. In GM's 2018 table 18OBDG04 the code reads DID $67 and fails only once the manufacturer enable counter is zero; the 2025 table 25OBDG04A instead keeps the check permanently on in production units. Both rate it Type A. Ford's 2023 diesel summary covers it for the 6.7 L Power Stroke with a continuous check of about 0.5 s. When all eight codes appear together, a new or reset controller is far more likely than eight bad injectors; a lone P2693 points to work on that one injector.

title: DTC P2697 - Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Circuit/Open

title: DTC P269B - Exhaust Aftertreatment Glow Plug Control Circuit/Open

title: DTC P26A3 - Engine Coolant Bypass Valve A Range/Performance
problem_description: P26A3 is a functional fault: the electrics of bypass valve A look fine, but the valve does not reach or report the position it should. title: DTC P26E1 - Sensor Power Supply D Circuit High
problem_description: With P26E1 the fourth sensor supply of the control module reads higher than its regulated value. title: DTC P26EA - Fuel Pump Control Module B

title: DTC P26FF - Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present (Bank 2)

title: DTC P270B - Transmission Friction Element B Temperature Too High
problem_description: P270B concerns the shift element lettered B. A multi-plate clutch has no sensor of its own, so the controller usually derives its heat from the energy turned into warmth while the plates slip and from the oil temperature, then compares the result with a limit. No maker publishes P270B with thresholds, and the letter mapping differs from gearbox to gearbox. title: DTC P270D - Transmission Friction Element D Temperature Too High
problem_description: P270D is stored when the thermal state of shift element D rises above the controller's limit. The heat comes from friction during slip, so anything that lengthens slip on D counts: a sluggish apply, leaking seals in its hydraulic circuit, or hard use with a heavy load. CARB treats transmission controls as monitored powertrain components. For the driver the code mostly means a protective torque or gear limit; it does not by itself prove mechanical damage, but it should be investigated if it returns.

title: DTC P2712 - Hydraulic Power Unit Leakage
problem_description: P2712 targets gearboxes whose clutches or shift forks are worked by a separate hydraulic power unit, typically an electric pump that charges a pressure accumulator. Such a system loses pressure only slowly when sealed; if pressure drops faster than expected or the pump has to recharge too often, the controller concludes there is a leak. No manufacturer documents P2712 publicly. The principle is described in Volkswagen's training booklet for the dry seven-speed DSG 0AM: an electric pump fills a 0.2 l gas accumulator, switches off at about 60 bar according to the pressure sensor and restarts near 40 bar. CARB counts automatic transmission controls among the monitored output components. A leaking accumulator, valve or seal can end in lost gears; P0944 covers a general pressure loss of the hydraulic unit.

Implausible pressure sensor signal (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2719 - Pressure Control Solenoid D Control Circuit Range/Performance

title: DTC P2728 - Pressure Control Solenoid E Control Circuit Range/Performance

On the Allison 1000 (16OBDG08, 17OBDG04) the TCM compares desired with actual current on PCS 1; a gap of at least 0.5 A in 10 of fewer than 20 samples sets a Type A fault with MIL. On the T76 six-speed table of 2016, where valve E serves the 1-2-3-4 clutch, an invalid voltage flag for 4.4 of 5 s sets it without MIL. Bulletin PI0893 explains the second case for 2013 vehicles with the 6T70/6T75: as a Type C history code next to P2719 and P0965 it can appear falsely with fluid between -0.5 and 0 °C in Park or Neutral and needs no parts. MIL behaviour therefore depends on the gearbox.
symptoms: MIL on Allison-equipped trucks
History code without symptoms on GM six-speeds
Firm shifts if pressure control is degraded
possible_causes: Coil current deviating from command (resistance change, poor contact) (likelihood: high)
False history code near 0 °C fluid temperature (GM 6T70/6T75) (likelihood: medium)
Unstable supply voltage to the TCM (likelihood: low)
Worn solenoid E (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2728 (Pressure Control Solenoid E Control Circuit Range/Performance).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: pressure control solenoid e, wiring harness.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.3-5 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Coil current deviating from command (resistance change, poor contact) (likelihood: high).

title: DTC P2729 - Pressure Control Solenoid E Control Circuit Low
problem_description: P2729 indicates the control line of solenoid E is pulled low, usually by a short to ground. On the Allison 1000 GM detects this when the output connection has almost no impedance to ground and confirms it within 75 ms (Type A). The eight-speed and six-speed tables of 2016 flag the low state for 0.3 s and set it after one trip. For the 2023 Corvette dual-clutch transmission, a sense voltage below roughly 1.7 V with the driver on, held for 150 ms, identifies a ground short at the system pressure pilot valve (Type A); Ford's TR9070 stores its shorted switch case under this number. GM bulletin PIP5646B for 2019-2020 Silverado and Sierra 8L90 shows that P2729 can also come from a failing TCM rather than the harness.

Abrupt stop or wheel lock at low speed in the GM 8L90 case
Limited gear selection

Shorted winding in solenoid E (likelihood: medium)
TCM internal failure (GM 8L90) (likelihood: medium)
Conductive contamination in the connector (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P272A - Transmission Range Select Motor Control Circuit
problem_description: P272A refers to the control circuit of the electric motor that moves the gearbox into the selected range in shift-by-wire designs. Mitsubishi documents it for the 2022 Outlander with CVT: the shift actuator has two three-phase windings fed through separate relays, and motor A is the one reported as range select motor. With ignition on and the actuator at rest, a phase that reads low although no phase is energised sets the code; a second test after ignition off turns relays A and B off in turn and briefly rotates the motor. Listed causes are an open relay A circuit, an open phase wire, a relay stuck off, the coil or the electric shift module. If only one winding fails nothing changes for the driver; with both lost shifting is blocked and the drivetrain goes to neutral.

Gear selection refused, vehicle in neutral (second fault)

Open U, V or W phase wire to motor A (likelihood: medium)
Faulty motor coil A in the shift actuator (likelihood: medium)
Electric shift control module fault (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P272B - Transmission Range Select Motor Control Circuit Current Too High
problem_description: P272B flags excessive current in the circuit of the range select motor, normally caused by a winding or wire shorted to supply. On the 2022 Mitsubishi Outlander with CVT, Mitsubishi checks this with ignition on: when one of the two phases that should be energised shows the non-energised voltage level (9-16 V instead of about 0 V), the code is set. The service text lists short circuits to power on either the A or the B winding, the connectors or the electric shift module as causes, so the code does not prove which winding is at fault. Unlike the open-circuit code P272A, the fail-safe is drastic: shifting is prohibited and the powertrain goes to neutral. The MIL comes on, and the yellow shift warning depends on road speed.

title: DTC P272C - Park Pawl Motor Control Circuit
problem_description: P272C concerns the control circuit of the motor that engages and releases the park pawl. In the shift actuator of the 2022 Mitsubishi Outlander with CVT this is winding B, powered through its own relay B, while winding A is reported under P272A. The detection mirrors that code: with ignition on and the actuator idle, any phase of B reading low without being energised triggers it, and an after-run test with ignition off switches the relays off one at a time and turns the motor a little. Causes named are an open relay B circuit, an open phase line, relay B stuck off, coil B or the shift module. Because the other winding can still drive the actuator, a single fault has no effect on driving; only when both circuits fail are shifts blocked and the car placed in neutral.

GM shares the logic with P2731, which covers the same check in first gear. Bulletin 21-NA-169 for low-mileage 9T45/50/60 units lists P2731 to P2733 together and, with clean fluid, renews the solenoid assembly together with the valve body. title: DTC P2735 - Pressure Control Solenoid F Intermittent

title: DTC P2737 - Pressure Control Solenoid F Control Circuit Range/Performance
problem_description: The standard title describes implausible readings on the control circuit of solenoid F that are neither a clean open nor a short. With the vehicle below 2 mph, accelerator released, engine between 600 and 1,200 rpm, fluid above 50 °C and the garage shift finished, the TCM compares the averaged pressures from the primary and secondary pulley sensors in both pump modes. If the differences stay too large, the valve is judged not to follow its command; GM classes this Type B, so the MIL comes on after two trips. Other makers do not publish P2737. title: DTC P2775 - Upshift Switch Circuit Range/Performance
problem_description: P2775 covers an upshift paddle or tip switch whose voltage is electrically possible but belongs to neither of its two legal states. If the voltage sits outside both windows for 120 s, P2775 sets as Type C, so without MIL. Ford's 2024 summary for the TR9070 twin-clutch gearbox lists P2775 as illegal voltage on the upshift paddle input. title: DTC P279A - Transfer Case Gear High Incorrect Ratio

title: DTC P280B - Transmission Range Sensor B Circuit Not Learned
problem_description: P280B flags missing or invalid adaptation values for the second range sensor signal. Where a design reads A and B in different modules, as GM does with sensor A in the TCM and sensor B in the engine module, a replaced or reprogrammed engine controller can lose the B reference while A is still learned. No maker documents P280B publicly, and CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 gives only the general duty to monitor transmission inputs. GM's correlation check P2805 shows how closely both paths are compared afterwards: their duty cycles must add up to 100 % within about 5 %. Without a valid B reference the plausibility checks against A cannot run. Perform the learn with a scan tool once circuit codes P2800-P2804 are cleared.

title: DTC P281E - Pressure Control Solenoid H Control Circuit High

title: DTC P287B - Shift Fork A Calibration Not Learned
problem_description: P287B says that the control unit has no valid learned reference positions for shift fork A and therefore cannot place it accurately in neutral or in its gears. Typical triggers are a new or reflashed TCM, an interrupted learn routine, or a fork position fault that makes the learn fail.

title: DTC P2880 - Engine Disconnect Clutch Actuator Circuit Low
problem_description: P2880 is stored when the signal in the actuator circuit of the engine disconnect clutch stays below its permitted window. The control module normally switches the output off to protect itself. No manufacturer publishes a description of this code; the circuit monitoring follows the general CARB demand that output components of the powertrain be checked for electrical faults. Whether the clutch then rests open or closed depends on its design; the Ford F-150 PowerBoost and the Audi plug-in hybrids use hydraulic clutches inside the transmission. title: DTC P2883 - Engine Disconnect Clutch Temperature Too High

Mercedes-Benz lists P288300 as clutch temperature too high among the codes its predictive repair tool evaluates for the 8F-DCT dual-clutch transmission (type 724.1, conventional and hybrid versions); the bulletin does not say which clutch it refers to. The module usually restricts torque or slip phases until the clutch has cooled, so the fault can disappear on its own.

title: DTC P2887 - Park Lock/Pawl Actuator Circuit

Volvo's Technical Journal 36754 concerns several 2024 models whose TCM stores P288772 with the message Transmission Service Required; the remedy is new TCM software, and Volvo explicitly says not to replace the gearbox.

title: DTC P288C - Engine Disconnect Clutch Actuator Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High

title: DTC P2890 - Cylinder 1 Ion Current Sense Circuit
problem_description: Some engines use the spark plug as a combustion sensor: between sparks a measuring voltage is applied, and the hot, ionised gas lets a small current flow whose shape reveals misfire and knock. Saab built the principle into its Trionic engines: on the four-cylinder T8 the coil of cylinder 1 feeds its ion signal to a separate processing module, which also decides whether cylinder 1 or 4 is on the firing stroke, because the engine has no camshaft sensor. A dead cylinder 1 signal can therefore disturb synchronisation as well. Saab used its own codes; no manufacturer publicly documents P2890.

title: DTC P2893 - Cylinder 1 Ion Current Sense Circuit High
problem_description: With P2893 the ion signal from cylinder 1 sits above its plausible ceiling. A signal line touching a supply voltage is the most direct explanation; crosstalk from the ignition primary circuit or a defective evaluation stage that saturates can show the same picture. Saab's ion detection module, for instance, receives the cylinder 1 trigger on pin 9 and the matching ion input on pin 16, both of which can be checked for foreign voltage. title: DTC P2896 - Cylinder 2 Ion Current Sense Circuit Low
problem_description: P2896 reports a cylinder 2 ion signal that remains under its lower limit. A ground short on the line from coil 2, a cracked plug insulator that drains the measuring voltage to the cylinder head, or a coil whose bias generator has failed can all produce a near-zero reading. Where several cylinders share a harness section or connector, a chafed spot can hit cylinder 2 alone if only its conductor is damaged, so the wiring along the cam cover deserves a look. On Saab's 2009 four-cylinder module the cylinder 2 ion input is pin 7, which allows measuring the line directly. No manufacturer publishes this code. Without a usable signal, misfire and knock detection for cylinder 2 lose their basis. P2897 is the high counterpart; cylinder 1 reports the same condition as P2892.

title: DTC P28C1 - Ion Sense Module Supply Voltage Low
problem_description: P28C1 means the ion sense module is powered, but its supply sits below the level it needs to work reliably. title: DTC P28C2 - Ion Sense Module Supply Voltage High
problem_description: P28C2 is stored when the voltage feeding the ion sense module exceeds its upper limit. The cause is rarely the module: a failing alternator regulator, a jump start from a 24 V source or a poor ground at the module that makes the measured difference look larger are more typical. title: DTC P28C3 - EVAP System High Load Purge Line B Performance
problem_description: Under boost the intake manifold is above ambient pressure, so turbo engines add a high-load purge path: compressed air drives an ejector (venturi) that draws canister vapour into the compressor inlet, with check valves keeping boost out of the tank side. CARB requires every purge path to be checked for missing flow, from 2021 including disconnected lines, unless the high-load path carries under 1 percent of purge mass on the US06 cycle. P28C3 is the function check of a second such line, B. Line A is P04F0, used for example by Genesis on the 2.5T with a dual purge ejector that clogs with debris. No manufacturer publicly documents P28C3 or names line B. Volvo's 2019–2020 Dual Purge action shows the typical fault: a check valve upsetting ejector flow at high load, logging a code and the MIL.

title: DTC P28C9 - Clutch A Motor Overspeed
problem_description: P28C9 is stored when the clutch A motor turns faster than the controller considers plausible for the pressure it is asked to hold. Because the pump in such actuators delivers oil straight into the closed clutch circuit, the motor should slow down once pressure is reached; if it keeps racing, the oil is escaping or the pump is not loaded. Likely reasons are a leaking clutch piston seal, air drawn in at low fluid level, or a broken coupling between motor shaft and gerotor so that the motor spins free. title: DTC P28CE - Clutch A Pressure Sensor Circuit Low

title: DTC P28D8 - Clutch B Motor Overspeed

title: DTC P2A00 - O2 Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1

Ford's 2023 diesels compare the measured oxygen share with a value derived from injected quantity, boost pressure and exhaust gas recirculation and expect close to 20.95 % in overrun. On GM's 3.0 L diesel a leaking intake manifold triggered it (bulletin 22-NA-128).

The letter C stands for a third element – a further metering valve, a cam-driven pump plunger or a unit injector with its own solenoid. No manufacturer publishes P2A13. Volvo and Mack list this fault type for elements B, D and F on their 11 and 13 litre truck engines of the US17 emissions level, where it traced back to the rail pressure system or a slipping cam lobe. For C, the heavy-duty rule 13 CCR 1971.1 on injection quantity and pressure control is the basis. P2A14 and P2A15 cover low and high electrical readings. Output is usually derated.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Lack of power, especially under load
Engine power derated by the control module
possible_causes: Fault in the high-pressure system (leak, relief valve, low-pressure supply) that the element cannot compensate (likelihood: high)
Worn or sticking metering element C (valve, plunger or cam lobe) (likelihood: medium)
Outdated engine control software or calibration (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2A13 (Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control C Range/Performance (Cam/Rotor/Injector)).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: injection pump metering c, injection pump, wiring harness.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 1-8 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Fault in the high-pressure system (leak, relief valve, low-pressure supply) that the element cannot compensate (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Worn or sticking metering element C (valve, plunger or cam lobe) (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

title: DTC P2A14 - Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control C Low (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
problem_description: P2A14 reports that the signal in the drive circuit of fuel metering element C has fallen below its expected window. In practice the control module sees too little voltage or current on that output, as happens when the line touches ground or, depending on the driver design, an open wire. C denotes a third metering element besides A and B, found only on pumps or engines with several separately driven elements. No maker documents P2A14 publicly. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel shows how such a check works for its single regulator: a control line shorted to ground for longer than one second sets P0253 as an immediate Type A fault. Coil of metering element C open or shorted to its housing (likelihood: medium)
Faulty output stage in the engine control module (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2A3F - Excessive Time to Enter Alternative Fuel Control
problem_description: On a bi-fuel or gas-start vehicle the control unit only changes over to gas once preconditions are met, for example warm coolant, enough pressure in the rail and a selected gas mode. P2A3F means this changeover did not happen within the calibrated time. GM's 2015 Impala bi-fuel bulletin PI1330 gives an idea of the conditions: below −20 °C ambient the engine starts on petrol and moves to CNG only when coolant reaches 50 °C. Ford's 2003 bi-fuel CNG pickups need at least 517 kPa rail pressure for a gas start and drop back to petrol below it. CARB treats the gas mode of such cars like a petrol engine up to model year 2018 and already demands a closed-loop entry time check (P0125 family). No maker documents P2A3F. Suspects are a slow thermostat, low tank pressure or a sticking valve.

Tank pressure too low for the switch-over (likelihood: medium)

The regulator normally lives in the engine bay, next to the right-hand strut mount on GM's 2015 Impala bi-fuel, and Blackstone requires warm engine coolant to circulate through its SAN209 unit so that it does not ice up. Its connector therefore sees heat, vibration and condensation. Loose terminals, a harness chafed against coolant hoses or moisture inside the plug are the usual suspects. No manufacturer publishes P2A6D; CARB expects circuit faults of such inputs to be detected. Wiggle-test the harness while watching live data, and look for corrosion in the connector.
symptoms: Check engine light on, sometimes clearing again
Gas gauge flickers or jumps
Sporadic switch from gas to petrol while driving
possible_causes: Loose or widened terminal in the sensor connector (likelihood: high)
Condensation or corrosion in the plug near the coolant-heated regulator (likelihood: medium)
Harness rubbing on hoses or brackets with intermittent contact (likelihood: medium)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2A6D (Alternative Fuel Rail Pressure Regulator Inlet Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: alt fuel rail pressure regulator, wiring harness, afcm.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.

recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Loose or widened terminal in the sensor connector (likelihood: high).

title: DTC P2A6E - Alternative Fuel Rail Pressure Regulator Inlet Pressure Too Low
problem_description: P2A6E is not a wiring fault: the inlet pressure sensor works, but the gas reaching the regulator is too weak for it to hold rail pressure. A regulator can only reduce pressure, so once the supply approaches its outlet setpoint, rail pressure sinks with it. ITT's CNG regulator patent addresses exactly this low-supply phase with a bypass that opens below a set inlet pressure. Common reasons are a nearly empty cylinder, a tank solenoid or manual valve that is not fully open, or a clogged high-pressure filter. Ford's 2003 bi-fuel CNG system closed the tank valve and fell back to petrol once system pressure dropped under 517 kPa (75 psia). No manufacturer publishes P2A6E; refuel first, then compare inlet pressure with a gauge.

Loss of power or stumbling in gas mode, especially at high load
Automatic switch to petrol or engine stalls on dedicated gas engines

High-pressure filter clogged or line restricted (likelihood: medium)
Inlet pressure sensor reading too low within its range (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2A6F - Alternative Fuel Rail Pressure Regulator Inlet Pressure Too High
problem_description: P2A6F reports a regulator inlet pressure above the calibrated maximum. Only cylinder pressure is present upstream of the regulator, so a genuinely high value usually comes from the tank side, such as overfilling at a dispenser without temperature compensation or a cold-filled cylinder that later warms up strongly; a transducer reading high but still in range is the other option. Blackstone's SAN209 regulator allows up to 4,500 psig at the inlet and carries a relief device on the outlet. No manufacturer documents P2A6F. Verify the reading against a gauge before suspecting the tank.

title: DTC P2A70 - Alternative Fuel Hydraulic Fuel Pump Select Valve Control Circuit
problem_description: Some heavy-duty LNG systems do not drive the cryogenic tank pump directly but through hydraulics: an engine- or motor-driven hydraulic pump supplies oil to a reciprocating hydraulic drive on each tank pump. Westport's patent US8726785B2 shows two LNG vessels whose pumps sit inside the tanks, plus a selector valve that the controller switches to decide which pump receives hydraulic flow. P2A70 covers the electrical control circuit of such a select valve and is set when the driver output detects a general fault. If the valve cannot be commanded, the system may be stuck on one tank or lose LNG supply. No manufacturer publishes P2A70; CARB's heavy-duty rule requires output components to be monitored. P2A72 and P2A73 separate the low and high cases.

title: DTC P2A71 - Alternative Fuel Hydraulic Fuel Pump Select Valve Control Range/Performance
problem_description: P2A71 concerns the function of the hydraulic fuel pump select valve rather than its wiring: the circuit is intact, but the system does not respond as expected after a switch command. In Westport's design the controller links the hydraulic pressure it measures to whichever pump the selector valve should be feeding; if the pressure pattern does not match the commanded pump, or the empty-tank logic sees no change after switching, the valve is probably sticking or leaking internally. Contaminated hydraulic oil, a worn spool or a weak solenoid are typical. Caterpillar's patent describes a related directional valve whose actuator is shifted once pressure sensors detect the stroke end. No manufacturer publishes P2A71 or its limits.

title: DTC P2A72 - Alternative Fuel Hydraulic Fuel Pump Select Valve Control Circuit Low
problem_description: P2A72 is set when the control circuit of the hydraulic fuel pump select valve reads lower than expected for the commanded state. On a low-side driver this typically means the control wire is shorted to ground, so the valve coil may stay energised; on a high-side driver a short to ground or a shorted coil pulls the output down and may trip its protection. Either way the controller can no longer trust which LNG tank pump is being driven. Westport's patented system relies on knowing the valve position to assign hydraulic pressure readings to the right pump, so tank selection and empty-tank detection become unreliable. No manufacturer documents P2A72. Measure coil resistance and check the harness for chafing against the chassis.

title: DTC P2A73 - Alternative Fuel Hydraulic Fuel Pump Select Valve Control Circuit High
problem_description: P2A73 signals that the select valve control circuit sits at a higher voltage than the commanded state allows. title: DTC P2A76 - Alternative Fuel Hydraulic Pump Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
problem_description: P2A76 is set when the hydraulic pump pressure reading looks electrically sound yet makes no sense for the operating state. Westport's patent explains why a fixed expectation is not enough: pressure rises with hydraulic pump speed, which follows engine speed when the pump is engine-driven, and with the LNG pressure the cryogenic pump works against. The controller therefore corrects its thresholds with a look-up table. A reading that stays flat while the pump strokes, shows no drop at stroke end, or disagrees with downstream fuel pressure points to a drifting sensor, but also to worn pump seals or low oil level. No manufacturer publishes P2A76 or its limits. Compare with a mechanical gauge on the test port and check the oil level.

title: DTC P2A7C - Alternative Fuel Hydraulic Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
problem_description: P2A7C is set when the hydraulic pressure sensor signal falls below its valid band, most often from a signal wire grounded against the chassis, an open 5 V reference or a sensor with an internal short. If this sensor watches the return side, as in one of Caterpillar's layouts, a dead-low reading would hardly stand out at first, since return pressure is low anyway; the range check against the minimum voltage still catches it. On the drive side a low value can mask the pressure rise that marks a completed stroke. The control may then rely on the remaining sensor or stop the LNG pump. Where both pressure sensors share a reference wire, check whether P2A77 is stored too. No manufacturer documents P2A7C or its thresholds.

With LNG the temperature gap is extreme, and Westport's patent CA2862664C describes the typical failure. At a cold start, at idle or under light load coolant crawls through the exchanger and can freeze inside it; flow then drops without stopping entirely, vaporizer capacity falls and the downstream gas temperature sinks, which can harm later components. Westport therefore runs fuel and coolant in parallel flow during start and idle and switches to counter flow afterwards. A stuck switching valve or ice can thus cause P2A8C. No manufacturer publishes the code or its limits.
symptoms: Malfunction lamp on
Reduced power or gas mode blocked, especially when cold
Ice on the vaporizer or gas lines behind it
possible_causes: Coolant partly frozen inside vaporizer B after cold start or long idling (likelihood: high)
Valve that switches between parallel and counter flow stuck (likelihood: medium)
Low coolant level or too little antifreeze in the mixture (likelihood: medium)
Deposits reducing heat transfer in vaporizer B (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2A8C (Alternative Fuel Vaporizer B Performance).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: alt fuel vaporizer b, engine coolant circuit, afcm.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 1-5 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Coolant partly frozen inside vaporizer B after cold start or long idling (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Valve that switches between parallel and counter flow stuck (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

title: DTC P2A8D - Alternative Fuel Vaporizer C Performance
problem_description: P2A8D concerns a third vaporizer, found where large engines or several fuel branches need more heat exchange than one or two units provide. The code means unit C turns too little liquid into usable gas, or delivers it too cold, while its outlet sensor works. Where A and B run under the same conditions, the module can single out C by comparison, and that is the likely logic, though no maker publishes it. Timing matters for any such check: US7073489B2 points out that a thermostat sitting in the coolant reacts only slowly to changes in gas flow, and CA2862664C notes that no vaporizing is needed while the engine runs on another fuel. A fair test therefore waits for warm coolant and real gas demand. CARB lists such functional checks under its comprehensive component rules.

title: DTC P2A8E - Alternative Fuel Pump A Performance
problem_description: P2A8E reports that alternative fuel pump A no longer delivers what it should, a mechanical or hydraulic fault rather than an electrical one. Such pumps move liquid fuel, typically LNG out of a cryogenic tank. A patent application now held by Cespira, US20080302111A1, shows how a controller can judge them from the delivery line pressure alone: each time the pump is commanded on, pressure has to climb from a lower to an upper set point within a known range of slopes. A clearly flatter rise means lost volumetric efficiency, and a falling pressure means the pump cannot even keep up with the engine. The document names worn piston seals, leaking static seals or check valves, dirt in the fuel and a weak hydraulic drive as causes. No manufacturer publishes P2A8E or its limits.

Hydraulic drive of pump A delivering too little force or speed (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P2A8F - Alternative Fuel Pump B Performance

title: DTC P2A90 - Alternative Fuel Pump C Performance

The pump diagnosis in US20080302111A1 explains how a slow pressure rise reveals the loss. No manufacturer publishes P2A90; P2A87 to P2A8A cover pump C's stroke valve.

title: DTC P2A91 - Alternative Fuel Tank Select Valve A Control Circuit/Open
problem_description: A tank select valve decides which storage vessel feeds the fuel system. That sets it apart from a tank shutoff valve (P224C, P2A22 and onward), which simply opens or isolates one cylinder, and from the hydraulic fuel pump select valve (P2A70 and onward), which routes drive oil to a pump. Westport's patent US8726785B2 shows the idea with two LNG vessels and one external pump, where an insulated valve links the pump to either vessel. P2A91 means the control circuit of select valve A is open or otherwise faulty, so the valve stays in its rest position. Fuel is then drawn only from the vessel reached in that position and the rest may become unusable. No manufacturer documents P2A91 publicly; CARB requires output circuits to be checked for continuity.

title: DTC P2A92 - Alternative Fuel Tank Select Valve A Control Performance
problem_description: P2A92 is the functional check for tank select valve A: the wiring tests pass, yet the fuel system does not behave as if the commanded vessel were connected. Software can judge this only through pressures. A patent by Cespira, the Westport and Volvo venture, outlines the logic for two compressed-gas supplies with their own pressure sensors: a supply-select valve assembly routes one supply to a compressor and the other to the regulator, and stages change whenever a supply falls under a set pressure. After such a command the newly chosen supply should start to lose pressure while the other holds steady. If nothing changes, or the wrong tank empties, valve A is probably sticking or leaking across its seat. No manufacturer publishes P2A92 or a threshold for it.

title: DTC P2A93 - Alternative Fuel Tank Select Valve A Control Circuit Low
problem_description: P2A93 is stored when the module measures a voltage on the control line of tank select valve A that falls short of the level expected for the commanded state. Valves near cryogenic lines collect condensation, so water in the connector is a plausible cause. No manufacturer documents P2A93; P2A94 is the high case.

title: DTC P2A94 - Alternative Fuel Tank Select Valve A Control Circuit High
problem_description: P2A94 reports a control voltage at tank select valve A above what the module expects for the commanded state. title: DTC P2A9D - Alternative Fuel High Pressure System Small Leak
problem_description: P2A9D points to a slow loss of gas from the high-pressure side, from the cylinders up to the regulator, too small to notice while driving. A Toyota and Denso patent, US6467466B1, explains the catch: with the valves open, a modest pressure drop cannot be told apart from consumption. The method therefore waits for a stopped engine with all shutoff valves shut, records the pressure, compares it after a set time and adds up the losses over several stops, so even traces show. Because tank pressure varies with content, it also offers a rate-based test. No manufacturer documents P2A9D publicly; CARB has gas vehicles under evaporative rules submit their own leak monitoring plan.

title: DTC P2A9E - Alternative Fuel Return Line Valve Control Circuit/Open

title: DTC P2AA1 - Alternative Fuel Return Line Valve Control Circuit High

title: DTC P2AA2 - Alternative Fuel Return Line Insufficient Flow
problem_description: P2AA2 is a hydraulic fault, not an electrical one: too little liquid fuel comes back from the rail to the tank. The return keeps the fuel in the rail cool and liquid, so a weak return lets it warm up and boil. Patent US5623907A on a liquid propane delivery system shows the parts involved: a check valve in the return which only opens at roughly 15 psi differential to hold line pressure, and a solenoid-controlled bypass that flushes vapor out of the rail before start-up. A Hyundai patent on an LPI engine routes the return through a regulator unit with its own return valve. A sticking check valve, a kinked line, a valve that does not open or a weak pump all reduce the flow. No manufacturer documents P2AA2 publicly; circuit faults of the valve are P2A9E to P2AA1.

title: DTC P2AA3 - Cold Start EGR B Flow Insufficient Detected
problem_description: P2AA3 belongs to the cold-start strategy (CSERS) newer diesels run in the first minutes after a long soak. P2AA3 is set when the second EGR path, B, delivers too little flow in that phase, so NOx rises while the catalysts are still cold. Which loop carries the letter B is up to the manufacturer. CARB's cold-start component checks require a response that is robustly detectable and in the commanded direction; where no feedback sensor exists, the monitor may judge the final command instead of the delivered flow. No manufacturer documents P2AA4 publicly; FCA uses only the A-side code P04DD in its published bulletins. The A/B ratio check across both paths is P2D1C.

title: DTC P2AA5 - EGR Cooler Bypass Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High Bank 1

title: DTC P2AA9 - Engine Coolant Bypass Valve B Position Sensor Circuit Low
problem_description: P2AA9 is set once the position sensor on coolant valve B reports a value below its valid band, which nearly always means the signal wire or the sensor output is pulled toward ground. Rotary coolant valves in thermal management modules report their angle so the engine computer can steer coolant between radiator, heater and other loops. No manufacturer documents P2AA9 publicly. GM's 2025 diesel tables list the matching check for valve C as P23C4: the SENT reading has to drop under 27 counts for 4 of 5 seconds, rated Type B with two trips, and the test only runs while SENT communication itself is healthy. Ford, by contrast, gives the letter B to a transmission cooling valve without position feedback. The high-side fault is P2AAA.

title: DTC P2AAC - Diesel Fuel Presence Sensor Circuit
problem_description: P2AAC is the general circuit fault of a sensor meant to recognise diesel where only gasoline belongs, so the system can react to misfuelling before damage occurs. No manufacturer documents this sensor or the code publicly, and its exact design is not described in sources available. P2AAC applies when the sensor circuit fails in a way that is neither clearly low (P2AAE) nor clearly high (P2AAF). CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs.

title: DTC P2AB8 - Wastegate Position Sensor A Circuit Low

title: DTC P2B10 - Cylinder 1 Injection Pulse Offset Not Learned
problem_description: P2B10 means the engine control holds no valid learned offset for injector 1 – the correction of the opening time used for very small injection quantities has not been established. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford, the one maker with a published monitor for this group, lists only the exceeded-limit codes (P2B11 and siblings) for its Power Stroke diesels. The legal basis is CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 (f)(4.2.4)(A)(i): a fuel system feedback that does not begin working within a time chosen by the manufacturer counts as a malfunction. A Bosch patent explains the learn itself: in overrun the activation time of a test injection is raised in small steps from a value too short to open the injector until the crankshaft speed reacts. P2B11 is the partner for a value that was learned but lies out of range.
symptoms: Warning lamp, otherwise often no noticeable effect
Possibly harder combustion noise at idle on cylinder 1
possible_causes: Learn values cleared – after replacing injector 1 or the control unit, or after an adaption reset with a scan tool (likelihood: high)
Too few coasting phases with fuel cut-off for the learn to run (likelihood: medium)
Injector 1 opening inconsistently, so no stable value is found (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2B10 (Cylinder 1 Injection Pulse Offset Not Learned).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: fuel injector cylinder 1, engine control module.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.3-5 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Learn values cleared – after replacing injector 1 or the control unit, or after an adaption reset with a scan tool (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Too few coasting phases with fuel cut-off for the learn to run (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.
source: OBDex / SAE J2012 & ISO 15031-6 Open Diagnostic Standard

title: DTC P2B11 - Cylinder 1 Injection Pulse Offset Exceeded Learning Limit
problem_description: P2B11 says the learned small-quantity correction for injector 1 has drifted beyond what the engine control may apply. Ford documents the code for its 3.0 L and 6.7 L Power Stroke diesels under Zero Fuel Calibration: the PCM fires a tiny test injection, compares the energising time that produced a measurable effect with the target stored for that injector and sets the code when the result is at least 156 µs too short or 254 µs too long. Ford TSB 18-2015 for the 2017 F-Super Duty 6.7 L ties P2B11 and its siblings to a fuel knock at idle caused by wrongly learned injector timing; the fix was resetting the high-pressure side, the minimum fuel mass adaption and the crank sensor learn, then reprogramming the PCM. P2B10 is the not-learned state of the same injector.

Diesel knock at idle, sometimes together with balance code P0263
possible_causes: Incorrectly learned injector values in the PCM (Ford TSB 18-2015, reset and reprogramming) (likelihood: high)
Injector 1 worn or coked so its opening behaviour has really shifted (likelihood: medium)
Disturbed crankshaft speed signal falsifying the learn result (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2B12 - Cylinder 2 Injection Pulse Offset Not Learned
problem_description: P2B12 is stored when injector 2's pulse offset has not been learned, so the controller still relies on a default value for the smallest injections. The public record contains no manufacturer using this exact code; the explanation here follows from the title and from the neighbouring monitors. Learning of this kind needs repeated coasting phases with fuel cut-off, because only then can the effect of a single test injection be picked up through the crankshaft speed signal, as a Bosch patent on zero-fuel quantity calibration sets out. Engines that rarely coast – long motorway runs, towing – or a recent adaption reset after injector work can therefore leave the learn unfinished. CARB treats feedback that never starts in time as a fault. Once learned but too far off, cylinder 2 reports P2B13 instead.

Possibly louder combustion on cylinder 2 at low load

Crankshaft speed signal too noisy to detect the test injection (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2B13 - Cylinder 2 Injection Pulse Offset Exceeded Learning Limit

title: DTC P2B14 - Cylinder 3 Injection Pulse Offset Not Learned
problem_description: P2B14 tells that no offset has yet been learned for injector 3. No carmaker publishes this code for a specific engine, and the GM and Ford tables checked do not contain it. A GM patent on fast learning of diesel injector corrections shows why such a learn can take long: corrections are kept per injector and per rail pressure level, so a six-cylinder with four pressure levels needs 24 learned cells, each filled only during suitable fuel cut-off phases. The patent's answer is to extrapolate from one measured pressure to the others. Until the cells for cylinder 3 are complete, small pilot injections on that cylinder run without their individual correction. Under CARB (f)(4.2.4)(A)(i) such feedback must start within a set time; P2B15 is the out-of-limit partner.

Slightly uneven idle in some cases

Rail pressure not holding steady enough during the test injection (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2B17 - Cylinder 4 Injection Pulse Offset Exceeded Learning Limit

Ford's summary sets the code when the measured energising time misses the target by 156 µs downward or 254 µs upward.

title: DTC P2B18 - Cylinder 5 Injection Pulse Offset Not Learned
problem_description: P2B18 means injector 5 has no learned offset. No manufacturer documents this exact code. A not-learned status, by contrast, says that no usable value exists yet, for example after a new injector or control unit or after an adaption reset. For diesel engines CARB (f)(4.2.4)(A)(i) requires detection of feedback that does not start in time. The limit-exceeded twin is P2B19.

title: DTC P2B1A - Cylinder 6 Injection Pulse Offset Not Learned
problem_description: P2B1A reports that the pulse offset for injector 6 has not been learned. Public manufacturer sources do not name this code; on the 3.0 L V6 Power Stroke built by Ford, where cylinder 6 is the last one, Ford's summary lists only the exceeded-limit code P2B1B. CARB explains why such learning exists in diesel engines: since 2010, sections (f)(4.2.2) and (f)(4.2.3) demand checks that the right fuel quantity arrives at the right crank angle, and where no failure could push emissions over the threshold, reaching the control limits serves as the criterion instead. An unlearned offset means that pilot quantities on cylinder 6 rest on nominal data only. Few symptoms beyond the lamp are to be expected; the cure is completing the learn under suitable driving, then checking injector 6 if it never succeeds.

title: DTC P2B1E - Cylinder 8 Injection Pulse Offset Not Learned
problem_description: P2B1E means injector 8 has not received a learned pulse offset. As the final cylinder in the group it belongs to V8 engines; Ford's 6.7 L V8 would be the obvious candidate, but Ford publishes only the exceeded-limit code P2B1F for it, so no manufacturer source for P2B1E exists. CARB leaves the time allowed for learning to the manufacturer: per (f)(4.2.4)(A)(i) a fault exists when feedback control has not begun within that interval. Because an eight-cylinder needs one learned set per injector and pressure level, GM patented an extrapolation of values to shorten the learning time. In service the code mostly points to a learn that was reset or never had suitable coasting phases; only if it comes back under good conditions do injector 8, its wiring or the crank signal come into question.
symptoms: Warning lamp

GM documents the check for its 3.0-litre inline-six Duramax diesel: in the 2025 table 25OBDG04B the driver stage flags a current above 5.5 A, and 80 failures in 100 samples taken every 12.5 ms set a Type B fault, so the MIL follows on the second trip. Enabling needs more than 11 V on the powertrain relay and an engine that is not cranking. A seized rotary valve, debris in the housing or a motor with shorted windings are typical reasons. GM bulletin 21-NA-149 lists P2B58 for LM2 trucks with a chafed engine harness. Heating and warm-up may suffer while the valve is stuck.
symptoms: MIL on after the second drive with the fault
Slow warm-up or weak cabin heat
Fans may run more often as a precaution
possible_causes: Rotary valve stiff or seized from deposits or debris in the housing (likelihood: high)
Valve motor with shorted turns (likelihood: medium)
Chafed engine harness on GM LM2 (bulletin 21-NA-149) (likelihood: medium)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2B58 (Engine Coolant Flow Control Valve Motor Current High).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: engine coolant flow control valve, wiring harness, ecm.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 1-10 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Rotary valve stiff or seized from deposits or debris in the housing (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Valve motor with shorted turns (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.
source: OBDex / SAE J2012 & ISO 15031-6 Open Diagnostic Standard

title: DTC P2B59 - Engine Coolant Flow Control Valve Control Circuit/Open

In GM's 25OBDG04B (3.0 L Duramax) the driver reports a load resistance above 200 kΩ, meaning one of the motor wires is disconnected; 80 of 100 samples set a Type B fault. Otherwise check the connector, the harness and the valve motor. Shorts to ground and to supply are reported separately as P2B5A and P2B5B.

title: DTC P2B5A - Engine Coolant Flow Control Valve Control Circuit Low
problem_description: P2B5A stands for a short to ground in the control wiring of the coolant flow control valve motor. GM's 2025 table for the 3.0-litre Duramax describes the detection: the driver sees more than 9 A flowing, which it interprets as one motor wire touching ground, and 80 out of 100 samples at 12.5 ms set a two-trip Type B fault once relay voltage exceeds 11 V. Unlike P2B58, where the motor itself draws too much current, the cause here is normally insulation damage in the harness, a pinched wire near the valve or water in the connector. The valve stays in its last or default position, so coolant distribution becomes fixed. Short to power is P2B5B, open circuit P2B59.

title: DTC P2B5C - Engine Coolant Flow Control Valve Supply Circuit Low
problem_description: With P2B5C the supply voltage reaching the driver of the coolant flow control valve motor is too low. GM monitors this on the 3.0-litre Duramax (25OBDG04B): if the motor driver sees less than 6 V while the powertrain relay delivers more than 11 V, the difference points at the feed path, and a Type B fault follows after 80 hits in 100 samples. Typical causes are a blown or loose fuse, a corroded relay contact or a damaged supply wire; 21-NA-149 includes P2B5C among the LM2 codes linked to a chafed harness. Without enough voltage the motor cannot position the valve, so engine temperature control falls back to a default. A weak battery alone rarely sets it, because the relay check would fail as well.

High resistance at a ground or splice of the feed circuit (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2B5D - Engine Coolant Flow Control Valve Position Sensor Circuit
problem_description: P2B5D is the general circuit code for the position sensor of the coolant flow control valve, the feedback that tells the engine computer how far the rotary valve has turned. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM's 3.0-litre Duramax, whose valve reports its position digitally over a SENT link, covers the sensor through the low and high codes P2B5E and P2B5F and a separate communication check instead. A system using P2B5D would flag an implausible or missing signal that fits neither low nor high. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(15) requires such input circuits to be checked for continuity. With no valid position the engine computer cannot regulate coolant flow and usually parks the valve in a safe position.

title: DTC P2B62 - Coolant Pump B Supply Voltage Circuit

title: DTC P2B63 - Coolant Pump B Stuck/Stalled
problem_description: P2B63 means coolant pump B is powered and commanded but its rotor does not turn, or stays far below target speed. Brushless auxiliary pumps notice this themselves, for example from high current without rotation, and report it to the engine computer. Ford lists the code in its 2024 gasoline OBD summary as failure type 71 (actuator stuck) of pump B, base code P261A, checked continuously above 11 V battery voltage. Causes are a seized bearing, debris or deposits jamming the impeller, a pump frozen in a weak antifreeze mix, or an internally failed motor. GM's patent US20160047374A1 explains how comparing measured current and speed against expected values exposes such a pump fault. P2B65 signals the opposite case, too little load. Pump D has the twin code P2B6A.

title: DTC P2B64 - Coolant Pump B Control Module Overtemperature

title: DTC P2B66 - Coolant Pump D Control Circuit/Open
problem_description: P2B66 is the open-circuit code for the control line of coolant pump D, the pump a manufacturer labels D in its thermal management. The driver stage in the engine computer detects a broken wire, an unplugged connector or a pump input that no longer draws current. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Ford's 2024 summary shows the analogous logic for pumps A and B (P2600, P261A): a continuous check from 11 V battery voltage, in which the smart driver reports the output fault. Under CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(15), output components must be watched for circuit faults. A short to ground is P2B67, a short to voltage P2B68; pumps C and E use P26F4 and P2DF4. Without control the pump stays off and its loop loses cooling.
symptoms: Warning lamp with stored code

title: DTC P2B75 - Coolant Heater A Control Circuit Performance

title: DTC P2B83 - Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Overspeed/Air In System
problem_description: P2B83 concerns the electric pump that keeps coolant moving through a water-cooled charge air cooler. GM documents this in its 2025 diesel table 25OBDG04B: a reported pump speed of 8,500 rpm or more in 8 of 10 one-second samples sets the code, provided the pump is fitted and enabled, the engine is not cranking and relay voltage is at least 11 V; Type B, MIL after two trips. GM's 3.0-litre Duramax uses such a pump (M10, bulletin 23-NA-102). GM's bulletin 18-NA-291 for the supercharged LT4 notes that this pump switches off once it draws air, so the loop must be vacuum filled. Too little speed is P2B84, the B pump has P2CB1. Hot charge air can cut power.

title: DTC P2B88 - Intake Air O2 Sensor Circuit Bank 1
problem_description: P2B88 is the catch-all electrical code for the oxygen sensor that some turbocharged engines mount in the intake tract, behind compressor and charge air cooler, to judge how much exhaust the recirculation system is feeding back. title: DTC P2B91 - Turbocharger/Supercharger B Temperature Sensor Circuit High
problem_description: P2B91 is stored when temperature sensor B delivers a signal above its permitted window. By far the most frequent reason is a broken current path: an unplugged or corroded connector, a cracked wire or an element that has burned open, which pulls the input up to its reference voltage. A short to the 5 V supply or to battery voltage has the same effect. For an NTC part this looks like severe cold, for a platinum resistor like severe heat; the sensor patent US8328419B2 from Heraeus explains why lead strain and heat cycling make such breaks a known weak point. No manufacturer publishes this code. Per CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 (e)(15) it is kept separate from the low fault P2B90 and the general circuit code P2B8F. Sensor A uses P2B70.
symptoms: Warning lamp with stored code

title: DTC P2B9B - Vehicle Conditions Incorrect for Particulate Matter Sensor Regeneration

title: DTC P2B9F - Coolant Pump B Underspeed

title: DTC P2BA2 - Engine Coolant Pump Stuck/Stalled
problem_description: P2BA2 belongs to the electric main water pump. title: DTC P2BA4 - Catalyst Feedgas Performance
problem_description: Many diesel SCR systems rely on the oxidation catalyst ahead of them to turn part of the NO into NO2, because a mix near half NO2 lets the SCR reaction run fast at low temperature. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 (f)(1.2.3)(B) requires this check for 2015 and later diesels, but lets a maker cover it with the regular NMHC efficiency monitor; Ford's 2023 diesel summary does exactly that via P0420. GM and Cummins patents describe two methods: comparing SCR efficiency measured by the NOx sensors, or judging the catalyst's light-off heat after a hydrocarbon dose. No maker documents P2BA4 publicly. P2BA5 is the same check for a coated particulate filter; the driver mainly notices a lit MIL and possibly SCR codes.

title: DTC P2BA6 - NOx Exceedance - SCR NOx Catalyst Performance

title: DTC P2BA7 - NOx Exceedence - Empty Reagent Tank
problem_description: P2BA7 records that NOx control has been lost because the DEF or AdBlue tank has run dry, so no reagent can be dosed. Regulation (EU) 2017/1151 Annex XVI requires a level warning no later than 2,400 km ahead of an empty tank and an inducement that keeps the vehicle from operating with an empty tank, typically by blocking the next engine start after a countdown. CARB 13 CCR 1968.2 (f)(2.2.3)(B) asks for an empty-reagent diagnosis but exempts makers whose inducement prevents running dry. Ford lists P2BA7 in its 2014 code interpretation table; no public document gives a threshold. The normal level code is P203F; P2BA7 is the consequence once the tank is empty. Refilling with enough fluid usually clears warning and limits.

title: DTC P2BAD - NOx Exceedence - Root Cause Unknown

GM PIP5007 notes that from 2012 this code takes over from P20EE/P207F as the diagnostic path when the DIC reports poor fluid quality. Nissan lists it as NOx Concentration Exceeded for the 2016 Titan XD with the Cummins 5.0 L and fixes it by reflashing the ECM. Diagnosis starts with DEF quality, dosing and sensors.

title: DTC P2BB0 - Alternative Fuel Consumption Too Low
problem_description: On engines that burn compressed natural gas, LPG or another fuel besides petrol or diesel, the controller can estimate how much gas it has injected and compare that with how fast the tank actually empties, judged by tank pressure or level. title: DTC P2BB1 - Alternative Fuel Consumption Too High

title: DTC P2BB2 - Alternative Fuel Tank Empty

title: DTC P2BB4 - Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 4 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

problem_description: P2BBC sets when the position signal of the bypass valve A sensor sits too low – usually an open signal wire, a short to ground or a lost 5 V supply to the sensor. GM uses the code on the 2019 Corvette ZR1 with the supercharged LT5, whose electronic compressor recirculation valve (eCRV) reports its position as a share of the reference voltage: a raw value under 10 % in 10 of 14 samples taken every 100 ms counts as a failure, checked while relay voltage is at least 11 V and the engine is not cranking. It is a Type A fault, so the MIL comes on in the first trip. The opposite case, a signal stuck near the reference, is P2BBD; a valve that does not follow its command is P23AA. Unable to trust the valve position, the module typically limits boost.
symptoms: Check engine light on in the first trip
Limited boost and weaker acceleration
Possibly further 5 V reference codes if the supply is shorted
possible_causes: Signal wire shorted to ground or chafed against the engine (likelihood: high)
Open 5 V reference wire or reference shorted by another sensor on the same supply (likelihood: medium)
Pushed-out or corroded terminal in the valve connector (likelihood: medium)
Defective position sensor in the valve actuator (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2BBC (Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit Low).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: turbo bypass valve a, wiring harness, ecm.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-3 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Signal wire shorted to ground or chafed against the engine (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Open 5 V reference wire or reference shorted by another sensor on the same supply (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

title: DTC P2BBD - Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Circuit High

With the reading implausible, the module usually holds the valve in a safe position and reduces boost, so the car feels flat and may make noise when the throttle snaps shut.

title: DTC P2BBE - Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Position Exceeded Learning Limit
problem_description: P2BBE is not a wiring fault but a failed end-stop learn. GM's 2019 tables for the LT5 Corvette ZR1 describe how the electronic recirculation valve is taught after each engine shutdown: the module first drives it to the closed stop and stores the sensor value, then repeats this for the open stop. If the learned closed value falls outside 85–95 % of the sensor range, or the learned open value outside 10–20 %, the code sets at once (Type A, MIL in one trip). The learn only runs while no position-sensor or valve-circuit fault is active. Typical causes are carbon or oil deposits, a bent flap or shaft, a worn actuator gear or a sensor that has shifted. Since the learn needs a key-off, a repair is only confirmed after a full shutdown. Circuit faults of the same sensor are P2BBB to P2BBD.

Position sensor shifted or drifted after a repair or with age (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P2BBF - Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Supply Voltage Low
problem_description: P2BBF concerns the power side of bypass valve A rather than its position feedback. Electric recirculation valves are moved by a small DC motor fed through an H-bridge in the engine module, and the bridge chip itself flags when its supply drops too far. GM documents exactly this for the eCRV of the 2019 Corvette ZR1: the motor driver reports low voltage in 80 of 100 samples at 12.5 ms, with relay voltage at least 11 V and the engine not cranking; Type A, MIL at once. Data sheets for throttle-type H-bridges such as NXP's MC33926 show how such an output stage switches off below its undervoltage lockout and reports this on a status line. Causes are a weak feed, a poor module ground or connector, or an internal driver fault. Without drive power the valve stays where it last stopped.

Often accompanied by other low-voltage codes

Corroded pins at the engine module or valve connector (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P2BC0 - Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Driver Current/Temperature Too High

P2BBF is the low-supply case of the same driver, P00D7 an overheated valve itself. The valve stops responding and boost is reduced.

title: DTC P2BEC - Fuel Control System A Too Lean Bank 1
problem_description: Engines that combine port and direct injection keep separate fuel trim adaptations for each injection mode. Ford, which uses this code on its PFDI engines such as the 2.7 L EcoBoost and 5.0 L V8 of the F-150, assigns system A to the direct-injection mode. A lean bank 1 in every mode would give P0171 instead. Suspects are therefore parts used only by DI: too little rail pressure because the high-pressure pump underdelivers, or restricted direct injectors. Ford also reflashes the PCM for it (20-2324, 22-2393).

title: DTC P2C04 - Fuel Pressure Regulator D Control Circuit High
problem_description: P2C04 covers the opposite electrical fault to P2C03: the switched ground end of the regulator D circuit is connected to battery voltage. title: DTC P2C11 - Reductant Pump A Current Too Low
problem_description: P2C11 watches the electric motor of the DEF (AdBlue) pump from the other side than P214E: its driver output carries less current than a working motor should draw, which points to an open winding, a poor plug contact or a motor spinning freely or not at all. Only GM documents it publicly, in its 2025 diesel tables (25OBDG04A/B): the DEF control module flags under 0.75 A while the pump is used as a heater for frozen fluid, and under 0.5 A during priming and normal running. Failures over 4 s within 400 samples set it as Type A, so the MIL comes on after one trip, and the code only heals in the next drive cycle. While it is active the pump is stopped, no fluid is dosed and the SCR catalyst loses its NOx conversion; the exhaust fluid warning follows.

Loose, corroded or spread terminals at the pump connector (likelihood: medium)
Open or high-resistance control or low-reference wire between control module and pump (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P2C2E - Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve B Supply Voltage Low
problem_description: P2C2E concerns the power stage of compressor bypass valve B, not its position signal. Such valves are moved by a small DC motor driven through an H-bridge, and the bridge reports when its own supply sags below a safe level. No manufacturer documents the B-side code publicly. GM's 2019 LT5 tables describe the equivalent for valve A (P2BBF): the motor driver flags low voltage in 80 of 100 checks spaced 12.5 ms apart, enabled at relay voltage of at least 11 V without cranking, Type A. NXP's MC33926 data sheet shows how a bridge of this kind disables its outputs under undervoltage and signals the fault. A weak battery feed, a poor module ground, a corroded relay or an internal driver fault are typical causes; the valve then remains in its last position.
symptoms: Check engine light
Valve no longer responds, boost reduced
Often accompanied by other low-voltage codes
possible_causes: Weak battery or voltage drop on the module feed (likelihood: high)
Poor ground or corroded relay contacts in the supply (likelihood: medium)
Internal fault of the H-bridge driver (likelihood: low)

Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: turbo bypass valve b, wiring harness, ecm.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-3 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Weak battery or voltage drop on the module feed (likelihood: high).

title: DTC P2C2F - Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve B Driver Current/Temperature Too High
problem_description: P2C2F is stored when the output stage driving compressor bypass valve B signals excessive current or overheating. The motor driver protects itself by limiting current and finally switching off, and reports this to the engine module. No manufacturer documents P2C2F; GM documents the A-side code P2BC0 for the supercharged 2019 LT5: a raised driver flag in 80 of 100 checks at 12.5 ms, with relay voltage of 11 V or more and no cranking, gives a Type A fault. NXP's MC33926 bridge, a typical part for such loads, regulates overcurrent and shuts down on overtemperature. Excess current mostly stems from a jammed valve working against its stop, a shorted motor winding or touching motor leads. Valve B overheating itself is P00D8; low supply to the same driver is P2C2E.

title: DTC P2C30 - Ignition Coil Primary Circuit Fuse A
problem_description: On engines whose ignition coils are fed through more than one fuse, the module checks each fuse so that it notices when a whole group of coils loses power. Expect MIL, misfire and hesitation. Which cylinders fuse A serves is not published.
