title: DTC P2C32 - Crankcase Pressure Sensor B Circuit
problem_description: A crankcase pressure sensor tells the engine module how the pressure in the crankcase ventilation compares with ambient, mainly so it can detect a disconnected or leaking breather line. P2C32 is the general circuit fault of sensor B: its signal is missing or cannot be decoded at all, without saying high or low. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Ford shows the pattern for sensor A: on digital SENT sensors, invalid frames or signal patterns set P051A within 5 s, while analogue sensors report the range, low and high codes. Maserati lists the B codes P2C33–P2C35 for the blow-by sensor of its 2021 V6 and V8, but not P2C32. CARB requires the ventilation system to be monitored; with the sensor down that check cannot run, so the MIL is to be expected.

Usually no change in driveability

Sensor electronics failed (likelihood: medium)
Engine module input or software fault (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2C36 - Crankcase Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

title: DTC P2C37 - Cold Start Engine Coolant Pump Performance
problem_description: Engines with a switchable or electric main coolant pump often keep the coolant still, or nearly so, right after a cold start so the cylinder head and catalyst warm up sooner. P2C37 reports that the pump did not behave as commanded during this cold-start phase, for example running when it should rest or failing to start when flow is requested. California rules require separate codes for faults detected during a cold-start strategy and ask makers of electric water pumps to submit a monitoring plan of their own. No manufacturer documents P2C37 publicly. An Audi patent shows one way to judge such a pump: once it is switched back on, the measured head temperature is checked against a model value derived from coolant temperature. Related are P2DE9/P2E82 (cold-start under- and overspeed) and P26CB.

title: DTC P2C3C - Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

title: DTC P2C4A - Clutch Actuator Position Sensor Circuit
problem_description: The clutch actuator position sensor reports how far the release mechanism of an automated or partly automated clutch has travelled, taken at the slave cylinder or inside the actuator rather than at the pedal. Typical designs are Hall sensors reading a magnet on the clutch piston. P2C4A is the general circuit fault of this sensor. Ford reports it in two ways: its 2024 OBD summary uses P2C4A as the base code behind the low and high faults P2C4C/P2C4D (failure types 11 and 12), and lists P2C4A_48 under P166F as an internal module check of the clutch actuation position, without MIL on manual gearboxes with stop in gear. Range, low, high and erratic faults have separate codes P2C4B–P2C4E. Without a valid signal the controller cannot judge clutch state, so start-stop or automated clutch functions are switched off.

Automated clutch may refuse to engage or drive off

Position sensor on slave cylinder or actuator failed (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P2C52 - Cylinder 1 Fuel Injector B Offset Learning At Min Limit
problem_description: Engines with two injectors per cylinder call the second one injector B; with port plus direct injection that is usually one of the two sets, but which one is the maker's choice. No manufacturer publishes this exact code; Volvo's Technical Journal 36016 names only the Max partner P2C53.

title: DTC P2C79 - NOx Adsorber - Sulfur Limit Exceeded

title: DTC P2C83 - Cold Start Shift Time Too Short

title: DTC P2C90 - Crankcase Ventilation System - Hose A Disconnected
problem_description: Under California's phase-in (20 % of 2023, 50 % of 2024, all 2025 models) every PCV hose carrying crankcase vapour must be watched for a break as large as its smallest bore, so makers moved from the general P04DB to per-hose codes. P2C90 covers hose A. Ford's 2024 summary says P2C90 replaces P04DB: the dirty side is tested once per trip while cranking, the clean side once per trip above 5 lb/min airflow, backed by extrapolation and flow-model checks over up to 15 minutes. Bulletins come from Ford (2024 F-150 3.5 and 5.2, 2026 Transit 3.5: PCV check plus software), Toyota and Lexus (2023 Crown, RX 500h: false codes, ECM logic changed) and Stellantis (Jeep 2.0 turbo; Wagoneer 3.0 with a too short make-up-air valve spring).
symptoms: Engine warning lamp, often without any other complaint
Oil mist or oily residue near the disconnected hose
Possibly unstable idle or lean mixture codes
possible_causes: PCV hose A pulled off, cracked or with a broken fitting (likelihood: high)
Detection software too sensitive (Ford, Toyota/Lexus and Stellantis updates) (likelihood: high)
PCV valve or make-up-air check valve not sealing (likelihood: medium)
Crankcase pressure sensor or its signal faulty (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2C90 (Crankcase Ventilation System - Hose A Disconnected).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: crankcase vent hose a, crankcase pressure sensor, intake manifold.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: DIY feasible. Estimated labor time: 0.2-1.5 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: PCV hose A pulled off, cracked or with a broken fitting (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Detection software too sensitive (Ford, Toyota/Lexus and Stellantis updates) (likelihood: high).
Clear diagnostic trouble codes with scanner after component repair and perform a verification test drive.
source: OBDex / SAE J2012 & ISO 15031-6 Open Diagnostic Standard

title: DTC P2C91 - Crankcase Ventilation System - Hose B Disconnected
problem_description: P2C91 is the second hose-specific PCV disconnection code: crankcase vapour line B is detected as open or broken, separately from line A (P2C90). Which physical hose carries the letter is the maker's choice; the code slot exists so that systems with two monitored lines can name the faulty one. The documented user is Stellantis on the Alfa Romeo Giulia and Stelvio (2021–22) with the 2.9-litre twin-turbo V6. Their two engine computers were reflashed in bulletins of 2023 and 2025 because P2C91 appeared together with crankcase pressure sensor B faults (P2C33) without a real leak. A hose that is genuinely loose lets oil mist or unmetered air escape, can upset idle and fuel trims, and keeps the lamp lit. Since 2025 every hose of this kind must be monitored, which is why such second codes appear.

Oil residue or hissing at a crankcase ventilation hose
Possibly rough idle

Crankcase pressure sensor B or its wiring faulty (likelihood: medium)

title: DTC P2C92 - Hybrid/EV Battery Contactor Control Supply Circuit/Open
problem_description: The main contactors of a traction battery are relays whose coils are energised by driver stages in the battery controller, and those drivers take their energy from a dedicated supply feed. P2C92 means this feed is missing or interrupted, for example because of a blown fuse, a broken wire or a feed relay that does not pull in. Why the feed is watched at all is explained in LG Energy Solution patent US12007445B2: a coil voltage that is too weak or not yet settled can leave a contactor only partly closed, so the controller checks the supply before closing each contactor and declares a fault after repeated failed checks. No manufacturer documents P2C92 publicly. With the feed gone, no contactor can close, so the car typically refuses ready mode and charging. CARB requires monitoring of hybrid components.
symptoms: Vehicle does not become ready to drive
Charging does not start
Hybrid or EV system warning
possible_causes: Fuse in the contactor supply feed blown (likelihood: high)
Supply wire or connector at the battery pack interrupted (likelihood: medium)
Relay or switch feeding the contactor drivers not closing (likelihood: medium)
Battery controller input or driver stage defective (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2C92 (Hybrid/EV Battery Contactor Control Supply Circuit/Open).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: hybrid battery contactor control supply, wiring harness, bms.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-6 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Fuse in the contactor supply feed blown (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Supply wire or connector at the battery pack interrupted (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

title: DTC P2C93 - Hybrid/EV Battery Contactor Control Supply Circuit Range/Performance
problem_description: With P2C93 the supply for the contactor drivers is present but does not behave as it should: it sags when a coil is switched on, ripples, or recovers too slowly before the next contactor in the closing sequence. A high-resistance contact or a weak feed therefore shows up here rather than as an open circuit. LG Energy Solution patent US12007445B2 describes the matching logic: before every contactor closes, the controller compares the supply with a minimum, waits and repeats the comparison if it is short, and only after a set number of failed tries records a supply fault. No manufacturer documents P2C93 publicly. For the driver the effect is often intermittent: the car may need several attempts to become ready or abort charging. CARB requires functional checks of hybrid components.
symptoms: Several attempts needed before the vehicle is ready
Charging stops unexpectedly
Intermittent hybrid or EV warning
possible_causes: Corroded or loose contact in the supply feed causing voltage drop (likelihood: high)
Weak 12 V battery or ground connection sagging under coil load (likelihood: medium)
Contactor coil drawing excessive current or driver stage faulty (likelihood: low)

Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: hybrid battery contactor control supply, wiring harness, bms.

Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.

title: DTC P2C94 - Hybrid/EV Battery Contactor Control Supply Circuit Low
problem_description: P2C94 says the supply feeding the contactor drivers lies below its lower limit. Ford is the maker that documents it: special service messages 51513 and 51783 (2023) describe 2021–2023 Escape, Corsair, Aviator, Mustang Mach-E, F-150 and Transit plug-in models whose AC charging at level 1 or 2 stops with the MIL on and P2C94 logged in the SOBDM, the on-board charger module. As a stopgap the charge handle is unplugged and reconnected; a new SOBDM does not help. TSB 23-2399, extended by 24-2027 to the 2023 E-Transit, blames SOBDM software and cures it by reprogramming. Ford does not say which supply it measures. On other vehicles a genuinely low feed, as described in patent US12007445B2, can stop contactors closing fully. Compare P2C95 for the high side.

title: DTC P2C95 - Hybrid/EV Battery Contactor Control Supply Circuit High
problem_description: P2C95 is the upper-limit counterpart of P2C94: the voltage on the feed for the contactor coil drivers exceeds what the battery controller accepts. An excessive supply is less common than a weak one, but it heats the coils and stresses the driver transistors, and it can mean the measurement is wrong, for instance when the sense line touches a higher potential or the feed regulator inside the controller has failed. LG Energy Solution patent US12007445B2 shows that controllers measure this supply before each contactor closes; an upper limit is the logical extension, although the patent itself deals with undervoltage. No manufacturer documents P2C95 publicly. Depending on strategy the controller may refuse to close contactors or open them, so loss of ready mode is possible. CARB requires monitoring of hybrid components.

title: DTC P2C96 - Hybrid/EV Battery Disable Circuit/Open
problem_description: Besides commands over the vehicle network, many high-voltage batteries have a separate wired input through which another controller can force the contactors open. The best-known use is the crash signal: in Volkswagen patent US9586481B2 the battery opens its contactor 10–100 ms after a hard-wired crash signal, versus roughly 20–200 ms when the message arrives over CAN, and blocks reclosing until the stored fault has been erased. Coda patent US20110304202A1 also ties battery disconnection to the airbag deployment decision. What exactly feeds the disable line is up to the maker. P2C96 means this line is open. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. Many designs read a lost signal as a shutdown request, so the car may not become ready. CARB requires monitoring of hybrid components.

title: DTC P2C97 - Hybrid/EV Battery Disable Circuit Low
problem_description: P2C97 is set when the high-voltage battery's wired disable input sits below its valid range, typically because the line is chafed through to body ground or the sending module pulls it low permanently. Whether low means shut down depends on the design. Where the line is active-low, a short to ground looks like a constant request to open the contactors, and the battery stays switched off; where a defined level is expected, the controller simply loses a trustworthy signal. The safety value of a hard-wired path is shown in Volkswagen patent US9586481B2, where it opens the contactor faster than a CAN message. No manufacturer documents P2C97 publicly. A shorted line should be traced section by section between the sender and the battery connector. CARB requires monitoring of hybrid components.

title: DTC P2C98 - Hybrid/EV Battery Disable Circuit High
problem_description: P2C98 flags a battery disable line whose level is above the permitted range, usually through a short to 12 V or a sender that drives the line too high. Unlike the low case, the risk here can be hidden: if a high level means all clear, a stuck-high line would no longer pass on a real shutdown request. That is the point of such a wire in Volkswagen patent US9586481B2, which lets a crash signal open the contactor within 10–100 ms, and in Coda patent US20110304202A1, which disconnects the battery once airbag deployment is decided. The controller therefore flags the line even while driving seems normal; the CAN path normally remains as a backup. No manufacturer documents P2C98 publicly. CARB requires monitoring of hybrid components. Inspect the line for contact with feed wires.

title: DTC P2C99 - Throttle Actuator A Control Exceeded Learning Limit
problem_description: An electronic throttle relies on learned values: the closed-stop position of its sensors and, in many systems, a correction that widens the commanded opening as carbon narrows the bore. P2C99 says a learned value for throttle A has run into its permitted limit, so the module can no longer compensate. No manufacturer publishes P2C99. GM shows both ideas elsewhere: its 2023 tables (23OBDG07) fail the lower-stop learn of throttle sensor bank 1 with in-house codes P30E3/P30E4 within one trip, and GM patents cap the learned throttle area correction and report how near it is to that cap as a coking value. Heavy deposits, a worn or replaced throttle body without relearn, or drifting sensors are typical. Idle may be unstable and power reduced. P2176 is the related idle-position code.

Idle speed too high, too low or hunting
Reduced power in a throttle emergency mode

Throttle body cleaned or replaced without resetting and relearning the adaptation (likelihood: medium)
Worn throttle shaft, plate or end stop shifting the closed position (likelihood: medium)
Throttle position sensor drifting (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2C9A - Throttle Actuator B Control Exceeded Learning Limit
problem_description: Throttle B exists only on engines with two electronically driven throttle bodies, usually one per cylinder bank on large V engines. P2C9A means a learned value of that second throttle – its closed-stop reference or the airflow correction stored for it – has reached the edge of the allowed range. Since both throttles must deliver matching air, a large learned offset on one side alone hints at deposits, a sticking plate or a replaced unit on that side. No manufacturer documents P2C9A. GM's 2023 tables handle the bank 2 throttle sensor with separate in-house codes (P30E5/P30E6) for the same stop-learn limit, judged within one trip. Expect rough or uneven idle, limited power if the module restricts the throttle, and possibly companion codes such as P218A (idle position of throttle B not learned).

title: DTC P2C9B - Cold Start Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A Range/Performance
problem_description: P2C9B checks wastegate A while the engine runs its catalyst warm-up strategy after a cold start, when the wastegate is commanded open so hot exhaust reaches the catalyst rather than the turbine. GM uses the code on the 2.7-litre L3B (table 19OBDG03D): it fails if the position error stays above 20 % for over 1 s, the actuator current above 1 A or the duty cycle above 40 %, judged on 25 of 30 samples at 100 ms; Type A, MIL after one trip. The 2025 table 25OBDG03B tightens the position limit to 10 % over 2 s (29 of 30). In the 19OBDG07 table for GM's twin-turbo 4.2-litre V8 the code flags a bank 1 bypass valve that sticks longer than 1 s during rapid heat-up. Causes are a stiff flap or linkage, a weak electric actuator or wiring. P2B81 covers the actuator outside cold start; P2C9C is turbo B.

Often no noticeable change in performance

title: DTC P2C9D - Fuel Pressure Regulator C Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too High
problem_description: P2C9D reports that the fuel pressure in the section governed by regulator C stays above its target although that regulator is already reducing delivery as far as it can. A third regulator letter is only needed where an engine has several pressure control elements, for instance two high-pressure pumps or separate rail circuits. No manufacturer documents P2C9D publicly. The closest published logic is GM's for regulators A and D (tables 23OBDG07 and 24OBDG07): measured and desired rail pressure may differ by no more than 3 MPa for a few seconds before a one-trip fault is stored. CARB demands a fault once fuel pressure control runs out of authority. Expect a hard, noisy idle or reduced power; P2C9E covers the underpressure side of the same regulator.

title: DTC P2C9E - Fuel Pressure Regulator C Exceeded Control Limits - Pressure Too Low
problem_description: P2C9E is the underpressure counterpart of P2C9D: the circuit run by regulator C cannot reach its pressure target even with the regulator already asking for full delivery. title: DTC P2CE7 - Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor C Circuit Low
problem_description: P2CE7 means the raw signal of filter pressure sensor C has dropped below its electrical floor, the typical picture of a signal wire shorted to ground or a lost 5 V supply. title: DTC P2CFF - A/C Clutch Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
problem_description: P2CFF does not come from a voltage comparison but from the protective logic of the clutch output itself. No manufacturer documents P2CFF publicly; Ford, which powers the field coil from body control module C, only names P2CFC and P2CFD. Plain open, low and high faults are P2CFC to P2CFE. The clutch drops out repeatedly or stays disengaged, so cooling cuts in and out.

title: DTC P2D20 - Reductant System Flow - Blocked
problem_description: P2D20 is the hard verdict after P2D1F: no measurable DEF passes, so the pump keeps pressure but nothing reaches the exhaust. A public manufacturer description of P2D20 does not exist; GM's 2025 diesel tables flag the matching symptom under P20E9 when DEF pressure stays more than 63 kPa above its setpoint for 4 s during closed loop control (Type A). Ford's 2023 diesels check flow plausibility under P218F and the dosing valve itself under P208E, stuck closed. California requires the delivery system to be monitored because without reductant the SCR catalyst stops reducing NOx. Frozen fluid, a fully crystallised nozzle or a closed valve are typical. Expect a fast countdown to reduced speed.
symptoms: Check engine light and DEF warning, often in frost
Countdown to speed limitation or start inhibit
Follow-up NOx efficiency codes
possible_causes: Dosing valve stuck closed or nozzle fully crystallised (likelihood: high)
Frozen DEF in line or valve due to a failed line heater (likelihood: medium)
Crushed or fully kinked DEF line (likelihood: medium)
Pump filter completely blocked by deposits (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code P2D20 (Reductant System Flow - Blocked).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: reductant lines, reductant injector, reductant pump, scr module.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-3 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Dosing valve stuck closed or nozzle fully crystallised (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Frozen DEF in line or valve due to a failed line heater (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.
source: OBDex / SAE J2012 & ISO 15031-6 Open Diagnostic Standard

title: DTC P2D21 - Turbocharger Interstage Pressure Sensor A Circuit
problem_description: Engines with two turbochargers in series can measure the pressure between the low-pressure and the high-pressure compressor. GM's patent on two-stage boost control uses this mid-stage value to split the pressure ratio between both stages and to steer the low-pressure wastegate; Cummins describes the same sensor between the stages and the intercooler. P2D21 is the general circuit code: the module rejects the signal but does not assign it to the low, high or erratic codes. No manufacturer documents P2D21 publicly. California requires input sensors to be checked for circuit faults and boost systems for under- and overboost. Single-turbo engines never set it. Expect reduced boost and power.

Reduced power, boost held to a safe value
Sluggish response while accelerating

Failed interstage pressure sensor (likelihood: medium)
Shared 5 V sensor supply faulty (likelihood: low)

Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.

title: DTC P2D22 - Turbocharger Interstage Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
problem_description: P2D22 flags an interstage pressure reading that is electrically valid but implausible, for instance offset, stuck or out of step with the other pressures. No manufacturer documents a detection rule. A Cummins patent on a two-stage engine shows what plausible means: with the compressor bypass valve open, interstage and charge pressure should be almost the same, about 102 kPa at 600 rpm and 119 kPa at 2,000 rpm; a service test compares both speeds, and if charge pressure and turbo speed check out while a code is stored, the interstage sensor is the suspect. California requires rationality checks for such inputs. A sensor that reads wrong can mislead the boost split between the stages.

Uneven boost build-up or reduced power
Possible boost deviation codes alongside

Stage bypass valve stuck, giving pressures the model does not expect (likelihood: low)

Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: turbo interstage pressure sensor a, wiring harness, ecm.

Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.

title: DTC P2D23 - Turbocharger Interstage Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
problem_description: P2D23 says the interstage pressure signal sits below the lowest voltage a working sensor can produce. Typical causes are a signal wire shorted to ground, a lost 5 V supply or an internal sensor short. No public table gives a threshold for this sensor; for comparison, Ford's 2023 diesels treat a DEF pressure sensor below 0.2 V as circuit low. The sensor itself sits between the two compressors of a series turbo system, as GM's two-stage control patent describes, where its value guides the low-pressure stage. California requires out-of-range checks on every such input. With the value missing, the controller usually falls back to a model and caps boost. A high reading is P2D24.

Further codes if the shared sensor supply is affected

title: DTC P2D24 - Turbocharger Interstage Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
problem_description: P2D24 is the opposite case to P2D23: the interstage pressure signal is pinned near or above the top of its range. On a three-wire sensor this usually points to an open ground, a signal wire touching the 5 V reference or battery voltage, or an open signal line pulled up inside the controller. Ford's 2023 diesels, as a comparable pressure sensor example, set circuit high above 4.85 V. No manufacturer documents P2D24 or its threshold. Cummins places the sensor between the low- and high-pressure stages ahead of the charge air cooler. California requires out-of-range monitoring. A falsely high value can make the controller think the low-pressure stage overboosts and cut its output.

title: DTC P2D25 - Turbocharger Interstage Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

California requires input sensors to be monitored for faults, and the boost system for slow response. Vibration and heat near the turbochargers make loose terminals and cracked insulation the leading suspects; a wiggle test while watching live data usually finds them.

title: DTC P2D26 - Coolant Pump E Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
problem_description: P2D26 belongs to the general auxiliary coolant pumps, not to the motor electronics family above: pump E is the fifth electric pump of a vehicle, and its assignment (low-temperature loop, charge air cooler, turbo or component cooling) depends entirely on the manufacturer. The code says the control circuit is intact but the pump does not run or does not deliver the expected effect. No manufacturer publicly documents P2D26. GM's diesel tables show the method on pump C (P2C48): they compute the phase current expected at the measured speed and set a type B fault after about 5 s outside the window. Ford's 2024 summary handles performance/stuck off (fault type 92) for its pumps continuously above 11 V. A seized rotor, air, a weak motor or wiring resistance are typical. Electrical faults on pump E have their own codes from P2DF4.

Possible reduced power, depending on what pump E cools

title: DTC P2D27 - Coolant Pump F Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
problem_description: P2D27 is the functional check for coolant pump F, the sixth auxiliary pump in the lettering scheme and thus only relevant on vehicles with very many electric pumps, typically plug-in hybrids, electric vehicles or heavy diesels with several separate loops. The control line answers, yet the pump stays off or falls short of what the module expects from speed, current or temperature response. No manufacturer publicly documents P2D27, and unlike pump E no further pump F fault codes appear in common code lists. Published logic exists only for siblings: GM's 2025 diesel table judges pump C (P2C48) by comparing phase current with speed above 2,800 rpm, 10 failures out of 12, type B. Ford's 2024 gasoline summary watches its pumps A and B (P2601, P261B) for 5 s from 11 V. Check the loop, then pump and wiring.

title: DTC P2D28 - Cold Start Propulsion Torque Performance
problem_description: P2D28 concerns the torque side of a cold start strategy. To heat the catalyst, the engine control asks for a torque reserve: spark is retarded and airflow raised so the wheels still get the requested torque while extra heat goes into the exhaust. A GM patent describes this, with a heat estimate turned into a reserve request that enters the propulsion torque calculation. The code means the torque delivered or commanded in this phase strayed from what the strategy planned. CARB allows cold start heating to be judged by the last commanded reserve of torque over the first 30 s at idle. Stellantis lists P2D28 for the 2026 Dodge Charger with the 3.0 l Sixpack engine; bulletin 18-022-26 says it was set falsely through a non-robust monitor and is cured by PCM software. P032F is the general low torque code.
symptoms: Check engine light shortly after a cold start
Hesitant or uneven pull while the engine is still cold
Often no noticeable symptom when the cause is software
possible_causes: Engine control software with a monitor that sets the code without a real fault (likelihood: high)
Throttle, intake leak or airflow error, so retarded spark cannot be balanced by more air (likelihood: medium)
Misfires or weak ignition while spark is heavily retarded (likelihood: medium)
Implausible temperature or speed input to the torque model (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2D29 - A/C Compressor Motor Stalled
problem_description: Hybrids and electric vehicles drive the A/C compressor with its own high-voltage motor and inverter. P2D29 reports that this motor is commanded to turn but does not rotate. No manufacturer documents P2D29 publicly. GM's 2019 hybrid tables cover a related check under its own code P1F0A: the filtered gap between commanded and fed-back compressor speed must stay inside limits while 960 to 8,600 rpm is requested, high-side pressure is below 2,800 kPa and pack voltage above 270 V; failure is Type B. A Tecumseh patent explains why current alone misses a stall and why high head pressure right after shutdown can hold the rotor. Without the compressor, cabin and often battery cooling are lost.

Compressor phase current or overload codes stored alongside

title: DTC P2D2A - Hybrid/EV Electronics Coolant Temperature Sensor A/B Correlation
problem_description: Some drives measure the coolant of the inverter and power electronics loop at two points. After a long rest both should read nearly the same, so P2D2A records that sensors A and B disagree by more than the allowed margin; the code does not say which one is wrong. No manufacturer documents P2D2A publicly. GM's 2019 hybrid tables run the idea with one sensor and other references under P0CEF: after at least 3,600 s with compressor, pump and propulsion off, the electronics coolant reading must stay within 27 °C of outside air or transmission fluid, or 28 °C of a refrigerant-based value (Type B). CARB requires inputs of inverter thermal management to be monitored.

title: DTC P2D2B - Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Temperature Sensor A/B Correlation
problem_description: Liquid-cooled traction batteries often have coolant sensors at pack inlet and outlet. title: DTC P2D2C - Engine Coolant Temperature Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation
problem_description: Engines with split or map-controlled cooling carry several coolant sensors, for example at head, block, inlet, outlet, radiator and heater core. GM's 2025 tables do the comparison under P0116 instead: once per valid cold start the coolant sensor is checked against two others from a configurable list that also includes oil, intake and outside air, Type B over two trips. title: DTC P2D2D - Cold Start Intake Manifold Runner Performance Bank 1
problem_description: P2D2D reports that the intake manifold runner or swirl flaps of bank 1 did not reach the position the cold start strategy asked for. Many engines hold these flaps in a special setting after a cold start to stir the charge and stabilise combustion while the catalyst warms up. CARB names intake runner, charge motion and swirl valves among the features that must respond to their cold start command, robustly and beyond what they would do without the strategy. The outside-cold-start counterpart is P200A. Stellantis uses P2D2D on the 2020 Ram 1500 with the 3.0 l EcoDiesel Gen 3 and eight-speed automatic: bulletins 18-008-21 and 18-002-23 list it with P2D2E and remedy it with new PCM software. Beyond software, a stiff flap shaft, a carbon-coated runner or a weak actuator are typical reasons.

Slightly rougher idle in the first minutes after a cold start

Flap shaft or runner coated with soot and oil deposits, stiff when cold (likelihood: medium)
Worn actuator or loose linkage on bank 1 (likelihood: medium)
Position sensor signal or wiring fault (likelihood: low)

title: DTC P2D2E - Cold Start Intake Manifold Runner Performance Bank 2
problem_description: P2D2E is the bank 2 version of the cold start runner check, so it only appears on V or boxer engines whose second cylinder row has its own flaps or actuator. The module compares the position commanded for the cold start phase with the feedback from that bank and flags a flap that stays short of target. Both FCA bulletins for the 2020 Ram 1500 3.0 l EcoDiesel V6 (18-008-21, 18-002-23) list it together with P2D2D, and the cure is a PCM reflash; when both banks report at once, software or a shared supply is more likely than two failing flaps. If only bank 2 is stored, inspect that side's shaft, linkage and connector. CARB demands the check for charge motion and swirl valves during cold starts; outside that window the same fault is P200B.

title: DTC P2D39 - Forced Hybrid/EV Battery Disconnect

title: DTC P2D3C - Cold Start Hybrid/EV Drive Motor Performance
problem_description: In a hybrid the electric drive motor can be part of the strategy that cuts emissions after a cold start, and P2D3C says it did not perform as that strategy required. CARB demands separate diagnostics for elements of the cold start strategy that are also monitored in normal operation, so a motor fault found during warm-up is kept apart from the general P0A90. No manufacturer documents P2D3C publicly. GM patent US8838316B2 explains the role: the motor drives the car and spins the unfuelled engine to roughly 1,000 to 1,800 rpm, ideally 1,200 to 1,400 rpm, so it can light off the catalyst with retarded spark; if the motor cannot cover the driver's request within its limits, the strategy is abandoned. A motor that falls short therefore costs catalyst heating and raises cold start emissions. Look for further motor, inverter or battery codes.

Engine starts earlier or runs rougher after a cold start than usual
Often no noticeable change in driving

title: DTC P2D3E - Cold Start Hybrid/EV Battery Performance
problem_description: P2D3E states that the traction battery could not support the cold start emission strategy as planned, typically because it could not deliver the power the strategy relied on. title: DTC P2D51 - Air Assisted Injector Control Circuit
problem_description: P2D51 is the general electrical code for the control circuit of an air-assist injection system, the circuit counterpart to P0065 to P0067. Assist air flowing around the injector tip breaks the fuel spray into finer droplets. In Ford's patented layout the air bypasses the throttle and is metered by a solenoid valve that the engine computer drives with a pulse-width signal, so a circuit fault concerns this valve, its wiring or the driver stage. Another Ford patent shows a passive variant in which only a shroud on the injector meters the air and nothing electrical can fail. No manufacturer documents P2D51 publicly. Without the valve, atomisation suffers mainly at idle and in cold starts. Low and high: P0066, P0067. Air-assisted DEF dosing uses separate reductant codes such as P2059.

title: DTC P2D86 - Fuel Temperature Sensor A/B Correlation

title: DTC P2D94 - Starter/Generator Phase Z Current Sensor Circuit High
problem_description: P2D94 completes the high-side series: the phase Z current sensor of the starter/generator outputs a value above its valid window. Inverters for 48 V starter/generators are built for three- or six-phase machines, and the controller relies on measured phase currents to set torque for engine restarts, boost and energy recovery. CARB's OBD rule requires input components, including the hybrid parts a manufacturer has to monitor, to detect wiring faults and readings outside the plausible range; a high-side code like this one is such an out-of-range finding. No manufacturer documents P2D94 publicly. Typical finds are a pinched lead or a loose plug at the machine, moisture in the electronics or a sensor defect, which often means replacing the starter/generator assembly. P2D97 is the low counterpart, P2D9A the intermittent fault.

title: DTC P2D95 - Starter/Generator Phase X Current Sensor Circuit Low

title: DTC P2DAE - Drive Motor A Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low

Winding probes are mostly NTC thermistors whose resistance collapses as they heat – Thinking Electronic quotes roughly 0.46 kOhm at 180 °C for its stator probes – so with the usual pull-up circuit a near-zero voltage would read as an impossibly hot winding. In practice it points to a short: signal lead to ground or to the motor housing, a shorted thermistor, or a lead pinched during assembly. On the 2023 Outlander PHEV, Mitsubishi's own code P3053 catches its V-phase probe when the signal stays at or under 0.1 V for half a second, provided the power drive unit has at least 8 V. No manufacturer documents P2DAE publicly. P2DAF is the opposite fault; real overheating would be P0A2F.

title: DTC P2DB1 - Drive Motor A Temperature Sensor C Circuit
problem_description: P2DB1 reports a circuit fault on a third temperature sensor (C) in drive motor A. title: DTC P2DCE - Control Pilot Charging Switch B Circuit/Open
problem_description: P2DCE reports an open or otherwise faulty control circuit of charging switch B, a vehicle-side switch on the control pilot line. Under SAE J1772 the car first loads the pilot with about 2.74 kΩ, pulling the 12 V supplied by the station down to roughly 9 V; closing a charging switch puts another 1.3 kΩ in parallel, the level falls to about 6 V and the station energises the cable. title: DTC P2DDD - Fuel Injection Quantity C Higher Than Expected
problem_description: P2DDD flags excess fuel from injection path C: the quantity really burned, as estimated from airflow and lambda, sits above the request. Besides the classic leaking injector, a possible trigger after repairs is a replacement injector whose individual flow code was not programmed into the engine control, so the module calculates with the wrong flow curve. Another is an EGR valve that leaves too little fresh air, which the estimate can read as surplus fuel. GM lets its system-A adaptation take away only about 8 to 14 mm³, depending on speed and load. No manufacturer documents P2DDD publicly. P2DDC is the shortfall in path C, P2DE1 the cold-start excess; smoke and higher consumption are what drivers notice.

Dark smoke under load
Higher fuel consumption

title: DTC P2DDF - Fuel Injection Quantity D Higher Than Expected

The estimate behind it depends heavily on the air side: if the airflow meter reports too little air, or the NOx or oxygen sensor shows a richer lambda than real, the module sees a surplus that the injectors never delivered, so sensors deserve a check before injectors are replaced. title: DTC P2DE0 - Cold Start Fuel Injection Quantity C Lower Than Expected

title: DTC P2DE4 - Drive Motor A Clutch Stuck Engaged
problem_description: Some hybrids and electric drive units can uncouple electric drive motor A from its axle through a clutch, so the motor stops turning when its torque is not needed. P2DE4 means the clutch stays closed although the control module has asked it to open; position feedback or speeds still show a coupled motor. No manufacturer documents P2DE4 publicly. Comparable hardware sits in the front drive unit of the 2024 Corvette E-Ray, which has a clutch pawl, a disconnect clutch actuator and a position switch; GM logs a faulty switch there as P08ED. A Schaeffler design for such a disconnect is spring-loaded towards the engaged state and needs current to release, so a dead actuator leaves it coupled. The motor is then dragged along, costing efficiency, and the system may restrict operation. The opposite fault is P2DE5.

title: DTC P2DE5 - Drive Motor A Clutch Stuck Disengaged

title: DTC P2DEB - Cylinder 2 Intake Valve Lift Range/Performance
problem_description: P2DEB singles out cylinder 2: its intake valve lift misses the target or follows a command too late. Lift control for each cylinder separately is the hallmark of electro-hydraulic systems like Fiat's MultiAir, sold by Schaeffler as UniAir: per cylinder, a solenoid decides how much of the cam stroke is passed through an oil-filled chamber to the intake valves; once it opens, the link collapses and a spring takes over. title: DTC P2DEC - Cylinder 3 Intake Valve Lift Range/Performance

title: DTC P2DFA - Coolant Pump E Supply Voltage Circuit

title: DTC P2E2B - Drive Motor A Excitation Current Too High

problem_description: P2E44 is the opposite fault: the command line of electronics coolant pump B reads higher than its commanded state allows, mostly because it touches a battery-fed wire or the driver can no longer pull it down. Many PWM pumps react to a permanently high input with an emergency mode; Pierburg's interface runs the pump at about 95 % speed for a duty cycle of 98 to 100 %. The loop may therefore stay cooled while the controller has lost all influence on the speed, which also wastes energy and adds noise. Ford's 2024 summary lists circuit high (fault type 12) as a separate failure type of its auxiliary pumps. No manufacturer publicly documents P2E44. Look for harness sections rubbing against live wires, moisture and a defective output stage in the module. P2E43 covers the low side, P0CEC is pump A's equivalent.

title: DTC P2E61 - Alternative Fuel Misfire Detected With Low Fuel
problem_description: P2E61 records misfire that occurs while the engine burns its gaseous fuel and that fuel is almost used up. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. CARB treats a bi-fuel car as alternate-fueled only while it runs on gas and lets makers seek approval to suspend misfire monitoring at 15 % fuel or less, since a nearly empty tank can cause misfire by itself. Ford patents explain it for CNG: the regulator keeps the rail at a few bar, but near 500 psi tank pressure the flow chokes and rail pressure wavers, so metering suffers; one known answer is switching to petrol at low tank pressure. Another Ford patent reads low rail pressure despite gas in the tank, e.g. from ice, as a supply restriction. Refill and recheck; misfire with ample gas is P2E58 to P2E60.

title: DTC P2E68 - System Too Lean During Cylinder Deactivation Bank 1

title: DTC P2E6D - Hybrid/EV Battery Pack A Cell Thickness Sensor Circuit High

title: DTC P2E8C - Battery Charger B Charge Sequence Signal 1 Circuit High

title: DTC P2E8D - Battery Charger B Charge Sequence Signal 1 Circuit Low
problem_description: P2E8D means the vehicle finds the first CHAdeMO sequence line low while the fast charger should be driving it. title: DTC P2E8E - Battery Charger B Charge Sequence Signal 2 Circuit High
problem_description: P2E8E concerns the second CHAdeMO sequence line, which works differently from the first: the station closes switch d2 to tie the line to ground, completing the circuit that sequence signal 1 feeds, and only then may the vehicle close its high-voltage contactors. title: DTC P2E8F - Battery Charger B Charge Sequence Signal 2 Circuit Low
problem_description: P2E8F reports the second CHAdeMO sequence line pulled low at a time it should be released. Because the station uses d2 to connect this line to ground as the very last step before the vehicle closes its contactors, and opens d2 first when the session ends, a line already at ground early, or still at ground once d2 is open, contradicts the sequence. title: DTC P2EA7 - DC/AC Converter A Input Voltage Too Low
problem_description: A DC/AC converter turns direct current into household AC for sockets in the vehicle. P2EA7 means the DC voltage reaching converter A is below the range in which it is allowed to run. title: DTC P2EB6 - Hybrid/EV Battery Inductive Charger Input Voltage High
problem_description: P2EB6 is the counterpart to P2EB5: the voltage at the input of the inductive charger is higher than its electronics accept. Too much induced voltage can stem from a ground unit sending more power than requested, a ride height that shifts the coupling, for example when the vehicle is loaded or unloaded during charging, or a control loop between both sides that has lost step. SAE J2954 sets the 85 kHz band and the power classes within which these limits work. No manufacturer documents P2EB6 publicly. The charger shuts down to protect itself and the battery; cable charging stays possible.

title: DTC P2EBD - Crankcase Temperature Sensor Circuit High
problem_description: P2EBD is set when the crankcase temperature signal rises above its highest valid voltage. With the usual pull-up arrangement this happens when the current path through the sensor is interrupted, for example by an unplugged or oil-soaked connector, a broken wire or an open element, or when the signal touches the 5 V reference or battery voltage. For an NTC thermistor, whose resistance grows as it cools, the module then sees an impossibly cold crankcase; a PTC element would read as overheated instead. No manufacturer documents P2EBD, so limits and debounce times are not public. Under (e)(15.2.1) of 13 CCR 1968.2 the high fault has to be stored separately from the low fault P2EBE and from the rationality fault P2EBC.

title: DTC P2EBE - Crankcase Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
problem_description: P2EBE reports a crankcase temperature signal below the lowest voltage the circuit can produce when intact. title: DTC U0001 - High Speed CAN Communication Bus
problem_description: U0001 is the umbrella code for trouble on the high-speed CAN, the fast two-wire network joining engine, transmission, brake and steering modules. GM/Saab logs it once a module's transmit error counter climbs past 255: that module disconnects itself, stops sending and works with substitute values. Older GM calibration tables treat it as a bus-off, Type B after 5 s (2006 V8 ECM), and a 2006 five-speed TCM flags it after 64 bus-off events with the MIL on at once. FCA names U0001 CAN C Bus (Ram 1500 steering gear harness, Jeep Compass wiring crushed by a console bolt); Volvo and Mack trucks store it together with U0010 in the aftertreatment module, with MIL and possible derate. Usually several modules report it at once; individual wire faults have their own codes U0003 to U0009.
symptoms: Several warning lamps and messages at the same time
Scan tool reaches some modules only or none at all
Shifting, steering assist or brake functions in fallback mode
Many lost-communication codes stored alongside
possible_causes: Bus pair chafed, pinched or crushed in the harness (likelihood: high)
Corroded, loose or bent pins at a module or splice connector (likelihood: high)
One module or its transceiver disturbing the whole bus (likelihood: medium)
History entry after a voltage dip or tester connected with ignition on (likelihood: low)

title: DTC U0002 - High Speed CAN Communication Bus Performance
problem_description: U0002 stands for impaired rather than lost traffic on the high-speed CAN, and makers fill the slot in different ways. GM/Saab sets it when a supervised periodic message, which also tells the receiver that its sender is alive, has not shown up within the 250 ms supervision time; the receiver then carries on with a default value. FCA calls U0002 CAN C Bus Off Performance: a reflash for the 2013 Ram 2500/3500 6.7 L diesel PCM changed it from a one-trip to a two-trip MIL fault, whereas the 2024-26 Dodge Charger steering column module stores it without MIL because dips in supply voltage lasting about 40 ms trip a software bug. problem_description: U0021 marks a break in the (+) wire of a two-wire low-speed CAN, called CAN-High in the fault-tolerant layout of ISO 11898-3. problem_description: U0062 means the (-) conductor of Vehicle Communication Bus D is forced high, usually by contact with battery plus. Built as high-speed CAN, Bus D carries this fault on CAN-Low, which can then no longer be pulled down any more; onsemi and NXP both list this short among those under which no frame gets through, so every Bus D member eventually ends up bus-off and other networks log its absence. Diagnosing transceivers such as NXP's TJA1041 recognise the short when its resistance is between 0 and 50 ohms. Texas Instruments adds a hardware angle: termination resistors should be rated for such a short, since a bus wire shorted to a 24 V line loads them with the transceiver's short-circuit current times that voltage, enough to destroy a quarter-watt part. No manufacturer documents U0062 publicly. CAN-Low near battery voltage confirms it.
symptoms: All functions on Bus D fail together
Lost-communication codes in modules on other networks
Warning lamps or fallback modes depending on the modules involved
possible_causes: (-) wire of Bus D chafed against a battery or ignition feed (likelihood: high)
Water in a connector linking the (-) wire to a supply pin (likelihood: medium)
Termination or transceiver damaged by a lasting short to supply (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code U0062 (Vehicle Communication Bus D (-) High).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: bus d wiring, can transceiver.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 1-5 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: (-) wire of Bus D chafed against a battery or ignition feed (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Water in a connector linking the (-) wire to a supply pin (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

title: DTC U0063 - Vehicle Communication Bus D (-) Shorted to Bus D (+)

On a CAN-type Bus D the receivers then measure no voltage difference, read every bit as recessive and cannot see any frame start; onsemi lists this short with those that block transmission completely. title: DTC U0066 - Vehicle Communication Bus E (+) Open
problem_description: U0066 indicates a break in the (+) wire of Vehicle Communication Bus E. Where Bus E is a two-wire CAN, like the infotainment CAN Audi and Volkswagen monitor under that slot, the (+) wire is CAN-High. The physical layer decides how visible the fault is. With fault-tolerant low-speed hardware, NXP's TJA1055 rides through a CAN-High interruption with drivers, termination and differential receiver left as they were, and only counts edges: once CAN-High and CAN-Low differ by four pulses, its error output goes low. A high-speed transceiver offers no such check, so modules notice only that partners beyond the break fall silent. No manufacturer documents U0066 publicly; Audi's A3 case of a badly seated contact carrier in a multi-pin connector shows how such interruptions arise.

title: DTC U0067 - Vehicle Communication Bus E (+) Low
problem_description: U0067 tells of the (+) conductor of Vehicle Communication Bus E being grounded. For a Bus E built as a high-speed CAN that is CAN-High, which a dominant bit needs to raise by about a volt; grounded, it cannot. onsemi describes the resulting cycle: the controller attempts a start-of-frame, fails, flags errors, becomes error passive and finally bus-off, then must wait for 128 groups of eleven recessive bits before it may try again, so its transmit line is active only about 2 % of the time. Every Bus E node goes silent, and modules on other networks log them as missing. NXP's fault-tolerant TJA1055 low-speed chip, by contrast, carries on despite the same short. No manufacturer documents U0067 publicly. CAN-High at a few ohms to ground with the battery off confirms it.

Shorted transceiver in a module on Bus E (likelihood: low)

title: DTC U0073 - Control Module Communication Bus A Off
problem_description: U0073 is logged by a module whose own CAN controller has withdrawn from Bus A. GM's 2019 tables flag more than five bus-off events, about 0.06 s, inside a 0.81 s window as Type A with MIL on the first trip, and the ECM suspends lost-communication tests such as U0101 while it is active. Bulletins trace U0073 to a loose ground (Trax, G103), backed-out terminals in the 6L80 transmission connector and harness rubbing on a cylinder head (Silverado LV3). title: DTC U007A - Control Module Communication Bus H Off
problem_description: Bus H appears in no public manufacturer document for U007A; the code merely says that one module's CAN controller has switched to bus off on the network its maker labels H. A high-speed CAN carries a 120 ohm resistor at each end, so with the battery disconnected the two wires should show roughly 60 ohms between them; about 120 ohms points to a missing terminator, near zero to the wires touching. problem_description: There is no public manufacturer documentation for U007E; the letter L is reserved for vehicles with a dozen or more networks. title: DTC U0086 - Vehicle Communication Bus F (-) Low
problem_description: U0086 says the (-) wire of Vehicle Communication Bus F sits too low, usually shorted to ground. On a FlexRay Bus F, as in the Audi A6/A7, that wire is bus minus (BM). At rest both FlexRay lines float near half the transceiver supply, and NXP specifies a near-zero difference between them in idle. title: DTC U009C - Vehicle Communication Bus I Performance
problem_description: U009C reports that Vehicle Communication Bus I carries traffic, but not at the quality the module expects. U009C has not been documented in public by any manufacturer. The causes lie in signal integrity rather than a hard fault. Texas Instruments ties the possible bus length to the data rate, roughly 40 m when running at 1 Mbit/s and 100 m at half that rate, and names cable bandwidth and intersymbol interference as the limits; repairs with long added wire or untwisted cable eat into that margin. CAN detects such distortion as protocol errors: Wikipedia explains that after five identical bits the sender adds one of the inverse value, and six identical bits in a row count as an error, prompting a repeat.

title: DTC U009E - Vehicle Communication Bus J Performance
problem_description: U009E flags unreliable traffic on Vehicle Communication Bus J without a total loss. No manufacturer publishes a use of U009E. Interference is a likely source. Texas Instruments names fluorescent lamps, switching power supplies and motor drives as typical emitters of common-mode noise that couples onto bus lines, and explains that a receiver without good rejection may take it for data. NXP adds that tolerated wiring faults also worsen electromagnetic behaviour. Where messages go unacknowledged, Wikipedia notes that nodes often resend them repeatedly, which can drive them into the error-passive state.

title: DTC U010B - Lost Communication With Exhaust Gas Recirculation Control Module B

title: DTC U014A - Lost Communication With Battery Energy Control Module C
problem_description: U014A concerns a third battery energy control module, C. Hybrid and electric vehicles use such units to watch cell voltages, temperatures and state of charge and to protect the pack; distributed or modular designs give several sub-packs their own controller, which is where letters beyond A and B come in. Without data from C the system cannot judge that part of the pack, so expect reduced power, blocked charging or no ready mode. title: DTC U014B - Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Inductive Charging Module
problem_description: U014B covers the vehicle-side controller of a wireless charging system. Inductive charging transfers energy without a plug, through a coil in a ground pad and a receiving coil under the car; the SAE J2954 standard, finalised in 2020, defines power classes of 3.7, 7.7 and 11 kW and relies on resonant coupling with about 85 percent efficiency. The module on board rectifies the received power, checks alignment and reports to the battery and charge controllers; if its messages stop, those controllers log U014B. No manufacturer documents the code publicly, and wireless charging is still rare in series production. The practical effect is that wireless charging does not start or is interrupted, while charging by cable and driving normally continue. U044C covers invalid data from this module.

problem_description: U0152 is the left-hand partner of U0153: a separate controller for the side restraints on the left no longer sends. In most cars side impacts are detected by satellite sensors in sills, B- or C-pillars that feed the central airbag unit; Bosch, for example, mounts its peripheral acceleration sensors on the left and right of the body and links them over the PSI5 sensor interface. Some architectures go further and give each side its own module on the vehicle bus, and only those can set this code. No manufacturer documents U0152 publicly. The listener, usually the main restraints module, logs the loss when the periodic message of the left unit is missing while voltage is in range. The airbag lamp lights and left-side or curtain protection may be lost; there is no MIL. U0151 is the main module, U0453 invalid data from the left unit.

Left side or curtain airbag possibly not ready
Code stored in the main airbag module

Left side restraints module internally faulty (likelihood: low)

title: DTC U0160 - Lost Communication With Audible Alert Control Module
problem_description: U0160 is stored when the audible alert module, the unit that produces chimes for an open door, unfastened belt, key left in or lights on, drops off the bus. Audi documents it together with U017E00 in bulletin 2081251 for 2025-26 A5, A6, Q5 and Q6 e-tron models, where both codes accompany a proactive occupant protection warning and dealers are asked to file a case report. Two such modules are typical because each front seat gets its own motorised retractor, as on the 2015 A3 with J854 and J855. Keep U017F apart from Audi's B130474/B130574: those describe a deviating tensioning actuator, not a lost link. If a retractor with control unit was replaced after a collision, Audi requires a basic setting with the scan tool. Pyrotechnic pretensioners are wired separately. No MIL.
symptoms: Pre-crash protection fault message in the instrument cluster
Reversible belt tightening on one seat inoperative
Often stored together with U017E
possible_causes: Retractor with control module replaced but not coded or basic-set (likelihood: high)
Supply or bus connector at module B loose (likelihood: medium)
Pretensioner module B internally faulty (likelihood: medium)
Bus line between airbag unit and module B damaged (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code U017F (Lost Communication With Seat Belt Pretensioner Module B).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: seatbelt pretensioner b, can bus, lin bus.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-3 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Retractor with control module replaced but not coded or basic-set (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Supply or bus connector at module B loose (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

title: DTC U0180 - Lost Communication With Automatic Lighting Control Module

Expect the lights to stay in manual mode or default to on; no MIL. U0181 and U0182 are the levelling and front lighting modules, U0481 invalid data.

title: DTC U0185 - Lost Communication With Antenna Control Module

problem_description: U0187 opens the J2012 series for networked disc players and changers: module A is the main CD or DVD drive, while U0188 to U0190 cover B to D. In many older cars the changer sat apart from the head unit, in the glovebox, under a seat or in the trunk, and reported to it over a data line. U0187 has no public manufacturer documentation; GM lists no disc drives at all and the NHTSA bulletin index has no match. The radio records the code when the drive's periodic message stays away, following the logic GM gives for all loss-of-communication codes. In GM's eAssist mild hybrids it is the second and final board: bulletin PIT5513D lists two high-voltage battery interface control modules, K112A and K112B, for Silverado and Sierra trucks of 2016 to 2018 and the 2018 LaCrosse, and the GM tables 16OBDG07B and 19OBDG03B accordingly contain only U01A0 and U01A1. Their rating is milder than in the plug-in hybrids: Type B, so the MIL waits for a second failing trip; the 2016 table asks for more than 9.1 V and 4.5 s. If B is logged alone, the fault lies at B or at the link from A to B; both letters together point rather to a shared feed or the master side. GM placed these powerpacks and both boards under parts restriction via its technical assistance center.
symptoms: MIL only after two consecutive failing trips (GM Type B)
Start-stop and electric assist unavailable
Hybrid system warning message
possible_causes: Chain connection between module A and module B interrupted or corroded (likelihood: high)
Battery interface control module B (GM K112B) defective (likelihood: medium)
Common low-voltage feed of the powerpack interrupted (then usually A as well) (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code U01A1 (Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module B).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: hv battery interface module b, communication bus.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 1-6 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Chain connection between module A and module B interrupted or corroded (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Battery interface control module B (GM K112B) defective (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

title: DTC U01A2 - Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module C
problem_description: U01A2 is stored when battery interface control module C, the third board of the chain, stays silent. How a controller reaches that verdict is spelled out in GM's 2016 hybrid table: the battery system module first logs U179C for one or more missing boards, then orders all boards into a loopback mode that bypasses the daisy chain. A board that answers in this mode still has power and working logic, so the master can separate a broken link from a dead unit and names only the first board it fails to recover; the code passes again once data returns for 100 ms. Audi bulletin 2081028 for the Q5 e (model years 2022 and 2024) lists U01A200 among the codes for modules A to H behind an electrical system malfunction warning.

Reduced drive power or no electric driving
Code returns immediately after clearing

Battery controller software that misreads the chain (update available) (likelihood: low)

title: DTC U01A4 - Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module E

In a plain daisy chain a break silences all boards behind it, and GM's logic names only the first. In such designs a lone E code is much more telling, since boards beyond the gap are still heard from the far end. GM's eight-board plug-in tables of 2016-2019 rate the loss of E as Type A.

title: DTC U01A5 - Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module F
problem_description: U01A5 says the battery controller no longer receives data from interface module F. Once such a board drops out, the cells it covers are unsupervised: no voltage readings, no temperatures and no balancing for that section. GM therefore puts all of these codes into a fault bundle called BICM Loss of Comm in its 2018 hybrid table, which blocks battery diagnostics that would otherwise misfire on missing values. On the road the controller shields the pack, so reduced power, refused charging or opened contactors are to be expected. Audi bulletin 2078135 for the 2016 A3 Sportback e-tron describes a drive system that cannot be activated and a red warning lamp, with U01A500 among the A-H codes plus P0AA500 and P0A7D00. title: DTC U01A6 - Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module G

GM's 2016-2019 plug-in tables classify G as Type A, lighting the MIL in the first failing trip, and Audi's bulletins for the 2016 A3 e-tron and the Q5 e list U01A600 together with the other seven letters.

title: DTC U01A9 - Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module J
problem_description: U01A9 stands for battery interface control module J, the tenth board. Apart from wiring, a typical trigger after repairs is configuration: monitoring chips in a chain usually get their address when communication starts. problem_description: U01AD names battery interface control module N, the fourteenth board in a monitoring chain. title: DTC U01B0 - Lost Communication With Battery Monitor Module
problem_description: U01B0 says the 12 V battery monitor module, a small sensor on the negative battery post that reports voltage, current, temperature and state of charge, has stopped replying. GM polls it over LIN: its 2018 engine tables (18OBDG03A) flag the code once frame 18_C02 has been absent for 1.25 s, the 2025 body controller tables (25OBDG04A) after 12.6 s; both rate it Type B, two trips. GM bulletins 15-NA-087 and 22-NA-214 list it with a disabled stop/start system and a lit MIL, have the battery and LIN wiring checked first and the sensor swapped last; afterwards it must relearn, which a parasitic drain above about 250 mA blocks. Volkswagen lists U01B000 with MIL in the engine controller of the 2024 Atlas. U04B1 is the invalid-data partner.
symptoms: Stop/start system disabled, message in the driver display
MIL on
Battery state of charge shown wrongly or battery saver functions inactive

title: DTC U0227 - Lost Communication With Door Window Motor F
problem_description: U0227 reports that door window motor F cannot be reached. Besides wiring faults, the LIN sleep and wake cycle is worth understanding here. In NXP's AN2960 window-lift example the motor node drops into low-power mode on a go-to-sleep request, or after four seconds without bus traffic, behaviour that LIN 2.0 makes mandatory for slaves, and it becomes active again on bus activity or through a wake pin. A node that fails to wake, for instance because of an unstable supply or a damaged transceiver, looks to the master like a lost node. No manufacturer documents U0227 publicly, and letter F is assigned by the maker. U0528 is the matching invalid-data code. No MIL.

title: DTC U0248 - Lost Communication With Remote Accessory Module
problem_description: No manufacturer explains publicly what the remote accessory module does or when U0248 is set. The name suggests a body-side unit that switches accessories outside the main controllers. Separate codes exist for Ford's SYNC interface unit (APIM, U0253) and for a remote start module (U0254). For the 2011 Saab 9-5, GM explains how lost-communication codes arise in general: receivers check for expected signals, some serving as a sender's heartbeat; when one stops, they fall back to default values and record a lost-contact code for that sender. The same GM code list has no entry for U0248. Any listener would follow that scheme once this module falls silent. What the driver notices depends entirely on the accessory involved; driving is unaffected. Invalid data from it are U0549.

title: DTC U0250 - Lost Communication With Impact Classification System Module

Unit A shows how such a check behaves: GM's body control module on the 2026 Colorado and Canyon flags lost contact as U0288, falsely even on trucks without the outlet. GM's 2023 Silverado and Sierra programme, which later activated the inverter for dashboard and bed outlets by adding a power control module and reprogramming the BCM, shows that option coding decides which converters the network expects. Only the sockets fed by B should fail.

title: DTC U0310 - Software Incompatibility With Fuel Pump Control Module
problem_description: A fuel pump control module drives the in-tank pump at variable speed so that the pressure requested by the engine controller is reached. U0310 is set when the two controllers do not accept each other's software or calibration. No manufacturer documents U0310 publicly. GM's 2013 Cadillac ATS 2.5 L shows how tightly the pair belongs together: against a rough idle GM released matching software for the ECM and the FPCM and had both reprogrammed, each in its own session (PI1092B). U0332 means a receiving controller rejects its software or variant. No manufacturer documents U0332 publicly. GM treats the unit as a programmable module in its own right: the warranty labour list has a separate operation for reprogramming it with SPS (06-08-47-001N), and after the brake controller of the 2014 Cadillac ELR was recalibrated, the yaw rate sensor learn is run in this module (recall 14087). Audi removed sporadic C051F00, a correlation fault of sensor module A on e-tron models, with new software for ABS unit J104 and suspension unit J775 (2061908). U0125 is lost contact. Stability control may switch off.
symptoms: Stability control or traction control warning lamp on
Driver assistance functions unavailable
Code follows module replacement or software update
possible_causes: Sensor module replaced by a part with another software or variant (likelihood: high)
Brake or suspension controller updated without matching the sensor module (likelihood: medium)
Yaw rate sensor learn skipped after programming (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code U0332 (Software Incompatibility With Multi-axis Acceleration Sensor Module A).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: multi axis accel sensor module a.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.3-2 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Sensor module replaced by a part with another software or variant (likelihood: high).

title: DTC U0333 - Software Incompatibility With Gear Shift Control Module B
problem_description: With shift-by-wire, both the driver's selector and the unit that actually moves the range are electronic modules; module B denotes a second such unit, either a further selector or the shift actuator. U0333 means its software or calibration does not fit the partner controller. Allison lists it for the sixth-generation controls of its 3000 and 4000 series, released in 2021, as Gear Shift Module 2 Incompatible, next to U0304 for module 1; the same bulletin warns that new push-button selectors do not work with fifth-generation TCMs and that the fitted selector must match the TCM calibration (SIL 14-TR-21). Lexus labels the shift actuator ECU of the 2022 NX 350 and NX 250 with B and reflashed its main and sub calibration in campaign 22LC03. U0291 is lost contact, U0592 invalid data.

title: DTC U0334 - Software Incompatibility With Radio
problem_description: On current vehicles the radio is the infotainment head unit: besides audio it runs navigation, voice control, phone connection and the setting menus for other systems such as seat heating. U0334 is stored when a controller relying on these services rejects the radio's software. No manufacturer documents U0334 publicly. FCA illustrates how tightly radio software levels build on each other: Uconnect 8.4 radios in European Jeep Cherokee 2019–2020 needed up to three USB stages to reach level 39.5, and skipping a stage could damage the unit so badly that it had to be replaced (08-033-21). On the Jeep Compass, an earlier update to 28.31 could leave the radio silent and grey out the heated seat and steering wheel buttons until 39.2 was installed (08-068-20). U0184 is lost contact, U0485 invalid data. No MIL.

title: DTC U0335 - Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Sensor Module

U0335 records that this controller or another partner rejects the module's software. Ford's 2014 code interpretation lists U0335 for the hybrid battery pack sensor module without a MIL marker. GM runs a comparable check in the Volt battery: its VITM compares the software versions of all slave modules 200 ms after power-up at 9 V or more and stores the maker-specific P1EB1 as Type A. Stellantis reprograms the battery pack control module and other units of the 2025 electric Dodge Charger and, if U029A for the sensor module remains, lets the car sleep for six minutes (08-028-25). title: DTC U0336 - Software Incompatibility With Restraints Control Module

Jaguar Land Rover shows why the software level matters: replacement RCMs for the Range Rover Evoque came with software older than the factory level, the tester picked its update from the module content instead of the as-built data, and the unit stored B0002-13 until a manual patch fixed the choice (SSM74259). title: DTC U0339 - Software Incompatibility With Body Control Module B

Ford has a BCM-B on 2022–2023 Mustang Stealth models, where a wrong configuration left the sill plates dark until program 23B60 reconfigured it with FDRS. U0142 is lost contact, U0443 invalid data. title: DTC U033C - Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module C
problem_description: U033C names the third interface board. GM's closest published check is its own code P1EB1 in the VITM of the Volt: at power-up the controller compares its own software version with that of all slave boards and logs P1EB1 if any one does not fit, within 200 ms, with at least 9 V and no slave lost-communication fault active. The 2015 table enters it as one trip, the 2018 table as Type A, meaning a MIL after one failed drive. GM thus reports one summary code rather than one per board, and a letter code like U033C does not appear there. Where a maker does use the letter codes, C stands for the third board only; U01A2 covers lost contact with it, U04A3 invalid data.

title: DTC U0340 - Software Incompatibility With Hybrid/EV Battery Interface Control Module G

For G, GM thus documents silence (U01A6), not a software conflict. The older four-board design is stricter: P1F06 to P1F09 make each slave return a key value computed by a seed-and-key algorithm and fail it when wrong values persist for 1 s within a 1.4 s window, Type B in the 2015 table. U04A7 is the invalid-data code for G.

title: DTC U0400 - Invalid Data Received

GM's 2025 tables (25OBDG03B, 25OBDG04B) describe the body control module checking alive rolling counters, protection values, checksums and CRCs of centre-stack signals, among them HVAC control requests: 8 failures in 10 samples, for some signals 14 in 18 or 15 in 16, set it at least 5 s after power-up, with the partial network active for 3 s, power mode Run and over 11 V; Type B. GM PIE0807A covers a MIL with U0485 and U1962 on the 2024 Traverse and Acadia 2.5 L. Stellantis lists it in 08-046-23, 08-014-24 and 08-101-25 (Grand Cherokee, Wagoneer, Pacifica), stored by the amplifier or with a MIL; radio software cures it. U0184 is lost contact.
symptoms: Radio resets, black screen or audio sources inoperative
Climate controls on the screen do not respond
MIL on some vehicles
possible_causes: Radio or infotainment software level with known message errors, fixed by an update (likelihood: high)
Radio resetting or waking late so that counters and checksums no longer match (likelihood: medium)
Low supply voltage or a disturbed bus connection to the centre stack (likelihood: low)
diagnostic_steps: Connect OBD-II diagnostic scanner and verify active code U0485 (Invalid Data Received From Radio).
Perform visual and physical inspection of affected components: radio head unit.
Check electrical wiring harnesses and connectors for looseness, corrosion, or pin displacement.
Measure reference voltage, ground continuity, and component resistance against manufacturer specifications.
Repair guidance: Professional technician service recommended. Estimated labor time: 0.5-2 hours
recommended_actions: Prioritize inspection of primary cause: Radio or infotainment software level with known message errors, fixed by an update (likelihood: high).
If issue persists, inspect secondary potential fault: Radio resetting or waking late so that counters and checksums no longer match (likelihood: medium).
Due to system criticality, have vehicle inspected by an ASE-certified technician.

title: DTC U0486 - Invalid Data Received From Antenna Control Module

U0185 would mean silence. Such modules sit in the roof fin, rear screen or bumper and amplify, combine or switch signals for radio, satellite, navigation, phone or remote key, and some raise a powered mast. Mercedes shows how water affects them: on the G-Class from model year 2019 without sunroof, a crack near the left rear roof rail pan lets water in, the keyless-go controller stores antenna module faults and the key may no longer unlock the car (LI65.10-P-074539); sealing the crack is the repair. No manufacturer documents U0486 itself. Expect weak reception or reduced key range, with no MIL.

Remote key does not unlock or works only at short range

title: DTC U0487 - Invalid Data Received From Audio Amplifier A
problem_description: U0487 means the external audio amplifier A keeps sending frames, but the radio or gateway finds their content invalid; once the amplifier vanishes from the bus, U0186 applies, and amplifier B has U0262 and U0563. Amplifiers return status such as mute state, sound settings and diagnostic results to the head unit. No manufacturer documents U0487 publicly. Mazda files faulty amplifier messages under U0186 with failure type 08 instead: on the 2019-2023 Mazda3 and CX-30 (SA-070-22) a backed-out pin in the MOST connector of the connectivity master unit caused it, together with static. Chrysler 08-020-14 reflashed amplifiers on 2013-2014 Ram, Durango and Grand Cherokee when the radio was muted because the amplifier went quiet. GM's Saab list calls the unit speaker amplifier module. Sound may mute or crackle; no MIL.
